351.s:
skanda uvāca
ramā rame ramāḥ śubhā ramāṃ rame rasās tathā /
ramayā ca ramābhyāñca ramābhiḥ kṛtamavyayaṃ //
351.d:
स्कन्द उवाच
रमा रमे रमाः शुभा रमां रमे रसास् तथा /
रमया च रमाभ्याञ्च रमाभिः कृतमव्ययं //
351.m: Skanda said: / Ramā, rame, ramāḥ, the auspicious ones; ramām, rame, rasāḥ likewise; / by Ramā (ramayā), ramābhyām, and ramābhiḥ; the imperishable is made;

351.s:
ramāyai ca ramābhyāś ca ramāyā ramayoḥ śubhaṃ /
ramāṇāñca ramāyāñca ramāsvevaṃ kalādyaḥ //
351.d:
रमायै च रमाभ्याश् च रमाया रमयोः शुभं /
रमाणाञ्च रमायाञ्च रमास्वेवं कलाद्यः //
351.m: to Ramā (ramāyai), ramābhyām, ramāyāḥ, ramayoḥ, auspiciousness; / of the Ramās (ramāṇām), ramāyām, and ramāsu; likewise kalā and others.

351.s:
jarā jarasau jara iti jarasaś ca jarā jarāṃ /
jarasañca jarāsvevaṃ sarvā sarve ca sarvayā //
351.d:
जरा जरसौ जर इति जरसश् च जरा जरां /
जरसञ्च जरास्वेवं सर्वा सर्वे च सर्वया //
351.m: Jarā, jarasau, jarāḥ, and jarasaḥ; jarā, jarām, / jarasam, and jarāsu; likewise sarvā, sarve, and by all (sarvayā);

351.s:
sarvasyai dehi sarvasyāḥ sarvasyāḥ sarvasyos tathā /
śeṣaṃ ramāvadrūpaṃ syād dve dve tisraś ca tisṛṇāṃ //
351.d:
सर्वस्यै देहि सर्वस्याः सर्वस्याः सर्वस्योस् तथा /
शेषं रमावद्रूपं स्याद् द्वे द्वे तिस्रश् च तिसृणां //
351.m: give to all (sarvasyai); of all (sarvasyāḥ), from all (sarvasyāḥ), of two alls (sarvasyoḥ) likewise; / the remainder of the form would be like ramā; dve, dve; tisraḥ, and tisṛṇām.

351.s:
buddhīrbuddhyā buddhaye ca buddhyai buddheś ca hemate /
kavivatsyānmunīnāñca nadī nadyau nadīṃ nadīḥ //
351.d:
बुद्धीर्बुद्ध्या बुद्धये च बुद्ध्यै बुद्धेश् च हेमते /
कविवत्स्यान्मुनीनाञ्च नदी नद्यौ नदीं नदीः //
351.m: Buddhiḥ, buddhyā, buddhaye, buddhyai, buddheḥ; O mind (he mate)! / It would be like kavi; and of sages (munīnām). Nadī, nadyau, nadīm, nadīḥ,

351.s:
nadyā nadībhirnadyai ca nadyāñcaiva nadīṣu ca /
kumārī jṛmbhaṇītyevaṃ śrīḥ śriyau ca śriyaḥ śriyā //
:p 248
351.d:
नद्या नदीभिर्नद्यै च नद्याञ्चैव नदीषु च /
कुमारी जृम्भणीत्येवं श्रीः श्रियौ च श्रियः श्रिया //
:प् 248
351.m:
nadyā, nadībhiḥ, nadyai, nadyām, and nadīṣu; / likewise kumārī, jṛmbhaṇī. Śrīḥ, śriyau, śriyaḥ, śriyā,
[Page 248]

351.s:
śriyai śriye strīṃ striyañca strīś ca striyaḥ striyā striyai /
striyāḥ strīṇāṃ striyāñca grāmaṇyāṃ dhenvai ca dhenave //
351.d:
श्रियै श्रिये स्त्रीं स्त्रियञ्च स्त्रीश् च स्त्रियः स्त्रिया स्त्रियै /
स्त्रियाः स्त्रीणां स्त्रियाञ्च ग्रामण्यां धेन्वै च धेनवे //
351.m: śriyai, śriye. Strīm, striyam, strīḥ, striyaḥ, striyā, striyai, / striyāḥ, strīṇām, striyām; grāmaṇyām; to a milch-cow (dhenvai and dhenave);

351.s:
jambūrjambvau ca jambūś ca jambūnāñca phalampiva /
varṣābhvau ca punarbhvau ca mātṝrvāpi ca gauś ca nauḥ //
351.d:
जम्बूर्जम्ब्वौ च जम्बूश् च जम्बूनाञ्च फलम्पिव /
वर्षाभ्वौ च पुनर्भ्वौ च मातॄर्वापि च गौश् च नौः //
351.m: jambūḥ, jambvau, jambūḥ, and drink the fruit of rose-apples (jambūnām)! / Varṣābhvau, punarbhvau, mātṝḥ, or gauḥ and nauḥ;

351.s:
vāgvācā vāgbhiś ca vākṣu śragbhyāṃ sraji strajos tathā /
vidvadbhyāñcaiva vidvatsu bhavatī syād bhavantyapi //
351.d:
वाग्वाचा वाग्भिश् च वाक्षु श्रग्भ्यां स्रजि स्त्रजोस् तथा /
विद्वद्भ्याञ्चैव विद्वत्सु भवती स्याद् भवन्त्यपि //
351.m: vāk, vācā, vāgbhiḥ, vākṣu; śragbhyām, sraji, srajoḥ likewise; / vidvadbhyām, and vidvatsu; bhavatī, and bhavanty as well;

351.s:
dīvyantī bhātī bhāntī ca tudantī ca tudatyapi /
rudatī rundhatī devī gṛhnatī coryantyapi //
351.d:
दीव्यन्ती भाती भान्ती च तुदन्ती च तुदत्यपि /
रुदती रुन्धती देवी गृह्नती चोर्यन्त्यपि //
351.m: dīvyantī, bhātī, bhāntī, tudantī, and tudaty as well; / rudatī, rundhatī, devī, gṛhṇatī, and corayanty as well;

351.s:
dṛṣat dṛṣadbhyāṃ dṛṣadi viśesaviduṣī kṛtiḥ /
samit samidbhyāṃ samidhi sīmā sīmni ca sīmani //
351.d:
दृषत् दृषद्भ्यां दृषदि विशेसविदुषी कृतिः /
समित् समिद्भ्यां समिधि सीमा सीम्नि च सीमनि //
351.m: dṛṣat, dṛṣadbhyām, dṛṣadi; viśeṣaviduṣī, kṛtiḥ; / samit, samidbhyām, samidhi; sīmā, sīmni, and sīmani.

351.s:
dāmanībhyāṃ kakudbhyāñca keyamābhyāṃ tathāsu ca /
gīrbhyāñcaiva girā gīrṣu subhūḥ supūḥ purā puri //
351.d:
दामनीभ्यां ककुद्भ्याञ्च केयमाभ्यां तथासु च /
गीर्भ्याञ्चैव गिरा गीर्षु सुभूः सुपूः पुरा पुरि //
351.m: [Forms like] *dāmanībhyām*, *kakudbhyām*, *keyamābhyām*, and likewise in [the locative plural suffix] *-su*; / with *gīrbhyām*, and *girā*, *gīrṣu*; *subhūḥ*, *supūḥ*, *purā*, [and] *puri*.

351.s:
dyaurdyubhyāṃ divi dyuṣu tādṛśyā tādṛśo diśaḥ /
yādṛśyāṃ yādṛśī tadvat suvacobhyāṃ suvacaḥsvapi /
asau cāmūmamū cāmūramūbhiramuyāmuyoḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vyākaraṇe strīliṅgaśabdasiddharūpaṃ
nāmaikapañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 249
:ś atha dvipañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo . adhyāyaḥ
napuṃsakaśabdasiddharūpaṃ
351.d:
द्यौर्द्युभ्यां दिवि द्युषु तादृश्या तादृशो दिशः /
यादृश्यां यादृशी तद्वत् सुवचोभ्यां सुवचःस्वपि /
असौ चामूममू चामूरमूभिरमुयामुयोः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे व्याकरणे स्त्रीलिङ्गशब्दसिद्धरूपं
नामैकपञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 249
:श् अथ द्विपञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो . अध्यायः
नपुंसकशब्दसिद्धरूपं
351.m:
*dyauḥ*, *dyubhyām*, *divi*, *dyuṣu*; *tādṛśyā*, *tādṛśaḥ*, *diśaḥ*; / in *yādṛśyām*, *yādṛśī*; likewise with *suvacobhyām*, and in *suvacaḥsu*; / *asau*, and *amūm*, *amū*, and *amūḥ*, with *amūbhiḥ*, *amuyā*, [and] of *amuyoḥ*.
Thus ends the three hundred and fifty-first chapter, named 'The Formation of Feminine Words' in grammar, in the Great Agni Purāṇa.
[Page 249]
Now begins the three hundred and fifty-second chapter.
The Formation of Neuter Words.

352.s:
skanda uvāca
napuṃsake kiṃ ke kāni kiṃ ke kāni tato jalaṃ /
sarvaṃ sarve ca pūrvādyāḥ somapaṃ somapāni ca //
352.d:
स्कन्द उवाच
नपुंसके किं के कानि किं के कानि ततो जलं /
सर्वं सर्वे च पूर्वाद्याः सोमपं सोमपानि च //
352.m: Skanda said: / In the neuter: *kim*, *ke*, *kāni*; *kim*, *ke*, *kāni*; then *jalam*; / *sarvam*, *sarve*, and [forms of stems ending in] *pūrva*, etc.; *somapam*, and *somapāni*.

352.s:
grāmaṇi grāmaṇinī ca grāmaṇi grāmaṇīnyapi /
vāri vāriṇī vārīṇi vāriṇāṃ vāriṇīdṛśaṃ //
352.d:
ग्रामणि ग्रामणिनी च ग्रामणि ग्रामणीन्यपि /
वारि वारिणी वारीणि वारिणां वारिणीदृशं //
352.m: *grāmaṇi*, and *grāmaṇinī*, *grāmaṇi*, and also *grāmaṇīni*; / *vāri*, *vāriṇī*, *vārīṇi*, of *vāriṇām*, [and] such as *vāriṇi*.

352.s:
śucaye śucine dehi mṛdune mṛdave tathā /
trapu trapuṇi trapuṇāñca khalapūni khalapvi ca //
352.d:
शुचये शुचिने देहि मृदुने मृदवे तथा /
त्रपु त्रपुणि त्रपुणाञ्च खलपूनि खलप्वि च //
352.m: Give to *śucaye* or *śucine*; likewise to *mṛdune* or *mṛdave*; / *trapu*, *trapuṇi*, and of *trapuṇām*; *khalapūni*, and in *khalapvi*.

352.s:
kartrā ca kartṛṇe kartre atiryatiriṇāntathā /
abhinyabhininī caive suvacāṃsi suvacāṃsi suvākṣu ca //
352.d:
कर्त्रा च कर्तृणे कर्त्रे अतिर्यतिरिणान्तथा /
अभिन्यभिनिनी चैवे सुवचांसि सुवचांसि सुवाक्षु च //
352.m: By *kartrā*, and to *kartṛṇe*, to *kartre*; likewise *atiryat*, [and] of *atiryatīnām*; / *abhin*, and *abhininī*; *suvacāṃsi*, *suvacāṃsi*, and in *suvākṣu*.

352.s:
yadyattvime tat karmāṇi idañceme tvimāni ca /
īdṛktvado 'munī amūni amunā syādamīṣu ca //
352.d:
यद्यत्त्विमे तत् कर्माणि इदञ्चेमे त्विमानि च /
ईदृक्त्वदो ऽमुनी अमूनि अमुना स्यादमीषु च //
352.m: *yat*, *yat*; but *ime*, *tat*, *karmāṇi*; and *idam*, *ime*, and *imāni*; / *īdṛk*; *adaḥ*, *amunī*, *amūni*; it would be with *amunā*, and in *amīṣu*.

352.s:
ahamāvāṃ vayaṃ māṃ vai ābāmasmānmayā kṛtaṃ /
āvābhyāñca tathāsmābhirmahyamasmabhyameva ca //
352.d:
अहमावां वयं मां वै आबामस्मान्मया कृतं /
आवाभ्याञ्च तथास्माभिर्मह्यमस्मभ्यमेव च //
352.m: *aham*, *āvām*, *vayam*; indeed *mām*, *āvām*, *asmān*; done by *mayā*; / and by *āvābhyām*, and likewise by *asmābhiḥ*; to *mahyam*, and indeed to *asmabhyam*;

352.s:
madāvābhyāṃ madasmacca putro 'yaṃ mama cāvayoḥ /
asmākamapi cāsmāsu tvaṃ yuvāṃ yūyamījire //
352.d:
मदावाभ्यां मदस्मच्च पुत्रो ऽयं मम चावयोः /
अस्माकमपि चास्मासु त्वं युवां यूयमीजिरे //
352.m: from *mat*, *āvābhyām*, and from *mat* and *asmat*; 'this is the son of *mama*, and of *āvayoḥ* / and also of *asmākam*'; and in *asmāsu*; *tvam*, *yuvām*, *yūyam*, they said;

352.s:
tvāṃ yuvāñca yuṣmāṃś ca tvayā yuṣmābhirīritaṃ /
tubhyaṃ yuvābhyāṃ yummabhyaṃ tvat yuvābhyāñca yuṣmat //
352.d:
त्वां युवाञ्च युष्मांश् च त्वया युष्माभिरीरितं /
तुभ्यं युवाभ्यां युम्मभ्यं त्वत् युवाभ्याञ्च युष्मत् //
352.m: *tvām*, and *yuvām*, and *yuṣmān*; spoken by *tvayā*, by *yuṣmābhiḥ*; / to *tubhyam*, to *yuvābhyām*, to *yuṣmabhyam*; from *tvat*, from *yuvābhyām*, and from *yuṣmat*;

352.s:
tava yuvayoryuṣmākaṃ tvayi yuṣmāsu bhāratī /
upalakṣaṇamatraiva ajjhalantāś ca te smṛtāḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vyākaraṇe napuṃsakaśabdasiddharūpaṃ
nāma dvipañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:p 250
:ś atha tripañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
kārakaṃ
352.d:
तव युवयोर्युष्माकं त्वयि युष्मासु भारती /
उपलक्षणमत्रैव अज्झलन्ताश् च ते स्मृताः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे व्याकरणे नपुंसकशब्दसिद्धरूपं
नाम द्विपञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:प् 250
:श् अथ त्रिपञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
कारकं
352.m:
of *tava*, of *yuvayoḥ*, of *yuṣmākam*; in *tvayi*, in *yuṣmāsu*, O Bhāratī. / This is merely an illustrative indication; and they are taught ending in vowels and consonants.
Thus ends the three hundred and fifty-second chapter, named 'The Formation of Neuter Words' in grammar, in the Great Agni Purāṇa. [Page 250]
Now begins the three hundred and fifty-third chapter.
Case-Relations (Kāraka).

353.s:
sukanda uvāca
kārakaṃ sampravakṣyāmi vibhaktyarthasamanvitaṃ /
grāmo 'sti hemahārkeha naumi viṣṇuṃ śriyā saha //
353.d:
सुकन्द उवाच
कारकं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि विभक्त्यर्थसमन्वितं /
ग्रामो ऽस्ति हेमहार्केह नौमि विष्णुं श्रिया सह //
353.m: Skanda said: / I will fully declare the case-relation accompanied by the meanings of the case-endings: / 'The village is here, O great Sun! Here I bow to Viṣṇu along with Śrī.'

353.s:
svatantraḥ kartā vidyāntaṃ kṛtinaḥ samupāsate /
hetukartālambhayate hitaṃ vai karmakartari //
353.d:
स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता विद्यान्तं कृतिनः समुपासते /
हेतुकर्तालम्भयते हितं वै कर्मकर्तरि //
353.m: The independent [agent] is the agent (kartṛ): 'The wise attend upon the end of knowledge'; / the causative agent causes one to obtain; indeed, the beneficial [is found] in the agent-as-object (karmakartṛ):

353.s:
svayaṃ bhidyet prākṛtadhīḥ svayañca chidyate taruḥ /
kartābhihita uttamaḥ kartānabhihito 'dhamaḥ //
353.d:
स्वयं भिद्येत् प्राकृतधीः स्वयञ्च छिद्यते तरुः /
कर्ताभिहित उत्तमः कर्तानभिहितो ऽधमः //
353.m: 'An ordinary mind would break by itself,' and 'The tree is cut by itself.' / The expressed agent is superior; the unexpressed agent is subordinate.

353.s:
kartānabhihito dharmaḥ śiṣye vyākhyāyate yathā /
kartā pañcavidhaḥ proktaḥ karma saptavidhaṃ śṛṇu //
353.d:
कर्तानभिहितो धर्मः शिष्ये व्याख्यायते यथा /
कर्ता पञ्चविधः प्रोक्तः कर्म सप्तविधं शृणु //
353.m: The unexpressed agent is the duty, as in: 'It is explained to the pupil.' / The agent is said to be of five kinds; hear of the object (karman) of seven kinds:

353.s:
īpsitaṃ karma ca yathā śraddadhāti hariṃ yatiḥ /
anīpsitaṃ karma yathā ahiṃ laṅghayate bhṛśaṃ //
353.d:
ईप्सितं कर्म च यथा श्रद्दधाति हरिं यतिः /
अनीप्सितं कर्म यथा अहिं लङ्घयते भृशं //
353.m: The desired object, as in: 'The ascetic places faith in Hari'; / the undesired object, as in: 'He repeatedly steps over a snake';

353.s:
naivepsitaṃ nānīpsitaṃ dugdhaṃ sambhakṣyanrajaḥ /
bhakṣyedpyakathitaṃ gopālo dogdhi gāṃ payaḥ //
353.d:
नैवेप्सितं नानीप्सितं दुग्धं सम्भक्ष्यन्रजः /
भक्ष्येद्प्यकथितं गोपालो दोग्धि गां पयः //
353.m: neither desired nor undesired: 'Eating milk, he eats dust'; / [the object] not specially stated: 'The cowherd milks milk from the cow';

353.s:
kartṛkarmātha gamayecchiṣyaṃ grāmaṃ gururyathā /
karma cābhihitaṃ pūjā kriyate vai śriye hareḥ //
353.d:
कर्तृकर्माथ गमयेच्छिष्यं ग्रामं गुरुर्यथा /
कर्म चाभिहितं पूजा क्रियते वै श्रिये हरेः //
353.m: then the object-as-agent: as 'The teacher makes the pupil go to the village'; / and the expressed object: 'Indeed, worship is performed for the glory of Hari';

353.s:
karmānabhihitaṃ stotraṃ hareḥ kuryāt sarvadaṃ /
karaṇaṃ dvividhaṃ proktaṃ vāhyamabhyantaraṃ tathā //
353.d:
कर्मानभिहितं स्तोत्रं हरेः कुर्यात् सर्वदं /
करणं द्विविधं प्रोक्तं वाह्यमभ्यन्तरं तथा //
353.m: the unexpressed object: 'One should sing the hymn of Hari that gives all.' / The instrument (karaṇa) is said to be of two kinds: external and likewise internal:

353.s:
cakṣuṣā rūpaṃ gṛhṇīti vāhyaṃ dātreṇa tallunet /
sampradānaṃ tridhā proktaṃ prerakaṃ brāhmaṇāya gāṃ //
:p 251
353.d:
चक्षुषा रूपं गृह्णीति वाह्यं दात्रेण तल्लुनेत् /
सम्प्रदानं त्रिधा प्रोक्तं प्रेरकं ब्राह्मणाय गां //
:प् 251
353.m:
'One perceives form with the eye'; the external: 'He would reap that with a sickle.' / The recipient (sampradāna) is said to be threefold: the prompter, [as in] 'a cow to the brāhmaṇa';
[Page 251]

353.s:
naro dadāpi nṛpataye dāsantadanumantṛkaṃ /
anirākartṛkaṃ bhartre dadyāt puṣpāṇi sajjanaḥ //
353.d:
नरो ददापि नृपतये दासन्तदनुमन्तृकं /
अनिराकर्तृकं भर्त्रे दद्यात् पुष्पाणि सज्जनः //
353.m: 'A man gives a servant to the king'—that has an assenting [recipient]; / having an unreceptive [recipient]: 'A virtuous man would give flowers to the master.'

353.s:
apadānaṃ dvidhā proktaṃ calamaśvāttu dhāvataḥ /
patitaścācalaṃ grāmādāgacchati sa vaiṣṇavaḥ //
353.d:
अपदानं द्विधा प्रोक्तं चलमश्वात्तु धावतः /
पतितश्चाचलं ग्रामादागच्छति स वैष्णवः //
353.m: The point of departure (apādāna) is said to be of two kinds: moving, as in 'fallen from a running horse'; / and unmoving: 'that Vaiṣṇava comes from the village.'

353.s:
caturdhā cādhikaraṇaṃ vyāpakandadhni ghṛtam /
tileṣu tailaṃ devārthamaupaśleṣikamucyate //
353.d:
चतुर्धा चाधिकरणं व्यापकन्दध्नि घृतम् /
तिलेषु तैलं देवार्थमौपश्लेषिकमुच्यते //
353.m: And the locus (adhikaraṇa) is fourfold: all-pervading: 'ghee in curd,' / 'oil in sesame seeds'; for the purpose of the gods; [the physical] contact is spoken of:

353.s:
gṛhe tiṣṭhet kapirvṛkṣe smṛtaṃ vaiṣayikaṃ yathā /
jale matsyo vane siṃhaḥ smṛtaṃ sāmīpyakaṃ yathā //
353.d:
गृहे तिष्ठेत् कपिर्वृक्षे स्मृतं वैषयिकं यथा /
जले मत्स्यो वने सिंहः स्मृतं सामीप्यकं यथा //
353.m: 'The monkey sits in the house, on the tree'; what is related to a sphere is taught, as in: / 'The fish is in the water, the lion in the forest'; what is based on proximity is taught, as in:

353.s:
gaṅgāyāṃ gho ṣo vasati aupacārikamīdṛśaṃ /
tṛtīyā vātha vā ṣaṣṭhī smṛtānabhihite tathā //
353.d:
गङ्गायां घो षो वसति औपचारिकमीदृशं /
तृतीया वाथ वा षष्ठी स्मृतानभिहिते तथा //
353.m: 'The cowherd settlement dwells on the Gaṅgā'—such is the figurative. / And when unexpressed, the third or the sixth [case] is taught, likewise:

353.s:
viṣṇuḥ sampūjyate lokair gantavyantena tasya vā /
prathamābhihitakartṛkarmaṇoḥ praṇameddharim //
353.d:
विष्णुः सम्पूज्यते लोकैर् गन्तव्यन्तेन तस्य वा /
प्रथमाभिहितकर्तृकर्मणोः प्रणमेद्धरिम् //
353.m: 'Viṣṇu is worshipped by people,' [and] 'It must be gone by him or of him.' / When the agent or object is expressed, the first [case is used]; 'One should bow to Hari.'

353.s:
hetau tṛtīyā cānnena vasedvṛkṣāya vai jalaṃ /
caturthī tādarthye 'bhihitā pañcamī paryupāṅmukhaiḥ //
353.d:
हेतौ तृतीया चान्नेन वसेद्वृक्षाय वै जलं /
चतुर्थी तादर्थ्ये ऽभिहिता पञ्चमी पर्युपाङ्मुखैः //
353.m: In the sense of cause the third [is used]: 'He would live by food'; 'indeed water for the tree.' / The fourth is taught in the sense of 'for the sake of that' (tādarthya); the fifth with words beginning with *pari*, *upa*, and *āṅ*:

353.s:
yoge vṛṣṭaḥ pari grāmāddevo 'yaṃ balavat purā /
pūrvo grāmādṛte viṣṇorna muktiritaro hareḥ //
353.d:
योगे वृष्टः परि ग्रामाद्देवो ऽयं बलवत् पुरा /
पूर्वो ग्रामादृते विष्णोर्न मुक्तिरितरो हरेः //
353.m: In connection [with them]: 'It rained around the village'; 'This god was previously powerful'; / 'east of the village'; 'Without Viṣṇu there is no liberation'; 'other than Hari.'

353.s:
pṛthagvinādyaistṛtīyā pañcamī ca tathā bhavet /
pṛthaggrāmādvihāreṇa vinā śrīś ca śriyā śriyaḥ //
353.d:
पृथग्विनाद्यैस्तृतीया पञ्चमी च तथा भवेत् /
पृथग्ग्रामाद्विहारेण विना श्रीश् च श्रिया श्रियः //
353.m: With *pṛthak*, *vinā*, and others, the third and also the fifth [case] occurs: / 'Apart from the village'; 'by excursion'; *vinā śrīḥ*, and *śriyā*, [or] *śriyaḥ*.

353.s:
karmapravacanīyākhyair dvitīyā yogato bhavet /
anvarjunañca yoddhāro hy abhito grāmamīritaṃ //
353.d:
कर्मप्रवचनीयाख्यैर् द्वितीया योगतो भवेत् /
अन्वर्जुनञ्च योद्धारो ह्य् अभितो ग्राममीरितं //
353.m: In connection with those called adnominal prepositions (karmapravacanīya), the second [case] occurs: / 'The warriors are after Arjuna'; indeed, 'around the village' is spoken of.

353.s:
namaḥsvāhāsvadhāsvastivaṣaḍādyaiś caturthyapi /
namo devāya te svasti tumarthādbhāvācinaḥ //
353.d:
नमःस्वाहास्वधास्वस्तिवषडाद्यैश् चतुर्थ्यपि /
नमो देवाय ते स्वस्ति तुमर्थाद्भावाचिनः //
353.m: And with *namaḥ*, *svāhā*, *svadhā*, *svasti*, *vaṣaṭ*, and the like, the fourth [case occurs]: / 'Homage to the god'; 'Hail to you'; from an action noun meaning the infinitive (-tum):

353.s:
pākāya paktaye yāti tṛtīyā sahayogake /
:p 252
hetvarthe kutsite 'ṅge sā tṛtīyā ca viśeṣaṇe //
353.d:
पाकाय पक्तये याति तृतीया सहयोगके /
:प् 252
हेत्वर्थे कुत्सिते ऽङ्गे सा तृतीया च विशेषणे //
353.m:
'He goes for cooking (*pākāya*, *paktaye*)'; the third [case occurs] in connection with 'with' (saha):
[Page 252]
In the sense of cause; in a defective limb, that third [case occurs]; and in an attribute:

353.s:
pitāgātsaha putreṇa kāṇo 'kṣṇā gadayā hariḥ /
arthena nivasedbhṛtyaḥ kāle bhāve ca saptamau //
353.d:
पितागात्सह पुत्रेण काणो ऽक्ष्णा गदया हरिः /
अर्थेन निवसेद्भृत्यः काले भावे च सप्तमौ //
353.m: 'The father went with the son'; 'blind in the eye'; 'Hari with the mace'; / 'The servant would reside for money.' And in time and condition, the seventh [case occurs]:

353.s:
viṣṇau nate bhavenmuktirvasante sa gato harim /
nṛṇāṃ svāmī nṛṣu svāmī nṛṇāmīśaḥsatāmpatiḥ //
353.d:
विष्णौ नते भवेन्मुक्तिर्वसन्ते स गतो हरिम् /
नृणां स्वामी नृषु स्वामी नृणामीशःसताम्पतिः //
353.m: 'When Viṣṇu is bowed to, liberation occurs'; 'In the spring he went to Hari.' / 'Master of men (*nṛṇām* / *nṛṣu*)'; 'Lord of men'; 'Protector of the good';

353.s:
nṛṇāṃ sākṣī nṛṣu sākṣī goṣu nātho gavāmpatiḥ /
goṣu sūto gavāṃ sūto rājñāṃ dāyādako 'stviha //
353.d:
नृणां साक्षी नृषु साक्षी गोषु नाथो गवाम्पतिः /
गोषु सूतो गवां सूतो राज्ञां दायादको ऽस्त्विह //
353.m: 'Witness among men (*nṛṇām* / *nṛṣu*)'; 'Master among cattle (*goṣu* / *gavām*)'; / 'Charioteer among cattle (*goṣu* / *gavām*)'; 'Let there be here an heir of kings.'

353.s:
annasya(1) hetorvasati ṣaṣṭhī smṛtyarthakarmaṇi /
mātuḥ smarati goptāraṃ nityaṃ syāt kartṛkarmaṇoḥ /
apāṃ bhettā tava kṛtirna niṣṭhādiṣu ṣaṣṭhyapi //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vyākaraṇe kārakaṃ nāma
tripañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha catuḥpañcaśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
samāsaḥ
353.d:
अन्नस्य(1) हेतोर्वसति षष्ठी स्मृत्यर्थकर्मणि /
मातुः स्मरति गोप्तारं नित्यं स्यात् कर्तृकर्मणोः /
अपां भेत्ता तव कृतिर्न निष्ठादिषु षष्ठ्यपि //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे व्याकरणे कारकं नाम
त्रिपञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ चतुःपञ्चशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
समासः
353.m:
'He lives for the sake of food'; the sixth [case] in the object of verbs of remembering: / 'He remembers the mother'; it is always [used] for the protector in the agent and object: / 'Splitter of waters'; 'your work'; but the sixth does not occur in participles (*niṣṭhā*), etc.
Thus ends the three hundred and fifty-third chapter, named 'Case-Relations' in grammar, in the Great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the three hundred and fifty-fourth chapter.
Compound Words (Samāsa).

354.s:
skanda uvāca
ṣoḍhā samāsaṃ vakṣyāmi aṣṭāviṃśatidhā punaḥ /
nityānityavibhāgena luglopena ca dvidhā //
354.d:
स्कन्द उवाच
षोढा समासं वक्ष्यामि अष्टाविंशतिधा पुनः /
नित्यानित्यविभागेन लुग्लोपेन च द्विधा //
354.m: Skanda said: / I will explain the compound as sixfold, and again twenty-eight-fold, / divided into obligatory and non-obligatory, and twofold by elision (*luk*) and non-elision (*aluk*).

354.s:
kumbhakāraś ca nityaḥ syāddhemakārādikas tathā /
rājñaḥ pumān rājapumān nityo 'yañca samāsakaḥ //
:n
1 arthasyeti ja..
:p 253
354.d:
कुम्भकारश् च नित्यः स्याद्धेमकारादिकस् तथा /
राज्ञः पुमान् राजपुमान् नित्यो ऽयञ्च समासकः //
:न्
1 अर्थस्येति ज..
:प् 253
354.m:
*Kumbhakāra* (potter) is obligatory, and likewise *hemakāra* (goldsmith) and others; / *rājñaḥ pumān* becomes *rājapumān*; and this compound is [also] obligatory.
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: Ja reads *arthasya*.] [Page 253]

354.s:
kaṣṭaśrito luksamāsaḥ kaṇṭhekālādikastvaluk /
syādaṣṭadhā tatpuruṣaḥ prathamādyasupā saha //
354.d:
कष्टश्रितो लुक्समासः कण्ठेकालादिकस्त्वलुक् /
स्यादष्टधा तत्पुरुषः प्रथमाद्यसुपा सह //
354.m: *Kaṣṭaśrita* is a compound with elision (*luk*); but *kaṇṭhekāla* and the like is without elision (*aluk*). / The tatpuruṣa compound may be eightfold, along with the first and subsequent nominal inflections.

354.s:
prathamātatpuruṣo 'yaṃ pūrvaṃ kāyasya vigrahe /
pūrvakāyo 'parakāyo hy adharottarakāyakaḥ //
354.d:
प्रथमातत्पुरुषो ऽयं पूर्वं कायस्य विग्रहे /
पूर्वकायो ऽपरकायो ह्य् अधरोत्तरकायकः //
354.m: This tatpuruṣa with the first [case occurs] in the analysis 'the front part of the body': / *pūrvakāyaḥ* (upper body), *aparakāyaḥ* (lower body), and indeed *adharakāyakaḥ* and *uttarakāyakaḥ*.

354.s:
ardhaṃ kaṇāyā ardhakaṇā bhikṣātūryamathedṛśam /
āpannajīvikastadvat dvitīyā cādharāśritaḥ //
354.d:
अर्धं कणाया अर्धकणा भिक्षातूर्यमथेदृशम् /
आपन्नजीविकस्तद्वत् द्वितीया चाधराश्रितः //
354.m:
Half of a particle is an ‘ardhakaṇā’; then a fourth of alms is ‘bhikṣātūryam’—such is this [compound].
Likewise, one who has attained a livelihood is ‘āpannajīvikaḥ’; and [compounded] with an accusative is ‘adharāśritaḥ’.

354.s:
varṣambhogyo varṣabhogyo dhānyārthaś ca tṛtīyayā /
caturthī syādviṣṇubalirvṛkabhītiś ca pañcamī //
354.d:
वर्षम्भोग्यो वर्षभोग्यो धान्यार्थश् च तृतीयया /
चतुर्थी स्याद्विष्णुबलिर्वृकभीतिश् च पञ्चमी //
354.m:
With an instrumental are ‘varṣambhogyo’ [or] ‘varṣabhogyaḥ’, and ‘dhānyārthaḥ’.
With a dative would be ‘viṣṇubaliḥ’; and ‘vṛkabhītiḥ’ with an ablative.

354.s:
rājñaḥ pumān rājapumān ṣaṣṭhī vṛkṣaphalaṃ tathā /
saptamī cākṣaśauṇḍo 'yamahito nañsamāsakaḥ //
354.d:
राज्ञः पुमान् राजपुमान् षष्ठी वृक्षफलं तथा /
सप्तमी चाक्षशौण्डो ऽयमहितो नञ्समासकः //
354.m:
The man of the king is ‘rājapumān’ with a genitive, as well as ‘vṛkṣaphalam’.
And with a locative is ‘akṣaśauṇḍaḥ’. ‘Ahitaḥ’ is a compound with the negative particle ‘nañ’.

354.s:
karmadhārayaḥ saptadhā nīlotpalamukhāḥ smṛtāḥ /
viśeṣaṇapūrvapado viśeṣyottaratas tathā //
354.d:
कर्मधारयः सप्तधा नीलोत्पलमुखाः स्मृताः /
विशेषणपूर्वपदो विशेष्योत्तरतस् तथा //
354.m:
The karmadhāraya compound is taught as sevenfold, of which ‘nīlotpala’ is foremost:
having an adjective as the first member; likewise, having a substantive as the subsequent member,

354.s:
vaiyākaraṇakhamūciḥ śītoṣṇaṃ dvipadaṃ śubham /
upamānapūrvapadaḥ śaṅkhapāṇḍara ity api //
354.d:
वैयाकरणखमूचिः शीतोष्णं द्विपदं शुभम् /
उपमानपूर्वपदः शङ्खपाण्डर इत्य् अपि //
354.m:
as in ‘vaiyākaraṇakhamūciḥ’; having two words [of equal rank], as in auspicious ‘śītoṣṇam’;
having the standard of comparison as the first member, as in ‘śaṅkhapāṇḍaraḥ’;

354.s:
upamānottarapadaḥ puruśavyāghra ity api /
sambhāvanāpūrvapado guṇavṛddhiritīdṛśam //
354.d:
उपमानोत्तरपदः पुरुशव्याघ्र इत्य् अपि /
सम्भावनापूर्वपदो गुणवृद्धिरितीदृशम् //
354.m:
having the standard of comparison as the subsequent member, as in ‘puruṣavyāghraḥ’;
having a supposition as the first member, as in such [examples] as ‘guṇavṛddhiḥ’,

354.s:
guṇa iti vṛddhirvācyā suhṛdeva suvandhukaḥ /
avadhāraṇapūrvapado bahubrīhiś ca saptadhā //
354.d:
गुण इति वृद्धिर्वाच्या सुहृदेव सुवन्धुकः /
अवधारणपूर्वपदो बहुब्रीहिश् च सप्तधा //
354.m:
where ‘vṛddhi’ is to be expressed as ‘guṇa’; and having a restriction as the first member, as in ‘suhṛdeva’ [and] ‘subandhukaḥ’.
And the bahuvrīhi compound is sevenfold:

354.s:
dvipadaś ca bahuvrīhirārūḍhbhavano naraḥ /
arcitāśeṣapūrvoyaṃ bahvaṅghriḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
354.d:
द्विपदश् च बहुव्रीहिरारूढ्भवनो नरः /
अर्चिताशेषपूर्वोयं बह्वङ्घ्रिः परिकीर्तितः //
354.m:
a two-word bahuvrīhi, such as the man who is ‘ārūḍhabhavanaḥ’ [one whose mansion is mounted];
this ‘arcitāśeṣa-’ is described [as having an adjective] first; and ‘bahvaṅghriḥ’ [having many feet],

354.s:
ete viprāścopadaśāḥ saṅkhyottarapadastvayam /
saṅkhyobhayapado yadvaddvitrā dvyekatrayo naraḥ //
354.d:
एते विप्राश्चोपदशाः सङ्ख्योत्तरपदस्त्वयम् /
सङ्ख्योभयपदो यद्वद्द्वित्रा द्व्येकत्रयो नरः //
354.m:
‘upadaśāḥ’ [meaning] these [about ten] brāhmaṇas, which has a numeral as the subsequent member;
as well as having numerals in both members, as in ‘dvitrāḥ’ [or] ‘dvyekatrayaḥ’ men;

354.s:
sahapūrvapado 'yaṃ syāt samūloddhṛtakastaruḥ /
:p 254
vyatihāralakṣaṇārthaḥ keśākeśi nakhānakhi //
354.d:
सहपूर्वपदो ऽयं स्यात् समूलोद्धृतकस्तरुः /
:प् 254
व्यतिहारलक्षणार्थः केशाकेशि नखानखि //

354.s:
diglakṣyā syāddakṣiṇapūrvā dvigurābhāṣito dvidhā /
ekavadbhāvi dviśṛṅgaṃ pañcamūlī tvekadhā //
354.d:
दिग्लक्ष्या स्याद्दक्षिणपूर्वा द्विगुराभाषितो द्विधा /
एकवद्भावि द्विशृङ्गं पञ्चमूली त्वेकधा //
354.m:
A direction to be characterized is ‘dakṣiṇapūrvā’. Dvigu is declared to be of two kinds:
producing a singular collective, as in ‘dviśṛṅgam’; but ‘pañcamūlī’ is of one kind.

354.s:
dvandvaḥ samāso dvividho hītaretarayogakaḥ /
rudraviṣṇū samāhāro bherīpaṭahamīdṛśam //
354.d:
द्वन्द्वः समासो द्विविधो हीतरेतरयोगकः /
रुद्रविष्णू समाहारो भेरीपटहमीदृशम् //
354.m:
The dvandva compound is twofold: namely, having mutual conjunction,
as in ‘rudraviṣṇū’; and a collective, such as ‘bherīpaṭaham’.

354.s:
dvidhākhyāto 'vyayībhāvo nāmapūrvapado yathā /
śākasya mātrā śākaprati yathāvyayapūrvakaḥ //
354.d:
द्विधाख्यातो ऽव्ययीभावो नामपूर्वपदो यथा /
शाकस्य मात्रा शाकप्रति यथाव्ययपूर्वकः //
354.m:
Avyayībhāva is declared to be twofold: having a noun as the first member,
as a mere vegetable is ‘śākaprati’; and having an indeclinable as the first member,

354.s:
upakumbhañcoparathyaṃ prādhānyena caturvidhaḥ /
uttarapadārthamukhyo dvandvaścobhayamukhyakaḥ /
pūrvārtheśo 'vyayībhāvo bahuvrīhiś ca vāhyagaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vyākaraṇe samāso nāma
catuḥpañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha pañcapañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
taddhitaṃ
354.d:
उपकुम्भञ्चोपरथ्यं प्राधान्येन चतुर्विधः /
उत्तरपदार्थमुख्यो द्वन्द्वश्चोभयमुख्यकः /
पूर्वार्थेशो ऽव्ययीभावो बहुव्रीहिश् च वाह्यगः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे व्याकरणे समासो नाम
चतुःपञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ पञ्चपञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
तद्धितं
354.m:
as in ‘upakumbham’ and ‘uparathyam’. In terms of primacy, [compound] is of four kinds:
the tatpuruṣa where the meaning of the subsequent member is principal; the dvandva where both are principal;
the avyayībhāva where the meaning of the first member dominates; and the bahuvrīhi which refers to an external meaning.
Thus ends the three hundred and fifty-fourth chapter, called Compounds in Grammar, in the Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Agni.
Now begins the three hundred and fifty-fifth chapter.
Secondary nominal suffixes (Taddhita)

355.s:
skanda uvāca
taddhitaṃ trividhaṃ vakṣye sāmānyavṛttirīdṛśī /
le vyaṃsalo vatsalaḥ syādilaci syāttuphenilaṃ //
355.d:
स्कन्द उवाच
तद्धितं त्रिविधं वक्ष्ये सामान्यवृत्तिरीदृशी /
ले व्यंसलो वत्सलः स्यादिलचि स्यात्तुफेनिलं //

355.s:
lomaśaḥ śe pāmano ne ilaci syāttu picchilaṃ /
aṇi prājña ārcakaḥ syāt dantāduraci danturaḥ //
355.d:
लोमशः शे पामनो ने इलचि स्यात्तु पिच्छिलं /
अणि प्राज्ञ आर्चकः स्यात् दन्तादुरचि दन्तुरः //
355.m:
‘lomaśaḥ’ with ‘śa’; ‘pāmanaḥ’ with ‘na’; with ‘ilac’, however, ‘picchilam’;
with ‘aṇ’, ‘prājñaḥ’ and ‘ārcakaḥ’ are formed; from ‘danta’ with ‘urac’, ‘danturaḥ’;

355.s:
re syānmadhuraṃ suśiraṃ re syāt keśara īdṛśaḥ /
:p 255
hiraṇyaṃ ye mālavo ve valaci syādrajasvalaḥ //
355.d:
रे स्यान्मधुरं सुशिरं रे स्यात् केशर ईदृशः /
:प् 255
हिरण्यं ये मालवो वे वलचि स्याद्रजस्वलः //

355.s:
inau dhanī karī hastī dhanikaṃ ṭikanīritaṃ /
payasvī vini māyāvī ūrṇāyuryuci īritaṃ //
355.d:
इनौ धनी करी हस्ती धनिकं टिकनीरितं /
पयस्वी विनि मायावी ऊर्णायुर्युचि ईरितं //
355.m:
with ‘ini’, ‘dhanī’, ‘karī’, ‘hastī’; ‘dhanikaḥ’ is stated with ‘ṭhan’;
with ‘vini’, ‘payasvī’ and ‘māyāvī’; with ‘yuc’, ‘ūrṇāyuḥ’ is stated;

355.s:
vāgmo mini ālaci syādvācālaścāṭacīritaṃ /
phalino varhiṇaḥ kekī vṛndārakas tathā kani //
355.d:
वाग्मो मिनि आलचि स्याद्वाचालश्चाटचीरितं /
फलिनो वर्हिणः केकी वृन्दारकस् तथा कनि //
355.m:
with ‘min’, ‘vāgmī’; with ‘ālac’, ‘vācālaḥ’; and ‘aṭac’ is stated;
‘phalinaḥ’, ‘barhiṇaḥ’, ‘kekī’; and likewise ‘vṛndārakaḥ’ with ‘kan’;

355.s:
āluci śītanna sahate śītāluḥ śvālurīdṛśaḥ /
himālurāluci syācca himaṃ na sahate tathā //
355.d:
आलुचि शीतन्न सहते शीतालुः श्वालुरीदृशः /
हिमालुरालुचि स्याच्च हिमं न सहते तथा //
355.m:
with ‘āluc’, one who cannot endure cold is ‘śītāluḥ’, and such is ‘śvāluḥ’;
and with ‘āluc’ is ‘himāluḥ’, likewise one who cannot endure snow;

355.s:
rūpaṃ vātādulaci syād vātulaścānapatyake /
vāśiṣṭhaḥ kauravo vāsaḥ pāñcālaḥ sosya vāsakaḥ //
355.d:
रूपं वातादुलचि स्याद् वातुलश्चानपत्यके /
वाशिष्ठः कौरवो वासः पाञ्चालः सोस्य वासकः //
355.m:
the form from ‘vāta’ with ‘ulac’ is ‘vātulaḥ’; and in the non-patronymic sense:
‘vāsiṣṭhaḥ’, ‘kauravaḥ’; residing [there] is ‘pāñcālaḥ’, this is his residence;

355.s:
tatra vāso māthuraḥ syādvettyadhīte ca cāndrakaḥ /
vyutkramaṃ vetti kramakaḥ naraś cakrāma kauśakaḥ //
355.d:
तत्र वासो माथुरः स्याद्वेत्त्यधीते च चान्द्रकः /
व्युत्क्रमं वेत्ति क्रमकः नरश् चक्राम कौशकः //
355.m:
dwelling there is ‘māthuraḥ’; he who knows or studies is ‘cāndrakaḥ’;
he who knows the inverted order is ‘kramakaḥ’; the man who has traversed is ‘kauśakaḥ’;

355.s:
priyaṅgūnāṃ bhavaṃ kṣetraṃ praiyaṅgavīnakaṃ khañi /
maudgīnaṃ kaudravīṇañca vaidehaścānapatyake //
355.d:
प्रियङ्गूनां भवं क्षेत्रं प्रैयङ्गवीनकं खञि /
मौद्गीनं कौद्रवीणञ्च वैदेहश्चानपत्यके //
355.m:
a field suitable for growing panic seeds is ‘praiyaṅgavīnam’ with ‘khañ’;
‘maudgīnam’ and ‘kaudravīṇam’; and ‘vaidehaḥ’ in a non-patronymic sense;

355.s:
iñi dākṣirdāśarathiḥ kaci nārāyaṇādikaṃ /
āśvāyanaḥ syācca phañi yaci gārgyaś ca vātsakaḥ //
355.d:
इञि दाक्षिर्दाशरथिः कचि नारायणादिकं /
आश्वायनः स्याच्च फञि यचि गार्ग्यश् च वात्सकः //
355.m:
with ‘iñ’, ‘dākṣiḥ’ and ‘dāśarathiḥ’; with ‘kañ’, ‘nārāyaṇa’ and the like;
with ‘phañ’ is ‘āśvāyanaḥ’; and with ‘yañ’, ‘gārgyaḥ’ and ‘vātsyaḥ’;

355.s:
ḍhhaki syādvainateyādiścāṭakerastathairaki(?) /
ḍhraki gaudherako rūpaṃ gaudhāraścārakīritaṃ //
355.d:
ढ्हकि स्याद्वैनतेयादिश्चाटकेरस्तथैरकि(?) /
ढ्रकि गौधेरको रूपं गौधारश्चारकीरितं //
355.m:
with ‘ḍhak’ are ‘vainateya’ and the like; and ‘cāṭakeraḥ’ with ‘erak’;
with ‘ḍhrak’, the form is ‘gaudherakaḥ’; and ‘gaudhāraḥ’ is stated with ‘ārak’;

355.s:
kṣatriyo ghe kulīnaḥ khe ṇye kairavyādayaḥ smṛtāḥ(?) /
yati mūrdhanyamukhyādiḥ sugandhiriti rūpakaṃ //
355.d:
क्षत्रियो घे कुलीनः खे ण्ये कैरव्यादयः स्मृताः(?) /
यति मूर्धन्यमुख्यादिः सुगन्धिरिति रूपकं //
355.m:
‘kṣatriyaḥ’ with ‘gha’; ‘kulīnaḥ’ with ‘kha’; with ‘ṇya’, ‘kairavya’ and others are taught;
with ‘yat’, ‘mūrdhanya’, ‘mukhya’, and the like; such is the formation ‘sugandhiḥ’;

355.s:
tārakādibhya itaci nabhastārakitādayaḥ /
anaṅi syācca kuṇḍodhnī puṣpadhanvasudhanvanī //
355.d:
तारकादिभ्य इतचि नभस्तारकितादयः /
अनङि स्याच्च कुण्डोध्नी पुष्पधन्वसुधन्वनी //
355.m:
after ‘tārakā’ and others, with ‘itac’, ‘nabhastārakita’ and the like;
with ‘anaṅ’ are ‘kuṇḍodhnaḥ’ [or feminine ‘kuṇḍodhnī’], ‘puṣpadhanvā’, and ‘sudhanvā’;

355.s:
cañcupi vittavañcuḥ syādvittamasya ca śabdake /
caṇapi syāt keśacaṇaḥ rūpe syāt paṭarūpakam //
:p 256
355.d:
चञ्चुपि वित्तवञ्चुः स्याद्वित्तमस्य च शब्दके /
चणपि स्यात् केशचणः रूपे स्यात् पटरूपकम् //
:प् 256

355.s:
īyasau ca paṭīyān syāt tarapyakṣatarādikam /
pacatitarāñca tarapi tamapyaṭatitamāmapi //
355.d:
ईयसौ च पटीयान् स्यात् तरप्यक्षतरादिकम् /
पचतितराञ्च तरपि तमप्यटतितमामपि //
355.m:
with ‘īyasun’, ‘paṭīyān’ is formed; with ‘tarap’, ‘akṣataram’ and the like;
and ‘pacatitarām’ with ‘tarap’; with ‘tamap’, ‘aṭatitamām’ as well;

355.s:
mṛdvītamā kalpapi syādindrakalpo 'rkakalpakaḥ /
rājadeśīyo deśīye deśye deśyādirūpakam //
355.d:
मृद्वीतमा कल्पपि स्यादिन्द्रकल्पो ऽर्ककल्पकः /
राजदेशीयो देशीये देश्ये देश्यादिरूपकम् //
355.m:
‘mṛdvītamā’; with ‘kalpap’, ‘indrakalpaḥ’ and ‘arkakalpaḥ’;
with ‘deśīyar’, ‘rājadeśīyaḥ’; with ‘deśya’, the form ‘deśya’ and the like;

355.s:
paṭujātīyo jātīye jānumātrañca mātraci /
ūrudvayaso dvayasaci urudaghnañca daghnaci //
355.d:
पटुजातीयो जातीये जानुमात्रञ्च मात्रचि /
ऊरुद्वयसो द्वयसचि उरुदघ्नञ्च दघ्नचि //
355.m:
with ‘jātīyar’, ‘paṭujātīyaḥ’; with ‘mātrac’, ‘jānumātram’;
with ‘dvayasac’, ‘ūrudvayasam’; and with ‘daghnac’, ‘ūrudaghnam’;

355.s:
tayaṭi syāt pañcatayaḥ dauvārikaṣṭhakīritaṃ /
sāmānyavṛttiruktātha avyayākhyaś ca taddhitaḥ //
355.d:
तयटि स्यात् पञ्चतयः दौवारिकष्ठकीरितं /
सामान्यवृत्तिरुक्ताथ अव्ययाख्यश् च तद्धितः //
355.m:
with ‘tayaṭ’ is ‘pañcatayaḥ’; ‘dauvārikaḥ’ is stated with ‘ṭhak’.
The general usage has thus been spoken; now the taddhita called indeclinable:

355.s:
yasmādyatatasili ca yatra tatra tralīritaṃ /
asmin kāle hy adhunāsyādidānīñcaiva dānyapi //
355.d:
यस्माद्यततसिलि च यत्र तत्र त्रलीरितं /
अस्मिन् काले ह्य् अधुनास्यादिदानीञ्चैव दान्यपि //
355.m:
from ‘yasmāt’, ‘yataḥ’ with ‘tasil’; with ‘tral’, ‘yatra’ and ‘tatra’ are stated;
in this time is ‘adhunā’; and with ‘dānīm’ is ‘idānīm’;

355.s:
sarvasmin sarvadā dāsyāttasminkāle rhilīritaṃ /
tarhi ho 'min kāla iha karhi kasmiṃś ca kālake //
355.d:
सर्वस्मिन् सर्वदा दास्यात्तस्मिन्काले र्हिलीरितं /
तर्हि हो ऽमिन् काल इह कर्हि कस्मिंश् च कालके //
355.m:
in all [time] is ‘sarvadā’ with ‘dā’; at that time is stated with ‘rhil’,
‘tarhi’; ‘iha’ in this time with ‘ha’; and ‘karhi’ at which time;

355.s:
yathā thāli thami kathaṃ pūrvasyāndiśi sañcayet /
astāti caiva pūrvasyāḥ pūrvādigrāmaṇīyakāḥ //
355.d:
यथा थालि थमि कथं पूर्वस्यान्दिशि सञ्चयेत् /
अस्ताति चैव पूर्वस्याः पूर्वादिग्रामणीयकाः //
355.m:
‘yathā’ with ‘thāl’; ‘katham’ with ‘thamu’; in the eastern direction one may gather;
with ‘astāt’ is ‘pūrvastāt’; from the east are ‘pūrvādigrāmaṇīyakāḥ’;

355.s:
purastāt sañcared gacchet sadyastulye 'hanīritaṃ /
uti pūrvābde ca parut pūrvatare parāryapi //
355.d:
पुरस्तात् सञ्चरेद् गच्छेत् सद्यस्तुल्ये ऽहनीरितं /
उति पूर्वाब्दे च परुत् पूर्वतरे परार्यपि //
355.m:
one may move about or go in front (‘purastāt’); ‘sadyas’ is stated for ‘on the very same day’;
in the previous year is ‘parut’ with ‘ut’; in the year before that, ‘parāri’;

355.s:
aiṣamo 'smin saṃbatsare rūpaṃ samasi ceritaṃ /
edyavau paredyavi syāt parasminnahanīritaṃ //
355.d:
ऐषमो ऽस्मिन् संबत्सरे रूपं समसि चेरितं /
एद्यवौ परेद्यवि स्यात् परस्मिन्नहनीरितं //
355.m:
in this year is the form ‘aiṣamaḥ’, stated with ‘samas’;
with ‘edyavi’, ‘paredyavi’ is stated in the sense of on the following day;

355.s:
adyāsminnahani dye syāt pūrvedyuś ca tathaidyusi /
dakṣiṇasyāndiśi vaset dakṣiṇāddakṣiṇādyubhau //
355.d:
अद्यास्मिन्नहनि द्ये स्यात् पूर्वेद्युश् च तथैद्युसि /
दक्षिणस्यान्दिशि वसेत् दक्षिणाद्दक्षिणाद्युभौ //
355.m:
with ‘dyus’, ‘adya’ is for ‘on this day’, and likewise ‘pūrvedyuḥ’ with ‘aidyusi’;
one may dwell in the southern direction: both ‘dakṣiṇāt’ and ‘dakṣiṇā’ [are used];

355.s:
uttarasyāndiśi vaseduttarāduttarādyubhau /
upari vasedupariṣṭād bhavedriṣṭāti ūrdhvakāt //
355.d:
उत्तरस्यान्दिशि वसेदुत्तरादुत्तराद्युभौ /
उपरि वसेदुपरिष्टाद् भवेद्रिष्टाति ऊर्ध्वकात् //
355.m:
one may dwell in the northern direction: both ‘uttarāt’ and ‘uttarā’ [are used];
one may dwell above: from the upper is formed ‘upariṣṭāt’ with ‘riṣṭāt’;

355.s:
uttareṇ ca pitroktaṃ āci ca syācca dakṣiṇā /
:p 257
āhau dakṣiṇāhi vaseddviprakāraṃ dvidhā ca dhā //
355.d:
उत्तरेण् च पित्रोक्तं आचि च स्याच्च दक्षिणा /
:प् 257
आहौ दक्षिणाहि वसेद्द्विप्रकारं द्विधा च धा //

355.s:
dhyamuñi caikadhyaṃ kuru tvaṃ dvaidhandhamuñi cedṛśaṃ /
dvau prakārau dvidhā dhāci(1) āsusurataraṃ yathā(2)* //
355.d:
ध्यमुञि चैकध्यं कुरु त्वं द्वैधन्धमुञि चेदृशं /
द्वौ प्रकारौ द्विधा धाचि(1) आसुसुरतरं यथा(2)* //
355.m:
with ‘dhyamuñ’, ‘do you make it unified’ (‘aikadhyam’); such is ‘dvaidham’ with ‘dhamuñ’;
in two manners is ‘dvidhā’ with ‘dhāc’, as well as ‘āsusuratara’;

355.s:
nipātāstaddhitāḥ proktāḥ taddhito bhāvavācakaḥ /
paṭorbhāvaḥ paṭutvantve padutā taliceritaṃ //
355.d:
निपातास्तद्धिताः प्रोक्ताः तद्धितो भाववाचकः /
पटोर्भावः पटुत्वन्त्वे पदुता तलिचेरितं //
355.m:
particles are called taddhita suffixes; a taddhita suffix denotes state of being:
the state of being sharp is ‘paṭutvam’ with ‘tva’; with ‘tal’, ‘paṭutā’ is stated;

355.s:
prathimā cemani pṛthoḥ saukhyaṃ sukhāt ṣyañīritam /
steyaṃ yāti ca stenasya ye sakhyuḥ sakhyamīritaṃ //
355.d:
प्रथिमा चेमनि पृथोः सौख्यं सुखात् ष्यञीरितम् /
स्तेयं याति च स्तेनस्य ये सख्युः सख्यमीरितं //
355.m:
and ‘prathimā’ from ‘pṛthu’ with ‘imanic’; from ‘sukha’, ‘saukhyam’ is stated with ‘ṣyañ’;
that of a thief is ‘steyam’ with ‘yat’; that of a friend is stated as ‘sakhyam’ with ‘ya’;

355.s:
kaperbhāvaś ca kāpeyaṃ sainyaṃ pathyaṃ yakīritaṃ /
āśvaṃ kaumārakaṃ cāṇi rūpaṃ cāṇi ca yauvanam /
ācāryakaṃ kaṇi proktamevamanyepi taddhitāḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vyakaraṇe taddhitasiddharūpaṃ nāma
pañcapañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha ṣaṭpañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
uṇādisiddharūpam
355.d:
कपेर्भावश् च कापेयं सैन्यं पथ्यं यकीरितं /
आश्वं कौमारकं चाणि रूपं चाणि च यौवनम् /
आचार्यकं कणि प्रोक्तमेवमन्येपि तद्धिताः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे व्यकरणे तद्धितसिद्धरूपं नाम
पञ्चपञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ षट्पञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
उणादिसिद्धरूपम्

356.s:
kumāra uvāca
uṇādayo 'bhidhāsyante pratyayā dhātutaḥ pare /
uṇi kāruś ca śilpī syāt jāyurmāyuś ca pittakaṃ //
356.d:
कुमार उवाच
उणादयो ऽभिधास्यन्ते प्रत्यया धातुतः परे /
उणि कारुश् च शिल्पी स्यात् जायुर्मायुश् च पित्तकं //
356.m: Kumāra said: / The suffixes called uṇādi and so forth, added after a verbal root, will now be explained. / With [the suffix] uṇ, kāru means an artisan; jāyu and māyu mean bile.

356.s:
gomāyurvāyurvedeṣu vahulaṃ syuruṇādayaḥ /
:n
1 pāṭho 'yam paunaruktyadoṣeṇa duṣṭaḥ
2 khayaṃ suṣṭhutarā yatheti ja.. / amumuttarā yatheti ṭa..
pāṭho 'yaṃ, etatpāṭhasthalābhisiktapāṭhāntarañca na samyak
pratibhāti
:p 258
āyuḥ svāduś ca hetvādyāḥ kiṃśārurdhānyaśūkakaḥ //
356.d:
गोमायुर्वायुर्वेदेषु वहुलं स्युरुणादयः /
:न्
1 पाठो ऽयम् पौनरुक्त्यदोषेण दुष्टः
2 खयं सुष्ठुतरा यथेति ज.. / अमुमुत्तरा यथेति ट..
पाठो ऽयं, एतत्पाठस्थलाभिसिक्तपाठान्तरञ्च न सम्यक्
प्रतिभाति
:प् 258
आयुः स्वादुश् च हेत्वाद्याः किंशारुर्धान्यशूककः //
356.m:
Gomāyu [means a jackal]; vāyu [means wind]. In the Vedas, the uṇādi suffixes are [employed] diversely.
[Footnote]
[Footnote:] 1. This reading is faulty through the fault of tautology.
[Footnote:] 2. "khayaṃ suṣṭhutarā yathā" thus in manuscript ja; "amumuttarā yathā" thus in manuscript ṭa.
[Footnote:] This reading, and another variant substituted in place of this reading, does not appear correct. / [Page 258]
Āyus [means life], and svādu [means sweet], hetu [means cause], and so forth; kiṃśāru means the beard of grain.

356.s:
kṛkavākuḥ kukkuṭaḥ syād gururbhartā marus tathā /
śayuścājagaro jñeyaḥ sa harāyudhamucyate //
356.d:
कृकवाकुः कुक्कुटः स्याद् गुरुर्भर्ता मरुस् तथा /
शयुश्चाजगरो ज्ञेयः स हरायुधमुच्यते //
356.m: Kṛkavāku means a rooster; guru [means] a teacher or husband; maru likewise [means a desert]. / Śayu is to be known as a python; that is spoken of as a weapon of Hara [Śiva].

356.s:
svarurvaṃjñaṃ trapurusi samasāraṃ phalgurīritaṃ /
gṛdhnaś ca krani kiraci mandiraṃ timiraṃ tamaḥ //
356.d:
स्वरुर्वंज्ञं त्रपुरुसि समसारं फल्गुरीरितं /
गृध्नश् च क्रनि किरचि मन्दिरं तिमिरं तमः //
356.m: Svaru [means sacrificial post]; vaṃjña […]; trapu [means] lead with [the suffix] usi; phalgu is declared to mean weak substance. / Gṛdhna [greedy] is formed with kran; with kirac [come] mandira [abode] and timira [darkness] meaning tamas.

356.s:
ilaci salilaṃ vāri kalyāṇaṃ bhaṇḍilaṃ smṛtaṃ /
budho vidvān kvasau syācca śiviraṃ guptasaṃsthitiḥ //
356.d:
इलचि सलिलं वारि कल्याणं भण्डिलं स्मृतं /
बुधो विद्वान् क्वसौ स्याच्च शिविरं गुप्तसंस्थितिः //
356.m: With ilac [comes] salila [meaning] water; bhaṇḍila is traditionally regarded as auspicious. / Budha means wise; with kvasu [are formed participles]; and śivira means a secret camp.

356.s:
oturviḍālaś ca tuni abhidhānādugādayaḥ /
karṇaḥ kāmī ca gṛhabhūrvāsturjaivātṛkaḥ smṛtaḥ //
356.d:
ओतुर्विडालश् च तुनि अभिधानादुगादयः /
कर्णः कामी च गृहभूर्वास्तुर्जैवातृकः स्मृतः //
356.m: Otu means a cat; with tun [the suffixes] ug and so forth are derived by naming: / karṇa [ear], kāmī [desirous], and land for a house is vāstu; jaivātṛka [long-lived] is traditionally remembered.

356.s:
anaḍvān vahatervini syājjātau jīvārṇavauṣadhaṃ /
nau vahnirinani hariṇaḥ mṛgaḥ kāmī ca bhājanam(1) //
356.d:
अनड्वान् वहतेर्विनि स्याज्जातौ जीवार्णवौषधं /
नौ वह्निरिननि हरिणः मृगः कामी च भाजनम्(1) //
356.m: Anaḍvān [ox] is from [the root] vah with [the suffix] vin; in the class of natural kinds [are formed] jīva, arṇava, [and] auṣadha; / nau [boat]; with inan [comes] vahni [fire]; hariṇa is a deer; kāmī [lustful] and bhājana [receptacle].

356.s:
kambojo bhājanambhāṇḍaṃ saraṇḍaś ca catuṣpadaḥ /
tarureraṇḍaḥ saṅghāto varūḍaḥ sāma nirbharaṃ //
356.d:
कम्बोजो भाजनम्भाण्डं सरण्डश् च चतुष्पदः /
तरुरेरण्डः सङ्घातो वरूडः साम निर्भरं //
356.m: Kamboja is a vessel, a pot; and saraṇḍa is a quadruped [lizard]; / the tree eraṇḍa [castor-oil plant]; varūḍa is a multitude; sāma is intense.

356.s:
sphāraṃ prabhūtaṃ syānnāntapratyaye cīravalkalaṃ /
kātaro bhīrurugrastu pracaṇḍo javasaṃ tṛṇaṃ //
356.d:
स्फारं प्रभूतं स्यान्नान्तप्रत्यये चीरवल्कलं /
कातरो भीरुरुग्रस्तु प्रचण्डो जवसं तृणं //
356.m: Sphāra means abundant; with a suffix ending in n [comes] cīra, [meaning] bark garment; / kātara means timid, fearful; ugra means fierce; javasa means grass.

356.s:
jagaccaiva tu bhūrloko kṛśānurjyotirarkakaḥ /
varvaraḥ kuṭilo dhūrtaś catvarañca catuṣpathaṃ //
356.d:
जगच्चैव तु भूर्लोको कृशानुर्ज्योतिरर्ककः /
वर्वरः कुटिलो धूर्तश् चत्वरञ्च चतुष्पथं //
356.m: Jagat means the earth, the world; kṛśānu means fire or the sun; / varvara means crooked, a rogue; and catvara means a crossroad.

356.s:
cīvaraṃ bhikṣuprāvṛttirādityo mitra īritaḥ /
putra sūnuḥ pitā tātaḥ pṛdākurvyāghravṛścike /
garto 'vaṭo 'tha bharato naṭo 'parepyuṇādayaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vyākaraṇe uṇādisiddharūpaṃ nāma
ṣatpañcāśaṭadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:n
1 pāṭho 'yaṃ na sādhu saṅgacchate
:p 259
:ś atha saptapañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
tiṅvibhaktisiddharūpaṃ
356.d:
चीवरं भिक्षुप्रावृत्तिरादित्यो मित्र ईरितः /
पुत्र सूनुः पिता तातः पृदाकुर्व्याघ्रवृश्चिके /
गर्तो ऽवटो ऽथ भरतो नटो ऽपरेप्युणादयः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे व्याकरणे उणादिसिद्धरूपं नाम
षत्पञ्चाशटधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:न्
1 पाठो ऽयं न साधु सङ्गच्छते
:प् 259
:श् अथ सप्तपञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
तिङ्विभक्तिसिद्धरूपं
356.m:
Cīvara means a mendicant's garment; the sun is called mitra; / putra and sūnu mean a son; pitā and tāta mean a father; pṛdāku refers to a tiger and a scorpion; / garta means a pit; bharata means an actor; and there are other uṇādi formations as well.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, in [the section on] grammar, the three hundred and fifty-sixth chapter, named 'The forms accomplished by the uṇādi [suffixes]'.
[Footnote]
[Footnote:] 1. This reading does not fit well. / [Page 259]
Now, the three hundred and fifty-seventh chapter.
The forms accomplished by the verbal endings (tiṅ).

357.s:
kumāra uvāca
tiṅvibhaktiṃ pravakṣyāmi tathādeśaṃ samāsataḥ /
tiṅstriṣvapi vartante bhāve karmaṇi kartari //
357.d:
कुमार उवाच
तिङ्विभक्तिं प्रवक्ष्यामि तथादेशं समासतः /
तिङ्स्त्रिष्वपि वर्तन्ते भावे कर्मणि कर्तरि //
357.m: Kumāra said: / I shall explain the tiṅ-inflection and its substitutes in brief. / The tiṅ endings occur in all three: in the state (bhāva), in the object (karman), [and] in the agent (kartṛ).

357.s:
sakarmakārmakācca kartari dvipade smṛtāḥ /
sakarmakākarmaṇi ca tadādeśastatheritaḥ //
357.d:
सकर्मकार्मकाच्च कर्तरि द्विपदे स्मृताः /
सकर्मकाकर्मणि च तदादेशस्तथेरितः //
357.m: From transitive and intransitive [roots] they are remembered in two voices for the agent; / and from a transitive [root] in the object; their substitutes are likewise stated.

357.s:
vartamāne laḍākhyāto vidhyādyarthe liṅīritaḥ /
vidhyādau loḍāśiṣi ca bhūtānadyatane ca laṅ //
357.d:
वर्तमाने लडाख्यातो विध्याद्यर्थे लिङीरितः /
विध्यादौ लोडाशिषि च भूतानद्यतने च लङ् //
357.m: Laṭ is taught in the present tense; liṅ is stated in the sense of injunction and the like; / loṭ is in injunction and the like, and in benediction; and laṅ is in the non-current past.

357.s:
bhūte luṅliṭ parokṣe 'tha bhāvinyadyatane ca luṭ /
liṅāśiṣi ca śeṣe 'rthe laḍbhaviṣyati ḷṅbhavet //
357.d:
भूते लुङ्लिट् परोक्षे ऽथ भाविन्यद्यतने च लुट् /
लिङाशिषि च शेषे ऽर्थे लड्भविष्यति ऌङ्भवेत् //
357.m: Luṅ is in the past; liṭ is in the unperceived [past]; and luṭ is in the non-current future; / liṅ is in benediction; and in the remaining sense [of future] lṛṭ occurs; [in conditional sense] there is lṛṅ.

357.s:
liṅnimimitte kriyātipattau pare navātmanepadam /
pūrvaṃ nava parasmaipadantiptasantīti prathamaḥ pumāna //
357.d:
लिङ्निमिमित्ते क्रियातिपत्तौ परे नवात्मनेपदम् /
पूर्वं नव परस्मैपदन्तिप्तसन्तीति प्रथमः पुमान //
357.m: When a cause for liṅ is present, upon non-performance of the action, the last nine are ātmanepada. / The first nine are parasmaipada; tip, tas, jhi (anti) form the first (third) person.

357.s:
sipthastha madhyamanaro mipvasmascottamaḥ pumān /
ta ātāṃ antātmane mukhyaḥ thāsāthāṃ dhvañca madhyamaḥ //
357.d:
सिप्थस्थ मध्यमनरो मिप्वस्मस्चोत्तमः पुमान् /
त आतां अन्तात्मने मुख्यः थासाथां ध्वञ्च मध्यमः //
357.m: Sip, thas, tha are the middle (second) person; mip, vas, mas are the highest (first) person. / Ta, ātām, jha (anta) are the main [endings] for the ātmanepada; thās, āthām, and dhvam are the middle;

357.s:
uttama i vahi mahi bhūvādyā dhātavaḥ smṛtāḥ /
bhuviredhiḥ pacirnandirdhvaṃsiḥ śraṃsiḥ padistvadiḥ //
357.d:
उत्तम इ वहि महि भूवाद्या धातवः स्मृताः /
भुविरेधिः पचिर्नन्दिर्ध्वंसिः श्रंसिः पदिस्त्वदिः //
357.m: iṭ, vahi, mahi are the highest. The roots are remembered as bhū and the rest: / bhū, edh, pac, nand, dhvaṃs, bhraṃś, pad, and vad;

357.s:
śīṅaḥ krīḍo juhotiś ca jahātiś ca dadhātyapi /
dīvyatiḥ svapitirnahiḥ sunotirvasireva ca //
357.d:
शीङः क्रीडो जुहोतिश् च जहातिश् च दधात्यपि /
दीव्यतिः स्वपितिर्नहिः सुनोतिर्वसिरेव च //
357.m: śīṅ, krīḍ, hu, hā, and also dhā; / div, svap, nah, su, and vas;

357.s:
tudirmṛśatirmuñcatiḥ rudhirbhujistyajistaniḥ /
śavādike vikaraṇe maniś caiva karotyapi //
:p 260
357.d:
तुदिर्मृशतिर्मुञ्चतिः रुधिर्भुजिस्त्यजिस्तनिः /
शवादिके विकरणे मनिश् चैव करोत्यपि //
:प् 260
357.m:
tud, mṛś, muc, rudh, bhuj, tyaj, tan; / with the conjugational marker śap and the rest, man and also kṛ;
[Page 260]

357.s:
krīḍtirvṛṅo grahiścoriḥ pā nīrarciś ca nāyakāḥ /
bhuvi syāt tiṅ bhavati saḥ bhavatastau bhavanti te //
357.d:
क्रीड्तिर्वृङो ग्रहिश्चोरिः पा नीरर्चिश् च नायकाः /
भुवि स्यात् तिङ् भवति सः भवतस्तौ भवन्ति ते //
357.m: krī, vṛ, grah, cur, pā, nī, arc are the leading roots. / For bhū there is tiṅ: bhavati saḥ ("he is"), bhavatas tau ("those two are"), bhavanti te ("they are");

357.s:
bhavasi tvaṃ yuvāṃ bhavatho yūyaṃ bhavatha cāpyahaṃ /
bhavāmyāvāṃ bhavāvaś ca bhavāmo hy edhate kulaṃ //
357.d:
भवसि त्वं युवां भवथो यूयं भवथ चाप्यहं /
भवाम्यावां भवावश् च भवामो ह्य् एधते कुलं //
357.m: bhavasi tvam ("you are"), yuvāṃ bhavathaḥ ("you two are"), yūyaṃ bhavatha ("you all are"), and also aham / bhavāmi ("I am"), āvāṃ bhavāvaḥ ("we two are"), and bhavāmaḥ ("we are"); edhate kulam ("the family prospers");

357.s:
edhete dve tathaidhante edhase tvaṃ hi medhayā /
edhethe ca samedhadhve edhe hy edhāvahe dhiyā //
357.d:
एधेते द्वे तथैधन्ते एधसे त्वं हि मेधया /
एधेथे च समेधध्वे एधे ह्य् एधावहे धिया //
357.m: edhete dve ("two prosper"), likewise edhante ("they prosper"); edhase tvam ("you prosper") indeed by intelligence; / edhethe ("you two prosper"), and samedhadhve ("you all prosper together"); edhe ("I prosper"), edhāvahe ("we two prosper") by wisdom;

357.s:
edhāmahe harerbhaktyā pacatītyādi pūrvavat /
bhūyate 'nubhūyate 'sau bhāve karmaṇi vai yaki //
357.d:
एधामहे हरेर्भक्त्या पचतीत्यादि पूर्ववत् /
भूयते ऽनुभूयते ऽसौ भावे कर्मणि वै यकि //
357.m: edhāmahe ("we prosper") by devotion to Hari. Pacati and so forth are as before. / Bhūyate, anubhūyate asau ("it is being experienced") in the state and object when [the suffix] yak is added.

357.s:
vubhūṣati samītyevaṃ ṇici bhāvayatīśvaraṃ /
yaṅi vobhūyate vādyaṃ vobhotei syācca yaṅluki //
357.d:
वुभूषति समीत्येवं णिचि भावयतीश्वरं /
यङि वोभूयते वाद्यं वोभोतेइ स्याच्च यङ्लुकि //
357.m: Bubhūṣati ("wishes to be"), samīti; with ṇic, bhāvayati īśvaram ("causes the Lord to exist"); / with yaṅ, bobhūyate ("is repeatedly"), or bobhoti occurs when yaṅ is elided.

357.s:
putrīyati putrakāmyatyevaṃ paṭapaṭāyate /
ghaṭayaty atha sani ṇici bubhūṣayati rūpakaṃ //
357.d:
पुत्रीयति पुत्रकाम्यत्येवं पटपटायते /
घटयत्य् अथ सनि णिचि बुभूषयति रूपकं //
357.m: Putrīyati ("acts like a son"), putrakāmyati ("desires a son"); likewise paṭapaṭāyate ("makes a crackling sound"); / ghaṭayati; then with san [and] ṇic, bubhūṣayati is the form.

357.s:
bhavedbhavetāñca liṅi bhaveyuś ca bhaveḥ pare /
bhavetañca bhavetaivaṃ bhaveyañca bhaveva ca bhavema ca //
357.d:
भवेद्भवेताञ्च लिङि भवेयुश् च भवेः परे /
भवेतञ्च भवेतैवं भवेयञ्च भवेव च भवेम च //
357.m: In liṅ: bhavet, bhavetām, and bhaveyuḥ; after that bhaveḥ, / bhavetam, and bhaveta; thus bhaveyam, and bhaveva, and bhavema.

357.s:
edheta edheyātāmedheran manasā śriyā /
edhethāś ca edheyāthāmedhedhvamedheya edhevahi edhemahi //
357.d:
एधेत एधेयातामेधेरन् मनसा श्रिया /
एधेथाश् च एधेयाथामेधेध्वमेधेय एधेवहि एधेमहि //
357.m: Edheta, edheyātām, edheran in mind through splendour; / edhethāḥ, and edheyāthām, edhedhvam, edheya, edhevahi, edhemahi.

357.s:
astu tāvadbhavatām loṭi bhavantu bhavatādbhava /
bhavataṃ bhavata bhavāni bhavāva ca bhavāma ca //
357.d:
अस्तु तावद्भवताम् लोटि भवन्तु भवताद्भव /
भवतं भवत भवानि भवाव च भवाम च //
357.m: In loṭ: astu, tāvat bhavatām, bhavantu, bhavatāt, bhava, / bhavatam, bhavata, bhavāni, bhavāva, and bhavāma.

357.s:
edhatāmedhetāmedhantāmedhai pacāvahai pacāmahai /
abhyanandadapacatāmacannapacas tathā //
357.d:
एधतामेधेतामेधन्तामेधै पचावहै पचामहै /
अभ्यनन्ददपचतामचन्नपचस् तथा //
357.m: Edhatām, edhetām, edhantām, edhai, pacāvahai, pacāmahai; / abhyanandat, apacatām, ācan, likewise apacaḥ,

357.s:
abhavatamabhavatāpacamapacāvāpacāma ca /
aidhatairdhetāmaidhadhvaṃ aidhe caidhāmahīritaṃ(?) //
357.d:
अभवतमभवतापचमपचावापचाम च /
ऐधतैर्धेतामैधध्वं ऐधे चैधामहीरितं(?) //
357.m: abhavatam, abhavata, apacam, apacāva, and apacāma; / aidhata, aidhetām, aidhadhvam, aidhe, and aidhāmahi are declared.

357.s:
abhūdabhūtāmabhūvanabhūścābhūvameva luṅ /
:p 261
aidhiṣṭaidhisātāṃ narāvaidhiṣṭhā eidhiṣīdṛśaṃ //
357.d:
अभूदभूतामभूवनभूश्चाभूवमेव लुङ् /
:प् 261
ऐधिष्टैधिसातां नरावैधिष्ठा एइधिषीदृशं //

357.s:
liṭi babhūva babhūvatuḥ babhūvuś ca bavhūvitha /
babhūvathurvabhūva ca babhūviva babhūvima //
357.d:
लिटि बभूव बभूवतुः बभूवुश् च बव्हूविथ /
बभूवथुर्वभूव च बभूविव बभूविम //
357.m: In liṭ: babhūva, babhūvatuḥ, babhūvuḥ, and babhūvitha, / babhūvathuḥ, and babhūva, babhūviva, babhūvima;

357.s:
pece pecāte pecire tvamedhāñcakṛṣe tathā /
edhāñcakrāthe pecidhve pece pecimahe tathā //
357.d:
पेचे पेचाते पेचिरे त्वमेधाञ्चकृषे तथा /
एधाञ्चक्राथे पेचिध्वे पेचे पेचिमहे तथा //
357.m: pece, pecāte, pecire; you, edhāñcakṛṣe, likewise / edhāñcakrāthe, pecidhve, pece, likewise pecimahe.

357.s:
luṭi bhavitā bhavitārau bhavitāro harādayaḥ /
bhavitāsi bhavitāstho bhavitāsmas tathā vayaṃ //
357.d:
लुटि भविता भवितारौ भवितारो हरादयः /
भवितासि भवितास्थो भवितास्मस् तथा वयं //
357.m: In luṭ: bhavitā, bhavitārau, bhavitāraḥ, Hara and others; / bhavitāsi, bhavitāsthaḥ, bhavitāsmaḥ, likewise we [are].

357.s:
paktā paktārau paktāraḥ paktāse tvaṃ śubhaudanaṃ /
paktādhve paktāhe cāhaṃ paktāsmahe hareś caruṃ //
357.d:
पक्ता पक्तारौ पक्तारः पक्तासे त्वं शुभौदनं /
पक्ताध्वे पक्ताहे चाहं पक्तास्महे हरेश् चरुं //
357.m: Paktā, paktārau, paktāraḥ; paktāse tvam ("you will cook") auspicious boiled rice; / paktādhve, and paktāhe aham ("I will cook"), paktāsmahe ("we will cook") Hari's caru offering.

357.s:
liṅāśiṣi sukhaṃ bhūyāt bhūyāstāṃ hariśaṅkarau /
bhūyāsuste ca bhūyāstvaṃ yuvāṃ bhūyāstamīśvarau //
357.d:
लिङाशिषि सुखं भूयात् भूयास्तां हरिशङ्करौ /
भूयासुस्ते च भूयास्त्वं युवां भूयास्तमीश्वरौ //
357.m: In benedictive liṅ: sukhaṃ bhūyāt ("may there be happiness"); bhūyāstām, Hari and Śaṅkara; / bhūyāsuḥ, those; and bhūyāḥ tvam ("may you be"); yuvām bhūyāstam īśvarau ("may you two be lords");

357.s:
bhūyāsta yūyaṃ bhūyāsamahaṃ bhūyāsma sarvadā /
yakṣīṣṭa hy edhiṣīyāstāṃ yakṣīrannedhisīya ca //
357.d:
भूयास्त यूयं भूयासमहं भूयास्म सर्वदा /
यक्षीष्ट ह्य् एधिषीयास्तां यक्षीरन्नेधिसीय च //
357.m: bhūyāsta yūyam ("may you all be"); bhūyāsam aham ("may I be"); bhūyāsma sarvadā ("may we always be"); / yakṣīṣṭa, edhiṣīyāstām, yakṣīran, and edhiṣīya;

357.s:
yakṣīvahyedhisīmahi liṅi cāyakṣyateti ḷṅ /
ayakṣyetāmayakṣyantāyakṣye 'yakṣyethāṃ yuvāṃ //
357.d:
यक्षीवह्येधिसीमहि लिङि चायक्ष्यतेति ऌङ् /
अयक्ष्येतामयक्ष्यन्तायक्ष्ये ऽयक्ष्येथां युवां //
357.m: yakṣīvahi, edhiṣīmahi; and in conditional liṅ, ayakṣyata; in lṛṅ: / ayakṣyetām, ayakṣyanta, ayakṣye, ayakṣyethāṃ yuvām;

357.s:
ayakṣyadhvamaidhiṣyāvahyaidhiṣyāmahyarervayam /
ḷṭi syādbhaviṣyatīti edhiṣyāmaha īdṛśam //
357.d:
अयक्ष्यध्वमैधिष्यावह्यैधिष्यामह्यरेर्वयम् /
ऌटि स्याद्भविष्यतीति एधिष्यामह ईदृशम् //
357.m: ayakṣyadhvam, aidhiṣyāvahi, aidhiṣyāmahi, we, of the enemy; / in lṛṭ there is bhaviṣyati, and edhiṣyāmahe, of this kind.

357.s:
evaṃ vibhāvayiṣyanti bobhaviṣyati rūpakaṃ /
ghaṭayet paṭayettadvat putrīyati ca kāmyati //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vyākaraṇe tiṅsiddharūpaṃ nāma
saptapañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:p 262
:ś athāṣaṭapañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
kṛtsiddharūpam
357.d:
एवं विभावयिष्यन्ति बोभविष्यति रूपकं /
घटयेत् पटयेत्तद्वत् पुत्रीयति च काम्यति //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे व्याकरणे तिङ्सिद्धरूपं नाम
सप्तपञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:प् 262
:श् अथाषटपञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
कृत्सिद्धरूपम्
357.m:
Thus they will derive [the causative] vibhāvayiṣyanti; bobhaviṣyati is the intensive form; / ghaṭayet, paṭayet likewise, and putrīyati and kāmyati.
Thus ends the three hundred fifty-seventh chapter, named “The Form of Inflected Verbal Forms (tiṅ),” in the Grammar of the Great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the three hundred fifty-eighth chapter.
The forms formed by primary suffixes (kṛt).

358.s:
kumāra uvāca
kṛtastriṣvapi vijñeyā bhāve karmaṇi kartari /
ajlyuṭ ktin ghaño bhāve yujakārata eva ca //
358.d:
कुमार उवाच
कृतस्त्रिष्वपि विज्ञेया भावे कर्मणि कर्तरि /
अज्ल्युट् क्तिन् घञो भावे युजकारत एव च //
358.m:
Kumāra said:
Primary suffixes (kṛt) are to be known in three meanings: action, object, and agent.
[The suffixes] ac, lyuṭ, ktin, and ghañ [occur] in the sense of action, as well as yuc and the suffix a.

358.s:
aci dharmasya vinaya utkaraḥ prakaras tathā /
devo bhadraḥ śrīkaraś ca lpuṭi rūpantu śobhanam //
358.d:
अचि धर्मस्य विनय उत्करः प्रकरस् तथा /
देवो भद्रः श्रीकरश् च ल्पुटि रूपन्तु शोभनम् //
358.m:
With ac [are formed] vinaya (‘conduct’) of dharma, utkara (‘heap’), and prakara (‘multitude’),
deva (‘god’), bhadra (‘auspicious’), and śrīkara (‘bestowing prosperity’); but with lyuṭ the form is śobhana (‘beautiful’).

358.s:
ktini vṛddhistutimatī ghañi bhāvo 'tha yucyapi /
kāraṇā bhāvanetyādi akāre ca cikitsayā //
358.d:
क्तिनि वृद्धिस्तुतिमती घञि भावो ऽथ युच्यपि /
कारणा भावनेत्यादि अकारे च चिकित्सया //
358.m:
With ktin [are formed] vṛddhi (‘growth’) and stuti (‘praise’), having sense; with ghañ, bhāva (‘state’); and with yuc also,
kāraṇā, bhāvanā (‘contemplation’), and the like; and with [the suffix] a, [forms such as] cikitsā (‘medical treatment’).

358.s:
tathā tavyo hy anīyaś ca kartavyaṃ karṇīyakam /
deyaṃ dhyeyañcaiva yati ṇyati kāryañca kṛtyakāḥ //
358.d:
तथा तव्यो ह्य् अनीयश् च कर्तव्यं कर्णीयकम् /
देयं ध्येयञ्चैव यति ण्यति कार्यञ्च कृत्यकाः //
358.m:
Likewise, [the gerundives] tavya and anīya [yield] kartavya (‘to be done’) and karaṇīya;
deya (‘to be given’) and dhyeya (‘to be meditated on’) are formed with yat; kārya (‘to be done’) with ṇyat; [these are] the gerundives (kṛtya).

358.s:
kartari ktādayo jñeyā bhāve karmaṇi ca kvacit /
gato grāmaṃ gato grāma āśliṣṭaś ca gurustvayā //
358.d:
कर्तरि क्तादयो ज्ञेया भावे कर्मणि च क्वचित् /
गतो ग्रामं गतो ग्राम आश्लिष्टश् च गुरुस्त्वया //
358.m:
Suffixes such as kta are to be known in the sense of the agent, and sometimes in the sense of action or object:
‘he has gone to the village’ (gato grāmam), ‘the village is gone to’ (gato grāmaḥ), and ‘the guru has been embraced by you’ (āśliṣṭaś ca gurus tvayā).

358.s:
śatṛṅ śānacau bhavan edhamāno bhavantyapi /
vuṇ tṛcau sarvadhātubhyo bhāvako bhavitā pathā //
358.d:
शतृङ् शानचौ भवन् एधमानो भवन्त्यपि /
वुण् तृचौ सर्वधातुभ्यो भावको भविता पथा //
358.m:
[The present participles] śatṛ and śānac [produce] bhavan (‘being’) and edhamāna (‘thriving’), as well as bhavantī;
vuñ and tṛc from all roots [yield forms such as] bhāvaka (‘causing to be’) and bhavitṛ (‘one who will be’).

358.s:
kvibantaś ca svayambhūś ca bhūte liṭaḥ kvansu kāna ca /
babhūvivān pecivāṃś ca pecānaḥ śraddadhānakaḥ //
358.d:
क्विबन्तश् च स्वयम्भूश् च भूते लिटः क्वन्सु कान च /
बभूविवान् पेचिवांश् च पेचानः श्रद्दधानकः //
358.m:
A word ending in kvip is svayambhū (‘self-existent’); in the past tense, kvasu and kānac replace liṭ:
babhūvivas, pecivas, pecāna, and śraddadhāna.

358.s:
aṇi syuḥ kumbhakārādyā bhūtepyuṇādayaḥ smṛtāḥ /
vāyuḥ pāyuś ca kāruḥ syādvahulaṃ chandasīritaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vyākaraṇe kṛtsiddharūpaṃ
nāmāṣṭapañcāśadadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:p 263
:ś athonaṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
svargapātālādivargāḥ
358.d:
अणि स्युः कुम्भकाराद्या भूतेप्युणादयः स्मृताः /
वायुः पायुश् च कारुः स्याद्वहुलं छन्दसीरितं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे व्याकरणे कृत्सिद्धरूपं
नामाष्टपञ्चाशदधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:प् 263
:श् अथोनषष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
स्वर्गपातालादिवर्गाः
358.m:
With the suffix aṇ there are words such as kumbhakāra (‘potter’); the uṇādi suffixes are also taught in the sense of the past:
vāyu (‘wind’), pāyu (‘anus’), and kāru (‘artisan’); [these] are stated abundantly in the Veda.
Thus ends the three hundred fifty-eighth chapter, named “The Form of Derived Primary Nominal Bases (kṛt),” in the Grammar of the Great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the three hundred fifty-ninth chapter.
The groups of words for heaven, the netherworld, and other domains.

359.s:
agnir uvāca
svargādināmaliṅgo yo haristaṃ pravadāmi te /
svaḥsvarganākatridivā dyodivau dvetripiṣṭapaṃ //
359.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
स्वर्गादिनामलिङ्गो यो हरिस्तं प्रवदामि ते /
स्वःस्वर्गनाकत्रिदिवा द्योदिवौ द्वेत्रिपिष्टपं //
359.m:
Agni said:
I shall tell you that [lexicon] which has the names and genders of heaven and other domains, which is Hari:
svar, svarga, nāka, tridiva, the two words dyo and div, and tripiṣṭapa [are synonyms for heaven].

359.s:
devā vṛndārakā lekhā rudrādyā gaṇadevatāḥ /
vidyādharo 'psaroyakṣarakṣogandharvakinnarāḥ //
359.d:
देवा वृन्दारका लेखा रुद्राद्या गणदेवताः /
विद्याधरो ऽप्सरोयक्षरक्षोगन्धर्वकिन्नराः //
359.m:
Devas, vṛndārakas, and lekhas [are gods]; the Rudras and others are class-deities;
vidyādhara, apsaras, yakṣa, rakṣas, gandharva, and kinnara,

359.s:
piśāco guhyakaḥ siddho bhūto 'mī devayonayaḥ /
devadviṣo 'surā daityāḥ sugataḥ syāttathāgataḥ //
359.d:
पिशाचो गुह्यकः सिद्धो भूतो ऽमी देवयोनयः /
देवद्विषो ऽसुरा दैत्याः सुगतः स्यात्तथागतः //
359.m:
piśāca, guhyaka, siddha, and bhūta—these are of divine origin;
asuras and daityas are the enemies of gods; Sugata and Tathāgata [refer to the Buddha].

359.s:
brahmātmabhūḥ surajyeṣṭho viṣṇur nārāyaṇo hariḥ /
revatīśo halī rāmaḥ kāmaḥ pañcaśaraḥ smaraḥ //
359.d:
ब्रह्मात्मभूः सुरज्येष्ठो विष्णुर् नारायणो हरिः /
रेवतीशो हली रामः कामः पञ्चशरः स्मरः //
359.m:
Brahmā, Ātmabhū, and Surajyeṣṭha [are Brahmā]; Viṣṇu, Nārāyaṇa, and Hari [are Viṣṇu];
Revatīśa, Halin, and Rāma [are Balarāma]; Kāma, Pañcaśara, and Smara [are the god of love].

359.s:
lakṣmīḥ padmālayā padmā sarvaḥ sarveśvaraḥ śivaḥ /
kapardo 'sya jaṭājūṭaḥ pināko 'jagavandhanuḥ //
359.d:
लक्ष्मीः पद्मालया पद्मा सर्वः सर्वेश्वरः शिवः /
कपर्दो ऽस्य जटाजूटः पिनाको ऽजगवन्धनुः //
359.m:
Lakṣmī, Padmālayā, and Padmā [are Lakṣmī]; Śarva, Sarveśvara, and Śiva [are Śiva];
kaparda is his matted hair; pināka and ajagava are [his] bow.

359.s:
pramathāḥ syuḥ pāriṣadā mṛḍānī caṇḍikāmbikā /
dvaimāturo gajāsyaś ca senānīragnibhūrguhaḥ //
359.d:
प्रमथाः स्युः पारिषदा मृडानी चण्डिकाम्बिका /
द्वैमातुरो गजास्यश् च सेनानीरग्निभूर्गुहः //
359.m:
The pramathas are [his] attendants; Mṛḍānī, Caṇḍikā, and Ambikā [are his consort];
Dvaimātura and Gajāsya [are Gaṇeśa]; Senānī, Agnibhū, and Guha [are Kārttikeya].

359.s:
ākhāṇḍalaḥ sunāsīraḥ sūtrāmāṇo divaspatiḥ /
pulomajā śacīndrāṇī devī tasya tu vallabhā //
359.d:
आखाण्डलः सुनासीरः सूत्रामाणो दिवस्पतिः /
पुलोमजा शचीन्द्राणी देवी तस्य तु वल्लभा //
359.m:
Ākhāṇḍala, Sunāsīra, Sutrāman, and Divaspati [are Indra];
Pulomajā, Śacī, and Indrāṇī are the goddess who is his beloved.

359.s:
syāt prāsādo vaijayanto jayantaḥ pākaśāsaniḥ /
airāvate 'bhramātaṅgairāvaṇābhramuvallabhāḥ(?) //
359.d:
स्यात् प्रासादो वैजयन्तो जयन्तः पाकशासनिः /
ऐरावते ऽभ्रमातङ्गैरावणाभ्रमुवल्लभाः(?) //
359.m:
His palace is Vaijayanta; Jayanta is the son of Pākaśāsana (Indra);
Airāvata, Abhramātaṅga, Airāvaṇa, and Abhramuvallabha [are his elephant].

359.s:
hrīdinī vajramastrī syāt kuliśambhiduraṃ paviḥ /
vyomayānaṃ vimāno 'strī pīyūṣamamṛtaṃ sudhā //
:p 264
359.d:
ह्रीदिनी वज्रमस्त्री स्यात् कुलिशम्भिदुरं पविः /
व्योमयानं विमानो ऽस्त्री पीयूषममृतं सुधा //
:प् 264

359.s:
syāt sudharmā devasabhā svargaṅgā suradīrghikā /
striyāṃ bahuṣvapsrasaḥ svarveśyā urvaśīmukhāḥ //
359.d:
स्यात् सुधर्मा देवसभा स्वर्गङ्गा सुरदीर्घिका /
स्त्रियां बहुष्वप्स्रसः स्वर्वेश्या उर्वशीमुखाः //
359.m:
Sudharmā is the assembly hall of the gods; Svargaṅgā and Suradīrghikā [refer to the celestial Gaṅgā];
apsarases, [used] in the feminine plural, are the courtesans of heaven, headed by Urvaśī.

359.s:
hāhā hūhūś ca gandharvā agnirvahnirdhanañcayaḥ /
jātavedāḥ kṛṣṇavartmā āśrayāśaś ca pāvakaḥ //
359.d:
हाहा हूहूश् च गन्धर्वा अग्निर्वह्निर्धनञ्चयः /
जातवेदाः कृष्णवर्त्मा आश्रयाशश् च पावकः //
359.m:
Hāhā and Hūhū are Gandharvas; Agni, Vahni, Dhanañjaya,
Jātavedas, Kṛṣṇavartman, Āśrayāśa, and Pāvaka [are the fire-god],

359.s:
hiraṇyaretāḥ saptārciḥ śukraś caivāśuśukṣaṇiḥ /
śucirappittamaurvastu vāḍavo vaḍavānalaḥ //
359.d:
हिरण्यरेताः सप्तार्चिः शुक्रश् चैवाशुशुक्षणिः /
शुचिरप्पित्तमौर्वस्तु वाडवो वडवानलः //
359.m:
as well as Hiraṇyaretas, Saptārcis, Śukra, Āśuśukṣaṇi,
Śuci, and Ap-pittam; the submarine fire is aurva, vāḍava, and vaḍavānala.

359.s:
vahnerdvayorjvālakīlāvarcirhetiḥ śikhā striyāṃ /
triṣu sphuliṅgo 'gnikaṇo dharmarājaḥ paretarāṭ //
359.d:
वह्नेर्द्वयोर्ज्वालकीलावर्चिर्हेतिः शिखा स्त्रियां /
त्रिषु स्फुलिङ्गो ऽग्निकणो धर्मराजः परेतराट् //
359.m:
In the masculine: the flame and blaze of fire; arcis, heti, and śikhā are in the feminine;
sphuliṅga and agnikaṇa (‘spark’) are in all three [genders]; Dharmarāja and Paretarāṭ [are Yama],

359.s:
kālo 'ntako daṇḍadharaḥ śrāddhedevo 'tha rākṣasaḥ /
kauṇapāsrapakravyādā yātudhānaś ca nairṛtiḥ //
359.d:
कालो ऽन्तको दण्डधरः श्राद्धेदेवो ऽथ राक्षसः /
कौणपास्रपक्रव्यादा यातुधानश् च नैरृतिः //
359.m:
as well as Kāla, Antaka, Daṇḍadhara, and Śrāddhadeva; next, rākṣasa,
kauṇapa, asrapa, kravyād, yātudhāna, and nairṛta [are demons].

359.s:
precetā varuṇaḥ pāśī śvasanaḥ sparśano 'nilaḥ /
sadāgatirmātariśvā prāṇo marut samīraṇaḥ //
359.d:
प्रेचेता वरुणः पाशी श्वसनः स्पर्शनो ऽनिलः /
सदागतिर्मातरिश्वा प्राणो मरुत् समीरणः //
359.m:
Pracetas, Varuṇa, and Pāśin [are Varuṇa]; Śvasana, Sparśana, Anila,
Sadāgati, Mātariśvan, Prāṇa, Marut, and Samīraṇa [are the wind-god].

359.s:
javo raṃhastarasī tu laghukṣipramarandrutam /
satvaraṃ capalaṃ tūrṇamavilambitamāśu ca //
359.d:
जवो रंहस्तरसी तु लघुक्षिप्रमरन्द्रुतम् /
सत्वरं चपलं तूर्णमविलम्बितमाशु च //
359.m:
Java, raṃhas, and taras [denote speed]; laghu, kṣipra, aram, druta,
satvara, capala, tūrṇa, avilambita, and āśu [denote swift].

359.s:
satate 'nāratāśrāntasantatāviratāniśaṃ /
nityānavaratājasramapyathātiśayo bharaḥ //
359.d:
सतते ऽनारताश्रान्तसन्तताविरतानिशं /
नित्यानवरताजस्रमप्यथातिशयो भरः //
359.m:
In the sense of continuous: anārata, aśrānta, santata, avirata, aniśam,
nitya, anavarata, and ajasram; and moreover, [in the sense of] excess: bhara,

359.s:
ativelabhṛśātyarthātimātrodgāṭanirbharam /
tīvraikāntanitāntāni gāḍhavāḍhadṛḍhāni ca //
359.d:
अतिवेलभृशात्यर्थातिमात्रोद्गाटनिर्भरम् /
तीव्रैकान्तनितान्तानि गाढवाढदृढानि च //
359.m:
ativela, bhṛśa, atyartha, atimātra, udgāḍha, nirbhara,
tīvra, ekānta, nitānta, gāḍha, bāḍha, and dṛḍha.

359.s:
guhyakeśo yakṣarājo rājarājo dhanādhipaḥ /
syāt kinnaraḥ kiṃpuruṣasturaṅgavadano mayuḥ //
359.d:
गुह्यकेशो यक्षराजो राजराजो धनाधिपः /
स्यात् किन्नरः किंपुरुषस्तुरङ्गवदनो मयुः //
359.m:
Guhyakeśa, Yakṣarāja, Rājarāja, and Dhanādhipa [are Kubera];
kinnara, kiṃpuruṣa, turaṅgavadana, and mayu [are synonyms].

359.s:
nidhir nā sevadhirvyoma tvabhraṃ puṣkaramambaram /
dyodivau cāntarīkṣaṃ khaṃ kāṣṭhāśākakubho diśaḥ //
359.d:
निधिर् ना सेवधिर्व्योम त्वभ्रं पुष्करमम्बरम् /
द्योदिवौ चान्तरीक्षं खं काष्ठाशाककुभो दिशः //
359.m:
Nidhi in the masculine is sevadhi; vyoman, abhra, puṣkara, ambara,
the two words dyo and div, antarīkṣa, and kha [mean the sky]; kāṣṭhā, āśā, kakubh, and diś [mean a direction].

359.s:
abhyantarantvantarālañcakravāḍantu manḍalaṃ /
:p 265
taḍitvān vārido meghastanayitnurvalāhakaḥ //
359.d:
अभ्यन्तरन्त्वन्तरालञ्चक्रवाडन्तु मन्डलं /
:प् 265
तडित्वान् वारिदो मेघस्तनयित्नुर्वलाहकः //
359.m:
Abhyantara and antarāla [denote space between]; cakravāḍa denotes a circular horizon or sphere.
[Page 265]
Taḍitvant, vārida, megha, stanayitnu, and valāhaka [mean a cloud].

359.s:
kādambanī meghamālā stanitaṃ garjitaṃ tathā /
śampāśatahradāhrādinyairāvatyaḥ kṣaṇaprabhāḥ(?) //
359.d:
कादम्बनी मेघमाला स्तनितं गर्जितं तथा /
शम्पाशतह्रदाह्रादिन्यैरावत्यः क्षणप्रभाः(?) //
359.m:
Kādambinī and meghamālā [mean a bank of clouds]; stanita and garjita [mean thunder];
śampā, śatahradā, hrādinī, airāvatī, kṣaṇaprabhā,

359.s:
taḍitsaudāminī vidyuccañcalā capalāpi ca /
sphurjathurvajraniṣpeṣo vṛṣṭighātastvavagrahaḥ //
359.d:
तडित्सौदामिनी विद्युच्चञ्चला चपलापि च /
स्फुर्जथुर्वज्रनिष्पेषो वृष्टिघातस्त्ववग्रहः //
359.m:
taḍit, saudāminī, vidyut, cañcalā, and capalā [mean lightning];
sphūrjathu is the crash of a thunderbolt; avagraha is the obstruction of rain (drought).

359.s:
dhārā sampāta āśāraḥ śīkaro 'mbukaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ /
varṣopalastu karakā meghachanne 'hni durdinaṃ //
359.d:
धारा सम्पात आशारः शीकरो ऽम्बुकणाः स्मृताः /
वर्षोपलस्तु करका मेघछन्ने ऽह्नि दुर्दिनं //
359.m:
Dhārāsampāta and āsāra [mean a cloudburst]; drops of water are called śīkara;
hail is varṣopala and karakā; a day covered with clouds is durdina.

359.s:
antardhā vyavadhā puṃsi tvantardhirapavāraṇaṃ /
apidhānatirodhānapidhānacchadanāni ca //
359.d:
अन्तर्धा व्यवधा पुंसि त्वन्तर्धिरपवारणं /
अपिधानतिरोधानपिधानच्छदनानि च //
359.m:
Antardhā and vyavadhā; in the masculine antardhi and apavāraṇa;
apidhāna, tirodhāna, pidhāna, and chādana [all mean concealment or covering].

359.s:
abjo jaivātṛkaḥ somo glaurmṛgāṅkaḥ kalānidhiḥ /
vidhuḥ kumudavandhuś ca vimbo 'strī maṇḍalaṃ triṣu //
359.d:
अब्जो जैवातृकः सोमो ग्लौर्मृगाङ्कः कलानिधिः /
विधुः कुमुदवन्धुश् च विम्बो ऽस्त्री मण्डलं त्रिषु //
359.m:
Abja, jaivātṛka, soma, glau, mṛgāṅka, kalānidhi,
vidhu, and kumudabandhu [mean the moon]; bimba is not feminine; maṇḍala is in all three genders [for orb].

359.s:
kalā tu ṣoḍśo bhāgo bhittaṃ śakalakhaṇḍake /
candrikā kaumudī jyotsnā prasādastu prasannatā //
359.d:
कला तु षोड्शो भागो भित्तं शकलखण्डके /
चन्द्रिका कौमुदी ज्योत्स्ना प्रसादस्तु प्रसन्नता //
359.m:
A digit (kalā) is the sixteenth part; bhitta [means] a broken fragment or part;
candrikā, kaumudī, and jyotsnā [mean moonlight]; prasāda is clarity (prasannatā).

359.s:
lakṣaṇaṃ lakṣmakaṃ cihnaṃ śobhā kāntirdyutiśchaviḥ /
suṣamā parmā śobhā tuṣārastuhinaṃ himaṃ //
359.d:
लक्षणं लक्ष्मकं चिह्नं शोभा कान्तिर्द्युतिश्छविः /
सुषमा पर्मा शोभा तुषारस्तुहिनं हिमं //
359.m:
Lakṣaṇa, lakṣman, and cihna [mean mark]; śobhā, kānti, dyuti, and chavi [mean beauty];
suṣamā is supreme beauty; tuṣāra, tuhina, and hima [mean frost].

359.s:
avasyāyastu nīhāraḥ prāleyaḥ śiśiro himaḥ /
nakṣatramṛkṣaṃ bhantārā tārakā pyuḍu vā striyāṃ //
359.d:
अवस्यायस्तु नीहारः प्रालेयः शिशिरो हिमः /
नक्षत्रमृक्षं भन्तारा तारका प्युडु वा स्त्रियां //
359.m:
Avaśyāya, nīhāra, prāleya, and śiśira hima [mean snow or mist];
nakṣatra, ṛkṣa, bha, tārā, tārakā, or uḍu in the feminine [mean star].

359.s:
gururjīva āṅgirasa uśanā bhārgavaḥ kaviḥ /
vidhuntudastamo rāhur lagnaṃ rāśyudayaḥ smṛtaḥ //
359.d:
गुरुर्जीव आङ्गिरस उशना भार्गवः कविः /
विधुन्तुदस्तमो राहुर् लग्नं राश्युदयः स्मृतः //
359.m:
Guru, Jīva, and Āṅgirasa [mean Bṛhaspati]; Uśanas, Bhārgava, and Kavi [mean Śukra];
Vidhuntuda, Tamas, and Rāhu [mean Rāhu]; lagna is stated to be the rising of a zodiacal sign.

359.s:
saptarṣayo marīcyatrimukhāścitraśikhaṇḍinaḥ /
haridaśvavraghmapūṣadyumaṇirmihiro raviḥ //
359.d:
सप्तर्षयो मरीच्यत्रिमुखाश्चित्रशिखण्डिनः /
हरिदश्वव्रघ्मपूषद्युमणिर्मिहिरो रविः //
359.m:
The Seven Sages (saptarṣi), beginning with Marīci and Atri, are the Citraśikhaṇḍins;
Haridaśva, Bradhna, Pūṣan, Dyumaṇi, Mihira, and Ravi [mean the sun].

359.s:
pariveṣastu paridhirupasūryakabhaṇḍale /
kiraṇo 'sramayūkhāṃśugabhastighṛṇidhṛṣṇayaḥ //
:p 266
359.d:
परिवेषस्तु परिधिरुपसूर्यकभण्डले /
किरणो ऽस्रमयूखांशुगभस्तिघृणिधृष्णयः //
:प् 266

359.s:
bhānuḥ karo marīciḥ strīpuṃsayordīdhitiḥ striyāṃ /
syuḥ prabhā rugrucistviḍbhābhāśchavidyutidīptayaḥ //
359.d:
भानुः करो मरीचिः स्त्रीपुंसयोर्दीधितिः स्त्रियां /
स्युः प्रभा रुग्रुचिस्त्विड्भाभाश्छविद्युतिदीप्तयः //
359.m:
bhānu, kara, and marīci in both masculine and feminine, and dīdhiti in the feminine [mean ray of light];
prabhā, ruk, ruci, tviṣ, bhā, bhās, chavi, dyuti, and dīpti [mean lustre];

359.s:
rociḥ śocirubhe klīve prakāśo dyota ātapaḥ /
koṣṇaṃ kavoṣṇaṃ mandoṣṇaṃ kaduṣṇaṃ triṣu tadvati //
359.d:
रोचिः शोचिरुभे क्लीवे प्रकाशो द्योत आतपः /
कोष्णं कवोष्णं मन्दोष्णं कदुष्णं त्रिषु तद्वति //
359.m:
rocis and śocis are both neuter; prakāśa, dyota, and ātapa [mean light or sunshine];
koṣṇa, kavoṣṇa, mandoṣṇa, and kaduṣṇa [mean lukewarm], in three genders when qualifying an object.

359.s:
tirmaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ kharaṃ tadvaddiṣṭo 'nehā ca kālakaḥ /
ghasro dināhanī caiva sāyaṃsandhyā pitṛprasūḥ //
359.d:
तिर्मं तीक्ष्णं खरं तद्वद्दिष्टो ऽनेहा च कालकः /
घस्रो दिनाहनी चैव सायंसन्ध्या पितृप्रसूः //
359.m:
Likewise, tigma, tīkṣṇa, and khara [mean sharp or hot]; diṣṭa, anehā, and kālaka [mean time];
ghasra, dina, and ahan [mean day]; the evening twilight is the mother of the ancestors (pitṛprasū).

359.s:
pratyūṣo 'harmukhaṃ kalyamuṣaḥpratyūṣasī api /
prāhṇāparāhṇamadhyāhṇāstrisandhyamatha śarvarī //
359.d:
प्रत्यूषो ऽहर्मुखं कल्यमुषःप्रत्यूषसी अपि /
प्राह्णापराह्णमध्याह्णास्त्रिसन्ध्यमथ शर्वरी //
359.m: Dawn is *pratyūṣa*, *aharmukha*, *kalya*, and also *uṣas* and *pratyūṣas*. / Morning, afternoon, and midday [are the three divisions of day]; the three junctures of the day [are *trisandhya*]; and night is *śarvarī*,

359.s:
yāmī tamī tamisrā ca jyotsnī candrakayānvitā /
āgāmivartamānāharyuktāyāṃ niśi pakṣiṇī //
359.d:
यामी तमी तमिस्रा च ज्योत्स्नी चन्द्रकयान्विता /
आगामिवर्तमानाहर्युक्तायां निशि पक्षिणी //
359.m: *yāmī*, *tamī*, and *tamisrā*. When accompanied by moonlight it is *jyotsnī*. / A night joined with the preceding and following days is a *pakṣiṇī*.

359.s:
ardharātraniśīthau pradoṣo rajanīmukhaṃ /
sa parvasandhiḥ pratipatpañcadaśyorya dantaram //
359.d:
अर्धरात्रनिशीथौ प्रदोषो रजनीमुखं /
स पर्वसन्धिः प्रतिपत्पञ्चदश्योर्य दन्तरम् //
359.m: Midnight is *ardharātra* and *niśītha*; *pradoṣa* is the beginning of the night. / The juncture of the phases is the interval between the first lunar day and the fifteenth.

359.s:
pakṣāntau pañcadaśyau dve paurṇamāsī tu pūrṇimā /
kalāhīne sānumatiḥ pūrṇe rākā niśākare //
359.d:
पक्षान्तौ पञ्चदश्यौ द्वे पौर्णमासी तु पूर्णिमा /
कलाहीने सानुमतिः पूर्णे राका निशाकरे //
359.m: The ends of the fortnights are two fifteenth days; full moon day is *paurṇamāsī* and *pūrṇimā*. / When deficient by a digit it is *anumati*; when the moon is completely full it is *rākā*.

359.s:
amāvāsyā tvamāvasyā darśaḥ sūryendusaṅgamaḥ /
sā dṛṣṭenduḥ sinīvālī sā naṣṭendukalā kuhūḥ //
359.d:
अमावास्या त्वमावस्या दर्शः सूर्येन्दुसङ्गमः /
सा दृष्टेन्दुः सिनीवाली सा नष्टेन्दुकला कुहूः //
359.m: New moon day is *amāvāsyā*, *amāvasyā*, and *darśa*, the conjunction of the sun and the moon. / When the moon is [still] seen, it is *sinīvālī*; when the digit of the moon has disappeared, it is *kuhū*.

359.s:
saṃvartaḥ pralayaḥ kalpaḥ kṣayaḥ kalpānta ity api /
kaluṣaṃ vṛjinaino 'ghamaṃhoduritaduṣkṛtam //
359.d:
संवर्तः प्रलयः कल्पः क्षयः कल्पान्त इत्य् अपि /
कलुषं वृजिनैनो ऽघमंहोदुरितदुष्कृतम् //
359.m: *Saṃvarta*, *pralaya*, *kalpa*, *kṣaya*, and *kalpānta* [all mean dissolution]. / Sin is *kaluṣa*, *vṛjina*, *enas*, *agha*, *aṃhas*, *durita*, and *duṣkṛta*.

359.s:
syāddharmamastriyāṃ puṇyaśreyasī sukṛtaṃ vṛṣaḥ /
mutprītiḥ pramado harṣaḥ pramodāmodasammadāḥ //
359.d:
स्याद्धर्ममस्त्रियां पुण्यश्रेयसी सुकृतं वृषः /
मुत्प्रीतिः प्रमदो हर्षः प्रमोदामोदसम्मदाः //
359.m: In the non-feminine it is *dharma*, *puṇya*, *śreyas*, *sukṛta*, and *vṛṣa* [for religious merit]. / Joy is *mud*, *prīti*, *pramada*, *harṣa*, *pramoda*, *āmoda*, and *sammada*;

359.s:
syādānandathurānandaḥ śarmaśātasukhāni ca /
śvaḥ śreyasaṃ śivaṃ bhadraṃ kalyāṇaṃ maṅgalaṃ śubham //
359.d:
स्यादानन्दथुरानन्दः शर्मशातसुखानि च /
श्वः श्रेयसं शिवं भद्रं कल्याणं मङ्गलं शुभम् //
359.m: it is [also] *ānandathu* and *ānanda*; while *śarma*, *śāta*, and *sukha* [mean happiness]. / Welfare is *śvaḥśreyasa*, *śiva*, *bhadra*, *kalyāṇa*, *maṅgala*, and *śubha*;

359.s:
bhāvukaṃ bhavikaṃ bhavyaṃ kuśalaṃ kṣemamastriyāṃ /
:p 267
daivaṃ diṣṭaṃ māgadheyaṃ bhāgyaṃ strī niyatirvidhiḥ //
359.d:
भावुकं भविकं भव्यं कुशलं क्षेममस्त्रियां /
:प् 267
दैवं दिष्टं मागधेयं भाग्यं स्त्री नियतिर्विधिः //
359.m:
[also] *bhāvuka*, *bhavika*, *bhavya*, *kuśala*, and *kṣema* in the non-feminine.
[Page 267]
Destiny is *daiva*, *diṣṭa*, *bhāgadheya*, *bhāgya*, and in the feminine *niyati* and *vidhi*.

359.s:
kṣetrajña ātmā puruṣaḥ pradhānaṃ prakṛtiḥ striyāṃ /
heturnā kāraṇaṃ vījaṃ nidānaṃ tvādikāraṇam //
359.d:
क्षेत्रज्ञ आत्मा पुरुषः प्रधानं प्रकृतिः स्त्रियां /
हेतुर्ना कारणं वीजं निदानं त्वादिकारणम् //
359.m: The soul is *kṣetrajña*, *ātman*, and *puruṣa*; primordial matter is *pradhāna* and, in the feminine, *prakṛti*. / Cause is masculine *hetu*, *kāraṇa*, and *bīja*; but the primary cause is *nidāna*.

359.s:
cittantu ceto hṛdayaṃ svāntaṃ hṛnmānasammanaḥ /
buddhirmanīṣā dhiṣaṇā dhīḥ prajñā śemuṣī matiḥ //
359.d:
चित्तन्तु चेतो हृदयं स्वान्तं हृन्मानसम्मनः /
बुद्धिर्मनीषा धिषणा धीः प्रज्ञा शेमुषी मतिः //
359.m: Mind is *citta*, *cetas*, *hṛdaya*, *svānta*, *hṛd*, *mānasa*, and *manas*. / Intellect is *buddhi*, *manīṣā*, *dhiṣaṇā*, *dhī*, *prajñā*, *śemuṣī*, and *mati*;

359.s:
prekṣopalibdhiścitsambitpratipajjñapticetanāḥ /
dhīrdhāraṇāvatī medhā saṅkalpaḥ karma mānasaṃ //
359.d:
प्रेक्षोपलिब्धिश्चित्सम्बित्प्रतिपज्ज्ञप्तिचेतनाः /
धीर्धारणावती मेधा सङ्कल्पः कर्म मानसं //
359.m: [also] *prekṣā*, *upalabdhi*, *cit*, *saṃvid*, *pratipad*, *jñapti*, and *cetanā*. / Intellect endowed with retention is *medhā*; intention is mental action.

359.s:
saṅkhyā vicāraṇā carcā vicikitsā tu saṃśayaḥ /
adhyāhārastarka ūhaḥ samau nirṇayaniś cayau //
359.d:
सङ्ख्या विचारणा चर्चा विचिकित्सा तु संशयः /
अध्याहारस्तर्क ऊहः समौ निर्णयनिश् चयौ //
359.m: Deliberation is *saṅkhyā*, *vicāraṇā*, and *carcā*; doubt is *vicikitsā* and *saṃśaya*. / Conjectural supply is *adhyāhāra*, *tarka*, and *ūha*; *nirṇaya* and *niścaya* are synonymous [for ascertainment].

359.s:
mithyādṛṣṭirnāstikatā bhrāntirmithyāmatirbhramaḥ /
aṅgīkārābhyupagamapratiśravasamādhayaḥ //
359.d:
मिथ्यादृष्टिर्नास्तिकता भ्रान्तिर्मिथ्यामतिर्भ्रमः /
अङ्गीकाराभ्युपगमप्रतिश्रवसमाधयः //
359.m: False view is *nāstikatā*; error is *bhrānti*, *mithyāmati*, and *bhrama*. / *Aṅgīkāra*, *abhyupagama*, *pratiśrava*, and *samādhi* [are words for acceptance].

359.s:
mokṣe dhīrjñānamanyatra vijñānaṃ śilpaśāstrayoḥ /
muktiḥ kaivalyanirvāṇaśreyoniḥśreyasāmṛtaṃ //
359.d:
मोक्षे धीर्ज्ञानमन्यत्र विज्ञानं शिल्पशास्त्रयोः /
मुक्तिः कैवल्यनिर्वाणश्रेयोनिःश्रेयसामृतं //
359.m: Regarding liberation, intellect is called *jñāna*; elsewhere, in crafts and sciences, it is *vijñāna*. / Liberation is *mukti*, *kaivalya*, *nirvāṇa*, *śreyas*, *niḥśreyasa*, and *amṛta*;

359.s:
mokṣo 'pavargo 'thājñānamavidyāhammatiḥ striyāṃ /
vimardotthe parimalo gandhe janamanohare //
359.d:
मोक्षो ऽपवर्गो ऽथाज्ञानमविद्याहम्मतिः स्त्रियां /
विमर्दोत्थे परिमलो गन्धे जनमनोहरे //
359.m: [also] *mokṣa* and *apavarga*. Ignorance is *ajñāna*, *avidyā*, and, in the feminine, *aham-mati*. / A fragrance arising from rubbing that captivates people is *parimala*;

359.s:
āmodaḥ so 'tinirhārī surabhirghrāṇatarpaṇaḥ /
śuklaśubhraśuciśvetaviśadaśvetapāṇḍarāḥ //
359.d:
आमोदः सो ऽतिनिर्हारी सुरभिर्घ्राणतर्पणः /
शुक्लशुभ्रशुचिश्वेतविशदश्वेतपाण्डराः //
359.m: that which is strongly diffusive is *āmoda*; fragrant is *surabhi* and *ghrāṇatarpaṇa*. / White is *śukla*, *śubhra*, *śuci*, *śveta*, *viśada*, *śveta*, and *pāṇḍara*;

359.s:
avadātaḥ sito gauro valakṣo dhavalo 'rjunaḥ /
hariṇaḥ pāṇḍuraḥ pāṇḍurīṣatpāṇḍustu dhūsaraḥ //
359.d:
अवदातः सितो गौरो वलक्षो धवलो ऽर्जुनः /
हरिणः पाण्डुरः पाण्डुरीषत्पाण्डुस्तु धूसरः //
359.m: [also] *avadāta*, *sita*, *gaura*, *valakṣa*, *dhavala*, and *arjuna*. / Greyish-white is *hariṇa*, *pāṇḍura*, and *pāṇḍu*; slightly pale is *dhūsara*.

359.s:
kṛṣṇe nīlāsitaśyāmakālaśyāmalamecakāḥ /
pīto gauro haridrābhaḥ pālāśo harito harit //
359.d:
कृष्णे नीलासितश्यामकालश्यामलमेचकाः /
पीतो गौरो हरिद्राभः पालाशो हरितो हरित् //
359.m: For black: *nīla*, *asita*, *śyāma*, *kāla*, *śyāmala*, and *mecaka*. / Yellow is *pīta*, *gaura*, and *haridrābha*; green is *pālāśa*, *harita*, and *harit*.

359.s:
rohito lohito raktaḥ śoṇaḥ kokanadacchaviḥ /
avyaktarāgastvaruṇaḥ śvetaraktastu pāṭalaḥ //
:p 268
359.d:
रोहितो लोहितो रक्तः शोणः कोकनदच्छविः /
अव्यक्तरागस्त्वरुणः श्वेतरक्तस्तु पाटलः //
:प् 268
359.m:
Red is *rohita*, *lohita*, *rakta*, *śoṇa*, and *kokanadacchavi*. / Of indistinct redness is *aruṇa*; pink is *pāṭala*.
[Page 268]

359.s:
śyāvaḥ syātkapiśo dhūmradhūmalau kṛṣṇalohite /
kaḍāraḥ kapilaḥ piṅgapiśaṅgaukadrupiṅgalau //
359.d:
श्यावः स्यात्कपिशो धूम्रधूमलौ कृष्णलोहिते /
कडारः कपिलः पिङ्गपिशङ्गौकद्रुपिङ्गलौ //
359.m: Dark brown is *śyāva* and *kapiśa*; reddish-black is *dhūmra* and *dhūmala*. / Tawny is *kaḍāra*, *kapila*, *piṅga*, *piśaṅga*, *kadru*, and *piṅgala*.

359.s:
citraṃ kirmīrakalmāṣaśavalaitātha karvure /
vyāhara uktirlapitamapabhraṃśo 'paśabdakaḥ //
359.d:
चित्रं किर्मीरकल्माषशवलैताथ कर्वुरे /
व्याहर उक्तिर्लपितमपभ्रंशो ऽपशब्दकः //
359.m: Variegated is *citra*, *kirmīra*, *kalmāṣa*, *śabala*, and *karbura*. / Speech is *vyāhāra*, *ukti*, and *lapita*; corrupt speech is *apabhraṃśa* and *apaśabda*.

359.s:
tiṅsuvantacayo kāvyaṃ kriyā vā kārakānvitā /
itihāsaḥ purāvṛttaṃ purāṇaṃ pañcalakṣaṇaṃ //
359.d:
तिङ्सुवन्तचयो काव्यं क्रिया वा कारकान्विता /
इतिहासः पुरावृत्तं पुराणं पञ्चलक्षणं //
359.m: Poetry is an assemblage of words ending in verbal and nominal inflections, or an action connected with case relations. / History is an ancient event; a Purāṇa has five characteristics.

359.s:
ākhyāyikopalabdhārthā prabandhaḥ kalpanā kathā /
samāhāraḥ saṃgrahastu pravahlikā prahelikā //
359.d:
आख्यायिकोपलब्धार्था प्रबन्धः कल्पना कथा /
समाहारः संग्रहस्तु प्रवह्लिका प्रहेलिका //
359.m: An *ākhyāyikā* has a historical plot; a literary composition of pure invention is a *kathā*. / A summary is *samāhāra* and *saṃgraha*; an enigma is *pravahlikā* and *prahelikā*.

359.s:
samasyā tu samāsārthā smṛtistu dharmasaṃhitā /
ākhyāhve cābhidhānañca vārtā vṛttānta īritaḥ //
359.d:
समस्या तु समासार्था स्मृतिस्तु धर्मसंहिता /
आख्याह्वे चाभिधानञ्च वार्ता वृत्तान्त ईरितः //
359.m: A *samasyā* is a condensed meaning; the *smṛti* is a code of sacred law. / A name is *ākhyā*, *āhva*, and *abhidhāna*; news is said to be *vārtā* and *vṛttānta*.

359.s:
