hūtirākāraṇāhvānamupanyāsastu vāṅmukhaṃ /
vivādo vyavahāraḥ syāt prativākyottare same //
359.d:
हूतिराकारणाह्वानमुपन्यासस्तु वाङ्मुखं /
विवादो व्यवहारः स्यात् प्रतिवाक्योत्तरे समे //
359.m: Calling is *hūti*, *ākāraṇā*, and *āhvāna*; an introductory remark is *upanyāsa*. / Dispute is *vivāda* and *vyavahāra*; reply and answer are synonymous.

359.s:
upoddhāta udāhāro hy artha mithyābhisaṃśanam /
abhiśāpo yaśaḥ kīrtiḥ praśnaḥ pṛcchānuyogakaḥ //
359.d:
उपोद्धात उदाहारो ह्य् अर्थ मिथ्याभिसंशनम् /
अभिशापो यशः कीर्तिः प्रश्नः पृच्छानुयोगकः //
359.m: An introductory explanation is *upoddhāta* and *udāhāra*; a false accusation is *abhiśāpa*. / Fame is *yaśas* and *kīrti*; inquiry is *praśna*, *pṛcchā*, and *anuyoga*.

359.s:
āmreḍitaṃ dvistriruktaṃ kutsāninde ca garhaṇe /
syādābhāṣaṇamālāpaḥ pralāpo 'narthakaṃ vacaḥ //
359.d:
आम्रेडितं द्विस्त्रिरुक्तं कुत्सानिन्दे च गर्हणे /
स्यादाभाषणमालापः प्रलापो ऽनर्थकं वचः //
359.m: A word repeated twice or thrice is *āmreḍita*; censure and blame are *kutsā*, *nindā*, and *garhaṇā*. / Addressing someone is *ābhāṣaṇa* and *ālāpa*; meaningless speech is *pralāpa*.

359.s:
anulāpo muhurbhāṣā volāpaḥ paridevanaṃ /
vipralāpo virodhoktiḥ saṃlāpo bhāṣaṇaṃ mithaḥ //
359.d:
अनुलापो मुहुर्भाषा वोलापः परिदेवनं /
विप्रलापो विरोधोक्तिः संलापो भाषणं मिथः //
359.m: Repeated speech is *anulāpa*; lamentation is *vilāpa*. / Contradictory speech is *vipralāpa*; conversation is mutual speech.

359.s:
supralāpaḥ suvacanamapalāpastu nihnavaḥ /
uṣatī vāgakalyāṇī saṅgataṃ hṛdayaṅgamaṃ //
359.d:
सुप्रलापः सुवचनमपलापस्तु निह्नवः /
उषती वागकल्याणी सङ्गतं हृदयङ्गमं //
359.m: Well-spoken utterance is *supralāpa*; concealment is *apalāpa*. / Inauspicious speech is *uṣatī*; that which touches the heart is *saṅgata*.

359_2.m: Exceedingly sweet speech is soothing; disconnected speech is meaningless.

0-r2.m:
[Verse 66a]
Harsh, vulgar, and indecent speech is *grāmya*; pleasing and truthful speech is *sūnṛta*.
[Verse 66b]
True is *satya*, *tathya*, *ṛta*, and *samyak*. Sound is *nāda*, *nisvāna*, and *nisvana*;
[Verse 67a]
[Page 269]
[also] *ārava*, *rāva*, *saṃrāva*, and *virāva*. Rustling sound is *marmara*;
[Verse 67b]
[namely] the sound of garments and leaves; the sound of ornaments is *śiñjita*.
[Verse 68a]
The sound of a lute is nikvaṇa and kvāṇa; the cry of animals is vāśita and ruta.
.068ācd
Kolāhala and kalakala [are synonymous]; gīta and gāna—these are equivalent.
.069āab
Pratiśrut is feminine for echo (pratidhvāna); one who sings from the strings and throat [is a nisādaka].
.069ācd
Kākalī, however, is a soft, subtle tone, a sweet, indistinct sound;
.070āab
Kala; mantra is deep; tāra is very high-pitched; these three can be in all three genders. // 70ā
.070ācd
Music possessed of rhythm is ekatāla; a vīṇā is a vallakī;
.071āab
It is a vipañcī, but when strung with seven strings, it is a parivādinī.
.071ācd
Stringed (tata) instruments are the lute and the like; covered with hide (ānaddha) are the drum (muraja) and the like;
.072āab
Wind instruments (śuṣira) are the flute and the like; solid (ghana) are bell-metal cymbals and the like.
.072ācd
Musical instruments are of these four kinds, termed vāditra and ātodya.

कृपा दया चानुकम्पाप्यनुक्रोशो ऽप्यथो हसः //
.078आच्द्/
:प् 270
हासो हास्यञ्च वीभत्सं विकृतं त्रिष्विदं द्वयं /
.066बब्/
विस्मयो ऽद्भुतमाश् चर्यं चित्रमप्यथ भैरवं //
.066ब्च्द्/
0-r2.m:
.073āab
Mṛdaṅgas and murajas have three varieties: aṅkya, āliṅgya, and ūrdhvaka.
.073ācd
The drum of victory is a ṭakkā; for a kettle-drum: bherī, ānaka, and dundubhi.
.074āab
Ānaka and paṭaha [are synonyms]; varieties include the jharjharī, ḍiṇḍima, and others.
.074ācd
Mardala and paṇava are equivalent; the measure of musical action is tāla.
.075āab
Laya is uniformity of tempo; tāṇḍava, nāṭya, lāsya, and nartana [are varieties of dance].
.075ācd
Tauryatrika is the triad consisting of dance, song, and instrumental music: this triad is dramatic performance (nāṭya).
.076āab
A king is bhaṭṭāraka and deva; an anointed queen is also devī.
.076ācd
Erotic (śṛṅgāra), heroic (vīra), pathetic (karuṇa), wondrous (adbhuta), comic (hāsya), terrible (bhayānaka),
.077āab
Odious (vībhatsa), and furious (raudra) are the aesthetic sentiments (rasa); the erotic is pure and radiant;
.077ācd
The heroic increases energy; kāruṇya, karuṇā, and ghṛṇā [are compassion];
.078āab
Kṛpā, dayā, anukampā, and anukrośa [also denote compassion]; now, laughter is hasa;
.078ācd
p. 270
Hāsa and hāsya [are synonyms]; vībhatsa and vikṛta: these two take all three genders;
.066Bab
Vismaya, adbhuta, āścarya, and citra [denote wonder]; then, bhairava,
.066Bcd

0-r2.s:
dāruṇaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ bhīṣmaṃ ghoraṃ bhīmaṃbhayānakaṃ /
.067Bab/
bhayaṅkaraṃ pratibhayaṃ raudrantūgramamī triṣu //
.067Bcd/
caturdaśa daratrāsau bhītirbhīḥ sādhvasambhayaṃ /
.068Bab/
vikāro mānaso bhāvo 'nubhāvo bhāvabodhanaḥ //68B//
.068Bcd/
garvo 'bhimāno 'haṅkāro mānaścittasamunnatiḥ /
.069Bab/
anādaraḥ paribhavaḥ paribhāvastiraskriyā //69B//
.069Bcd/
vrīḍā lajjā trapā hrīḥ syādabhidhyānaṃ dhane spṛhā /
.070Bab/
kautūhalaṃ kautukañca kutukañca kutūhalaṃ //70B//
.070Bcd/
stroṇāṃ vilāsavivvokavibhramā lalitantathā /
.071Bab/
helā līletyamī hāvāḥ kriyāḥ śṛṅgārabhāvajāḥ //
.071Bcd/
dravakeliparīhāsāḥ krīḍā līlā ca kūrdanaṃ /
.072Bab/
syādāchuritakaṃ hāsaḥ sotprāsaḥ samanāksmitaṃ //
.072Bcd/
adhobhuvanapātālaṃ chidraṃ śvabhraṃ vapā śuṣiḥ /
.073Bab/
gartāvaṭau bhuvi śvebhre tamiśrantimiraṃ tamaḥ //
0-r2.d:
दारुणं भीषणं भीष्मं घोरं भीमंभयानकं /
.067बब्/
भयङ्करं प्रतिभयं रौद्रन्तूग्रममी त्रिषु //
.067ब्च्द्/
चतुर्दश दरत्रासौ भीतिर्भीः साध्वसम्भयं /
.068बब्/
विकारो मानसो भावो ऽनुभावो भावबोधनः //68ब्//
.068ब्च्द्/
गर्वो ऽभिमानो ऽहङ्कारो मानश्चित्तसमुन्नतिः /
.069बब्/
अनादरः परिभवः परिभावस्तिरस्क्रिया //69ब्//
.069ब्च्द्/
व्रीडा लज्जा त्रपा ह्रीः स्यादभिध्यानं धने स्पृहा /
.070बब्/
कौतूहलं कौतुकञ्च कुतुकञ्च कुतूहलं //70ब्//
.070ब्च्द्/
स्त्रोणां विलासविव्वोकविभ्रमा ललितन्तथा /
.071बब्/
हेला लीलेत्यमी हावाः क्रियाः शृङ्गारभावजाः //
.071ब्च्द्/
द्रवकेलिपरीहासाः क्रीडा लीला च कूर्दनं /
.072बब्/
स्यादाछुरितकं हासः सोत्प्रासः समनाक्स्मितं //
.072ब्च्द्/
अधोभुवनपातालं छिद्रं श्वभ्रं वपा शुषिः /
.073बब्/
गर्तावटौ भुवि श्वेभ्रे तमिश्रन्तिमिरं तमः //
0-r2.m:
Dāruṇa, bhīṣaṇa, bhīṣma, ghora, bhīma, bhayānaka,
.067Bab
Bhayaṅkara, pratibhaya, raudra, and ugra—these take all three genders.
.067Bcd
Fourteen [synonyms for fear]: dara, trāsa, bhīti, bhī, sādhvasa, bhaya;
.068Bab
A mental modification is a state of feeling (bhāva); that which indicates an emotional state is an external manifestation (anubhāva). // 68B
.068Bcd
Garva, abhimāna, ahaṅkāra, māna, and cittasamunnati [denote pride];
.069Bab
Anādara, paribhava, paribhāva, and tiraskriyā [denote disrespect]. // 69B
.069Bcd
Vrīḍā, lajjā, trapā, and hrī denote shame; abhidhyāna is longing for wealth;
[Verse 70b]
Curiosity and eagerness are *kautūhala*, *kautuka*, *kutuka*, and *kutūhala*.
[Verse 70c]
Women's amorous play, feigned anger, confusion, and gracefulness,
[Verse 71a]
as well as wantonness and sport—these gestures and bodily movements arise from the erotic sentiment.
[Verse 71b]
Sport, play, and jesting are *drava*, *keli*, *parīhāsa*, *krīḍā*, *līlā*, and *kūrdana*.
[Verse 72a]
A subtle laugh is *āchuritaka*; sarcastic laughter is accompanied by a slight smile.
[Verse 72b]
The lower world is *adhobhuvana* and *pātāla*; a hole or cavity is *chidra*, *śvabhra*, *vapā*, and *śuṣi*.
[Verse 73a]
A pit in the earth is *garta* and *avaṭa*; darkness is *tamiśra*, *timira*, and *tamas*.

0-r2.s:
.073Bcd/
sarpaḥ pṛdākurbhujago dandaśūko vileśayaḥ /
.074Bab/
viṣaṃ kṣveḍaś ca garalaṃ nirayo durgatiḥ striyāṃ //
.074Bcd/
payaḥ kīlālamamṛtamudakaṃ bhuvanaṃ vanaṃ /
.075Bab/
bhaṅgastaraṅga ūrmirvā kallolollolakau ca tau //75B//
.075Bcd/
pṛṣantivindupṛṣatāḥ kūlaṃ rodhaś ca tīrakaṃ /
.076Bab/
toyotthitaṃ tat pulinaṃ jambālaṃ paṅkakardamau //
.076Bcd/
jalocchāsāḥ parīvāhāḥ kūpakāstu vidārakāḥ /
.077Bab/
:p 271
ātārastarapaṇyaṃ syāddroṇī kāṣṭhāmbuvāhinī //
.077Bcd/
kaluṣaścāvilo 'cchastu prasanno 'tha gabhīrakaṃ /
.078Bab/
agādhaṃ dāsakaivartau śambūkā jalaśuktayaḥ //
.078Bcd/
0-r2.d:
.073ब्च्द्/
सर्पः पृदाकुर्भुजगो दन्दशूको विलेशयः /
.074बब्/
विषं क्ष्वेडश् च गरलं निरयो दुर्गतिः स्त्रियां //
.074ब्च्द्/
पयः कीलालममृतमुदकं भुवनं वनं /
.075बब्/
भङ्गस्तरङ्ग ऊर्मिर्वा कल्लोलोल्लोलकौ च तौ //75ब्//
.075ब्च्द्/
पृषन्तिविन्दुपृषताः कूलं रोधश् च तीरकं /
.076बब्/
तोयोत्थितं तत् पुलिनं जम्बालं पङ्ककर्दमौ //
.076ब्च्द्/
जलोच्छासाः परीवाहाः कूपकास्तु विदारकाः /
.077बब्/
:प् 271
आतारस्तरपण्यं स्याद्द्रोणी काष्ठाम्बुवाहिनी //
.077ब्च्द्/
कलुषश्चाविलो ऽच्छस्तु प्रसन्नो ऽथ गभीरकं /
.078बब्/
अगाधं दासकैवर्तौ शम्बूका जलशुक्तयः //
.078ब्च्द्/
0-r2.m:
[Verse 73b]
A serpent is *sarpa*, *pṛdāku*, *bhujaga*, *dandaśūka*, and *vileśaya*.
.074Bab
Viṣa, kṣveḍa, and garala [mean "poison"]; niraya and durgati [mean "hell"], in the feminine.
.074Bcd
Payaḥ, kīlāla, amṛta, udaka, bhuvana, [and] vana [mean "water"];
.075Bab
bhaṅga, taraṅga, or ūrmi [mean "wave"]; and kallola and ullolaka [mean a large wave]. //75B
.075Bcd
Pṛṣanti, bindu, [and] pṛṣat [mean "drop"]; kūla, rodhaḥ, and tīraka [mean "bank"];
.076Bab
risen from the water, that is a pulina ["sandbank"]; jambāla, paṅka, and kardama [mean "mud"];
.076Bcd
jalocchāsas are parīvāhas ["overflows"]; kūpakas are vidārakas ["trenches"];
.077Bab
:p 271
ātāra is tarapaṇya ["ferry-toll"]; droṇī is a wooden canoe.
.077Bcd
Kaluṣa and āvila [mean "turbid"]; accha is prasanna ["clear"]; then gabhīraka [means "deep"];
.078Bab
agādha [means "unfathomable"]; dāsa and kaivarta [mean "fisherman"]; śambūkas are freshwater shells.
.078Bcd

359-r2.s:
saugandhikantu kahlāraṃ nīlamindīvaraṃ kajaṃ /
syādutpalaṃ kuvalayaṃ site kumudakairave //
359-r2.d:
सौगन्धिकन्तु कह्लारं नीलमिन्दीवरं कजं /
स्यादुत्पलं कुवलयं सिते कुमुदकैरवे //
359-r2.m:
Saugandhika is kahlāra [white water-lily]; blue [water-lily] is indīvara; the water-born
utpala is kuvalaya; kumuda and kairava are white [water-lilies].

359-r2.s:
śālūkameṣāṃ kandaḥ syāt padmaṃ tāmarasaṅkajaṃ /
nīlotpalaṃ kuvalayaṃ raktaṃ kokanadaṃ smṛtam //
359-r2.d:
शालूकमेषां कन्दः स्यात् पद्मं तामरसङ्कजं /
नीलोत्पलं कुवलयं रक्तं कोकनदं स्मृतम् //
359-r2.m:
Śālūka is their bulbous root; padma, tāmarasa, and kaja [mean lotus];
nīlotpala is kuvalaya; kokanada is known as the red [lotus].

359-r2.s:
karahāṭaḥ śiphā kandaṃ kiñjalkaḥ keśaro 'striyāṃ /
khaniḥ striyāmākaraḥ syāt pādāḥ pratyantaparvatāḥ //
359-r2.d:
करहाटः शिफा कन्दं किञ्जल्कः केशरो ऽस्त्रियां /
खनिः स्त्रियामाकरः स्यात् पादाः प्रत्यन्तपर्वताः //
359-r2.m:
Karahāṭa, śiphā, and kanda [mean root-stalk]; kiñjalka is keśara ["filament"], not feminine;
khani, in the feminine, is ākara ["mine"]; pādas are the adjacent hills;

359-r2.s:
upatyakādrerāsannā bhūmirūrdhvamadhityakā /
svargapātālavargādyā uktā nānārthakān śṛṇu //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe svargapātālādivargā
nāmonaṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha ṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
avyayavargāḥ
359-r2.d:
उपत्यकाद्रेरासन्ना भूमिरूर्ध्वमधित्यका /
स्वर्गपातालवर्गाद्या उक्ता नानार्थकान् शृणु //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे स्वर्गपातालादिवर्गा
नामोनषष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ षष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
अव्ययवर्गाः
359-r2.m:
upatyakā is the land near a mountain; above [it] is adhityakā ["tableland"].
The sections on heaven, netherworld, and so forth have been told; now hear the homonyms.
:e Thus ends the three hundred and fifty-ninth chapter in the Mahāpurāṇa of Agni, entitled "The Sections on Heaven, the Netherworld, and so forth."
:ś Now the three hundred and sixtieth chapter.
The Group of Indeclinables.

360.s:
agnir uvāca
āṅīṣadarthe 'bhivyāptau sīmārthe dhātuyogaje /
ā pragṛhyaḥ smṛtau vākye 'pyāstu syāt kopapīḍyoḥ //
360.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
आङीषदर्थे ऽभिव्याप्तौ सीमार्थे धातुयोगजे /
आ प्रगृह्यः स्मृतौ वाक्ये ऽप्यास्तु स्यात् कोपपीड्योः //

360.s:
pāpakutseṣadarthe ku dhigjugupsananindayoḥ /
cānvācayasamāhāretaretarasamuccaye //
:p 272
360.d:
पापकुत्सेषदर्थे कु धिग्जुगुप्सननिन्दयोः /
चान्वाचयसमाहारेतरेतरसमुच्चये //
:प् 272

360.s:
svastyāśīḥ kṣemapuṇyādau prakarṣe laṅghane 'pyati /
svitpraśne ca vitarke ca tu syādbhede 'vadhāraṇe //
360.d:
स्वस्त्याशीः क्षेमपुण्यादौ प्रकर्षे लङ्घने ऽप्यति /
स्वित्प्रश्ने च वितर्के च तु स्याद्भेदे ऽवधारणे //
360.m:
"Svasti" is in blessing, welfare, merit, and the like; "ati" is in excellence and also transgression;
"svit" is in question and deliberation; "tu" is in distinction and determination.

360.s:
sakṛtsahaikavāre syādārāddūrasamīpayoḥ /
pratīcyāṃ carame paścādutāpyarthavikalpayoḥ //
360.d:
सकृत्सहैकवारे स्यादाराद्दूरसमीपयोः /
प्रतीच्यां चरमे पश्चादुताप्यर्थविकल्पयोः //
360.m:
"Sakṛt" is in [the sense of] "together" and "once"; "ārāt" is in "distant" and "near";
"paścāt" is in "western" and "subsequent"; "uta" is also in the sense of and alternative.

360.s:
punaḥsadārthayoḥ śaśvat sākṣāt pratyakṣatulyayoḥ /
khedānukampāsantoṣavismayāmantraṇe vata //
360.d:
पुनःसदार्थयोः शश्वत् साक्षात् प्रत्यक्षतुल्ययोः /
खेदानुकम्पासन्तोषविस्मयामन्त्रणे वत //
360.m:
"Śaśvat" is in the senses of "again" and "always"; "sākṣāt" is in [the sense of] direct perception and equal;
"vata" is in weariness, pity, contentment, astonishment, and invocation.

360.s:
hanta harṣe 'nukampāyāṃ vākyārambhaviṣādayoḥ /
prati pratinidhau vīpsālakṣaṇādau prayogataḥ //
360.d:
हन्त हर्षे ऽनुकम्पायां वाक्यारम्भविषादयोः /
प्रति प्रतिनिधौ वीप्सालक्षणादौ प्रयोगतः //
360.m:
"Hanta" is in joy, pity, the commencement of a sentence, and dejection;
"prati" is used in [the sense of] a substitute, repetition, characteristic mark, and the like.

360.s:
iti hetau prakaraṇe prakāśādisamāptiṣu /
prācyāṃ purastāt prathame purārthe 'grata ity api //
360.d:
इति हेतौ प्रकरणे प्रकाशादिसमाप्तिषु /
प्राच्यां पुरस्तात् प्रथमे पुरार्थे ऽग्रत इत्य् अपि //
360.m:
"Iti" is in cause, context, manifestation, and completion;
"purastāt" and "agrataḥ" are also in the east, in the first, and in the sense of formerly.

360.s:
yāvattāvacca sākalye 'vadhau māne 'vadhāraṇe /
maṅgalānantarārambhapraśnakārtsneṣv athotha ca //
360.d:
यावत्तावच्च साकल्ये ऽवधौ माने ऽवधारणे /
मङ्गलानन्तरारम्भप्रश्नकार्त्स्नेष्व् अथोथ च //
360.m:
"Yāvat" and "tāvat" are in completeness, limit, measure, and determination;
"atha" and "uta" are in auspiciousness, subsequence, beginning, question, and entirety.

360.s:
vṛthā nirarthakāvidhyornānānekobhayārthayoḥ /
nu pṛcchāyāṃ vikalpe ca paścātsādṛśyayoranu //
360.d:
वृथा निरर्थकाविध्योर्नानानेकोभयार्थयोः /
नु पृच्छायां विकल्पे च पश्चात्सादृश्ययोरनु //
360.m:
"Vṛthā" is in uselessness and impropriety; "nānā" is in the senses of manifold and both;
"nu" is in inquiry and deliberation; "anu" is in subsequence and resemblance.

360.s:
praśnāvadhāraṇānujñānunayāmantraṇe nanu /
garhāsamuccayapraśnaśaṅkāsambhāvanāsv api //
360.d:
प्रश्नावधारणानुज्ञानुनयामन्त्रणे ननु /
गर्हासमुच्चयप्रश्नशङ्कासम्भावनास्व् अपि //
360.m:
"Nanu" is in question, determination, permission, conciliation, and invocation,
and also in reproach, accumulation, question, doubt, and supposition.

360.s:
upamāyāṃ vikalpe vā sāmitvardhe jugupsite /
amā saha samīpe ca kaṃ vāriṇi ca mūrdhani //
360.d:
उपमायां विकल्पे वा सामित्वर्धे जुगुप्सिते /
अमा सह समीपे च कं वारिणि च मूर्धनि //
360.m:
"Vā" is in comparison and alternative; "sāmi" is in "half" and "despised";
"amā" is in "together" and "near"; and "kam" is in water and on the head.

360.s:
ivetthamarthayorevaṃ nūnaṃ tarke 'rthaniś caye /
tūṣṇīmarthe sukhe joṣaṃ kimpṛcchāyāṃ jugupsane //
360.d:
इवेत्थमर्थयोरेवं नूनं तर्के ऽर्थनिश् चये /
तूष्णीमर्थे सुखे जोषं किम्पृच्छायां जुगुप्सने //
360.m:
"Iva" and "evam" are in the sense of "thus"; "nūnam" is in conjecture and certainty of meaning;
"joṣam" is in the sense of "silently" and in "happily"; "kim" is in inquiry and reproach.

360.s:
nāma prākāśyasambhāvyakrodhopagamakutsane /
alaṃ bhūṣaṇaparyāptiśaktivāraṇavācakam //
:p 273
360.d:
नाम प्राकाश्यसम्भाव्यक्रोधोपगमकुत्सने /
अलं भूषणपर्याप्तिशक्तिवारणवाचकम् //
:प् 273

360.s:
hūṃ vitarke paripraśne samayāntikamadhyayoḥ /
punaraprathame bhede nirniś cayaniṣedhayoḥ //
360.d:
हूं वितर्के परिप्रश्ने समयान्तिकमध्ययोः /
पुनरप्रथमे भेदे निर्निश् चयनिषेधयोः //
360.m:
"Hūm" is in conjecture and interrogation; "samayā" is in "near" and "middle";
"punar" is in the non-initial, and in difference; "nir" is in certainty and negation.

360.s:
syātprabandhe cirātīte nikaṭāgāmike purā /
uraryurī corarī ca vistāre 'ṅgīkṛte trayam //
360.d:
स्यात्प्रबन्धे चिरातीते निकटागामिके पुरा /
उरर्युरी चोररी च विस्तारे ऽङ्गीकृते त्रयम् //
360.m:
"Purā" is in uninterrupted continuance, the distant past, and the near future;
"urari", "urī", and "orarī" are the triad in expansion and assent.

360.s:
svarge pare ca loke svarvārtāsambhāvayoḥ kila /
niṣedhavākyālaṅkāre jijñāsāvasare(1) khalu //
360.d:
स्वर्गे परे च लोके स्वर्वार्तासम्भावयोः किल /
निषेधवाक्यालङ्कारे जिज्ञासावसरे(1) खलु //
360.m:
"Svar" is in heaven and the other world; "kila" is in report and probability;
"khalu" is in prohibition, sentence ornament, desire to know, and an appropriate occasion.

360.s:
samīpobhayataḥśīghrasākalyābhimukhe 'bhitaḥ /
nāmaprakāśayoḥ prādurmitho 'nyonyaṃ rahasyapi //
360.d:
समीपोभयतःशीघ्रसाकल्याभिमुखे ऽभितः /
नामप्रकाशयोः प्रादुर्मिथो ऽन्योन्यं रहस्यपि //
360.m:
"Abhitaḥ" is in "near", "on both sides", "quickly", "entirely", and "facing";
"prādur" is in manifestation and light; "mithaḥ" and "anyonya" are also in secret.

360.s:
tiro 'ntardhau tiryagarthe hā viṣādaśugartiṣu /
ahahetyadbhute khede hi hetāvavadhāraṇe //
360.d:
तिरो ऽन्तर्धौ तिर्यगर्थे हा विषादशुगर्तिषु /
अहहेत्यद्भुते खेदे हि हेताववधारणे //
360.m:
"Tiras" is in concealment and crooked direction; "hā" is in dejection, grief, and pain;
"ahaha" is in wonder and weariness; "hi" is in cause and determination.

360.s:
cirāya cirarātrāya cirasyādyāścirārthakāḥ /
muhuḥ punaḥ punaḥ śaśvadabhīkṣṇamasakṛt samāḥ //
360.d:
चिराय चिररात्राय चिरस्याद्याश्चिरार्थकाः /
मुहुः पुनः पुनः शश्वदभीक्ष्णमसकृत् समाः //
360.m:
"Cirāya", "cirarātrāya", "cirasya", and others mean "for a long time";
"muhuḥ", "punaḥ punaḥ", "śaśvat", "abhīkṣṇam", and "asakṛt" are equivalent.

360.s:
srāgjhaṭityañcasāhnāya sapadi drāṅmaṅkhu ca drute /
balavat suṣṭhu kimuta vikalpe kiṃ kimūta ca //
360.d:
स्राग्झटित्यञ्चसाह्नाय सपदि द्राङ्मङ्खु च द्रुते /
बलवत् सुष्ठु किमुत विकल्पे किं किमूत च //
360.m:
"Srāk", "jhaṭiti", "añjasā", "ahnāya", "sapadi", "drāk", and "maṅkhu" mean "swiftly";
"balavat" and "suṣṭhu" [mean "exceedingly"]; "kimuta" is in alternative, and also "kiṃ" and "kimūta".

360.s:
tu hi ca sma ha vai pādapūraṇe pūjanepyati /
divāhnītyatha doṣā ca naktañca rajanāviti //
360.d:
तु हि च स्म ह वै पादपूरणे पूजनेप्यति /
दिवाह्नीत्यथ दोषा च नक्तञ्च रजनाविति //
360.m:
"Tu", "hi", "ca", "sma", "ha", and "vai" are used to fill out a meter, and also in honorific sense;
"divā" is by day; then "doṣā" and "naktam" mean at night.

360.s:
tiryagarthe sāci tiro 'pyatha sambodhanārthakāḥ /
syuḥ pyāṭpāḍṅga he hai bhoḥ samayā nikaṣā hiruk //
360.d:
तिर्यगर्थे साचि तिरो ऽप्यथ सम्बोधनार्थकाः /
स्युः प्याट्पाड्ङ्ग हे है भोः समया निकषा हिरुक् //
360.m:
"Sāci" and "tiras" are in crooked direction; then expressing invocation
would be "pyāṭ", "pāṭ", "aṅga", "he", "hai", and "bhoḥ"; "samayā", "nikaṣā", and "hiruk" [mean "near" and "without"].

360.s:
atarkite tu sahasā syāt puraḥ purato 'grataḥ /
svāhā devahavirdāne śrauṣaṭ vauṣaṭ vaṣaṭ svadhā //
360.d:
अतर्किते तु सहसा स्यात् पुरः पुरतो ऽग्रतः /
स्वाहा देवहविर्दाने श्रौषट् वौषट् वषट् स्वधा //
360.m:
In unexpectedness is "sahasā"; "puraḥ", "purataḥ", and "agrataḥ" [mean "in front"];
"svāhā" is in offering oblations to gods; "śrauṣaṭ", "vauṣaṭ", "vaṣaṭ", and "svadhā" [are sacrificial calls].

360.s:
kiñcidīṣanmanāgalpe pretyāmutra bhavāntare /
:n
1 jijñāsānunaya iti ña..
:p 274
yathā tathā caiva sāmye aho ho iti vismaye //
360.d:
किञ्चिदीषन्मनागल्पे प्रेत्यामुत्र भवान्तरे /
:न्
1 जिज्ञासानुनय इति ञ..
:प् 274
यथा तथा चैव साम्ये अहो हो इति विस्मये //
360.m:
"Kiñcit", "īṣat", and "manāk" are in smallness; "pretya" and "amutra" mean in another life;
:n
1. "Jijñāsānunaye" in other manuscripts.
:p 274
"yathā", "tathā", and "eva" are in similarity; "aho" and "ho" are in astonishment.

360.s:
maune tu tūṣṇīṃ tūṣṇīkaṃ sadyaḥ sapadi tatkṣaṇe /
diṣṭyā śamupayoṣañcetyānande 'thāntare 'ntarā //
360.d:
मौने तु तूष्णीं तूष्णीकं सद्यः सपदि तत्क्षणे /
दिष्ट्या शमुपयोषञ्चेत्यानन्दे ऽथान्तरे ऽन्तरा //
360.m:
In silence are "tūṣṇīm" and "tūṣṇīkam"; "sadyaḥ", "sapadi", and "tatkṣaṇe" [mean "immediately"];
"diṣṭyā", "śam", "upa", and "yoṣam" are in joy; then in between are "antare", "antarā",

360.s:
antareṇa ca madhye syuḥ prasahya tu haṭārthakam /
yukte dve sāmprataṃ sthāne 'bhīkṣṇaṃ śasvadanārate //
360.d:
अन्तरेण च मध्ये स्युः प्रसह्य तु हटार्थकम् /
युक्ते द्वे साम्प्रतं स्थाने ऽभीक्ष्णं शस्वदनारते //
360.m:
and "antareṇa", which are in the middle; "prasahya" has the sense of "by force";
the two, "sāmpratam" and "sthāne", mean fit; "abhīkṣṇam" and "śaśvat" mean uninterruptedly;

360.s:
abhāve nahyano nāpi māsma mālañca vāraṇe /
pakṣāntare cedyadi ca tattve tv addhāñjasā dvayam //
360.d:
अभावे नह्यनो नापि मास्म मालञ्च वारणे /
पक्षान्तरे चेद्यदि च तत्त्वे त्व् अद्धाञ्जसा द्वयम् //
360.m:
in absence are "nahi", "no", and "nāpi"; "māsma", "mā", and "alam" are in prohibition;
"ced" and "yadi" are in alternative; in truth are the two: "addhā" and "añjasā".

360.s:
prākāśye prādurāviḥ syādomevaṃ paramaṃ mate /
samantatastu paritaḥ sarvato viśvagityapi //
360.d:
प्राकाश्ये प्रादुराविः स्यादोमेवं परमं मते /
समन्ततस्तु परितः सर्वतो विश्वगित्यपि //
360.m:
In the sense of manifestation [there are] *prāduḥ* and *āviḥ*; *om*, *evam*, and *paramam* [are used] for assent;
and *samantatas*, *paritas*, *sarvatas*, and *viśvak* [denote] 'all around'.

360.s:
akāmānumatau kāmamasūyopagame 'stu ca /
nanu ca syādvirodhoktau kaccit kāmapravedane //
360.d:
अकामानुमतौ काममसूयोपगमे ऽस्तु च /
ननु च स्याद्विरोधोक्तौ कच्चित् कामप्रवेदने //
360.m:
*Kāmam* expresses reluctant assent; *astu* expresses consent despite disapproval;
*nanu* is used in contradictory statement; *kaccit* in inquiring after desires.

360.s:
niḥṣamaṃ duḥṣamaṃ garhye yathāsvantu yathāyathaṃ /
mṛṣā mithyā ca vitathe yathārthantu yathātathaṃ //
360.d:
निःषमं दुःषमं गर्ह्ये यथास्वन्तु यथायथं /
मृषा मिथ्या च वितथे यथार्थन्तु यथातथं //
360.m:
*Niḥṣamam* and *duḥṣamam* mean reprehensible; *yathāsvam* means 'properly';
*mṛṣā* and *mithyā* mean false; *yathārtham* means 'truthfully'.

360.s:
syurevantu punarvaivetyavadhāraṇavācakāḥ /
prāgatītārthakaṃ nūnamavaśyaṃ niś caye dvayaṃ //
360.d:
स्युरेवन्तु पुनर्वैवेत्यवधारणवाचकाः /
प्रागतीतार्थकं नूनमवश्यं निश् चये द्वयं //
360.m:
*Eva*, *tu*, *punar*, *vai*, and *vā* are restrictive particles;
*prāk* signifies past time; the pair *nūnam* and *avaśyam* [denote] certainty.

360.s:
saṃvadvarṣe 'vare tvarvāgāmevaṃ svayamātmanā /
alpe nīcair mahatyuccaiḥ prāyobhūmny adrute śanaiḥ //
360.d:
संवद्वर्षे ऽवरे त्वर्वागामेवं स्वयमात्मना /
अल्पे नीचैर् महत्युच्चैः प्रायोभूम्न्य् अद्रुते शनैः //
360.m:
*Saṃvat* [is used] for a year; *arvāk* for inferior; *ām* and *evam* [mean] 'yes'; *svayam* means 'by oneself';
*nīcais* [means] in a small measure; *uccais* [means] loudly or greatly; *prāyas* mostly; *śanais* slowly [or] gently.

360.s:
sanā nitye vahirvāhye smātīte 'stamadarśane /
asti sattve ruṣoktāvūmuṃ praśne 'nunaye tvayi //
360.d:
सना नित्ये वहिर्वाह्ये स्मातीते ऽस्तमदर्शने /
अस्ति सत्त्वे रुषोक्तावूमुं प्रश्ने ऽनुनये त्वयि //
360.m:
*Sanā* [is used] for eternal; *bahis* for outside; *sma* for the past; *astam* for disappearance;
*asti* for existence; *ūm* in angry speech; *u* in questioning; and *ayi* in conciliation.

360.s:
hūṃ tarke syāduṣā rātreravasāne namo natau /
punararthe 'ṅganindāyāṃ duṣṭhu suṣṭhu praśaṃsane //
360.d:
हूं तर्के स्यादुषा रात्रेरवसाने नमो नतौ /
पुनरर्थे ऽङ्गनिन्दायां दुष्ठु सुष्ठु प्रशंसने //
360.m:
*Hūm* is used in conjecture; *uṣā* at the end of night; *namas* in bowing;
*aṅga* [is used] in the sense of 'again' or reproach; *duṣṭhu* in censure; *suṣṭhu* in praise.

360.s:
sāyaṃ sāye prage prātaḥ prabhāte nikaṣāntike /
parutparāryaisamo 'bde pūrve pūrvatare yati //
:p 275
360.d:
सायं साये प्रगे प्रातः प्रभाते निकषान्तिके /
परुत्परार्यैसमो ऽब्दे पूर्वे पूर्वतरे यति //
:प् 275

360.s:
adyātrāhny atha pūrvehnītyādau pūrvottarā parāt /
tathādharānyānyataretarātpūrvedyurādayaḥ //
360.d:
अद्यात्राह्न्य् अथ पूर्वेह्नीत्यादौ पूर्वोत्तरा परात् /
तथाधरान्यान्यतरेतरात्पूर्वेद्युरादयः //
360.m:
*Adya* means 'on this day'; then *pūrvedyuḥ* and the others are formed from *pūrva*, *uttara*, *para*,
and likewise from *adhara*, *anya*, *anyatara*, and *itara* [in the sense of 'on the previous day', etc.].

360.s:
ubhayadyuścobhayedyuḥ pare tvahni paredyapi /
hyo gate 'nāgate 'hni śvaḥ paraśvaḥ śvaḥpare 'hani //
360.d:
उभयद्युश्चोभयेद्युः परे त्वह्नि परेद्यपि /
ह्यो गते ऽनागते ऽह्नि श्वः परश्वः श्वःपरे ऽहनि //
360.m:
*Ubhayadyuḥ* and *ubhayedyuḥ* [mean] 'on both days'; *paredyavi* means 'on the other day';
*hyas* means 'yesterday' when a day has passed; *śvas* means 'tomorrow' when a day has not yet arrived; *paraśvas* means 'the day after tomorrow'.

360.s:
tadā tadānīṃ yugapadekadā sarvadā sadā /
etarhi sampratīdānīmadhunā sāmpratantathā //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe avyayavargā nāma
ṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś athaikaṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nānārthavargāḥ
360.d:
तदा तदानीं युगपदेकदा सर्वदा सदा /
एतर्हि सम्प्रतीदानीमधुना साम्प्रतन्तथा //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अव्ययवर्गा नाम
षष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथैकषष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
नानार्थवर्गाः
360.m:
*Tadā* and *tadānīm* [mean 'then']; *yugapat* and *ekadā* [mean 'at once' and 'at one time']; *sarvadā* and *sadā* [mean 'always'];
*etarhi*, *samprati*, *idānīm*, *adhunā*, and *sāmpratam* [mean 'now'].
Thus ends the three hundred and sixtieth chapter, entitled 'The Group of Indeclinables', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the three hundred and sixty-first chapter.
The Group of Polysemous Words.

361.s:
agnir uvāca
ākāśe tridive nāko lokastu bhavane jane /
padye yaśasi ca ślokaḥśare khaḍge ca sāyakaḥ //
361.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
आकाशे त्रिदिवे नाको लोकस्तु भवने जने /
पद्ये यशसि च श्लोकःशरे खड्गे च सायकः //

361.s:
ānakaḥ paṭaho bherī kalaṅko 'ṅkāpavādayoḥ /
mārute vedhasi vradhne puṃsi kaḥ kaṃ śiro 'mbunoḥ //
361.d:
आनकः पटहो भेरी कलङ्को ऽङ्कापवादयोः /
मारुते वेधसि व्रध्ने पुंसि कः कं शिरो ऽम्बुनोः //
361.m:
*Ānaka* means a war-drum and kettledrum; *kalaṅka* [is used] for a spot and defamation;
*ka* in the masculine means wind, the creator, and the sun; *kam* [in the neuter] means head and water.

361.s:
syāt pulākastucchadhānye saṃkṣepe bhaktasikthake /
mahendraguggulūlūkavyālagrāhiṣu kauśikaḥ //
361.d:
स्यात् पुलाकस्तुच्छधान्ये संक्षेपे भक्तसिक्थके /
महेन्द्रगुग्गुलूलूकव्यालग्राहिषु कौशिकः //
361.m:
*Pulāka* means shrivelled grain, abbreviation, and a grain of boiled rice;
*kauśika* [is used] for Indra, bdellium, an owl, and a snake-catcher.

361.s:
śālāvṛkau kapiśvānau mānaṃ syānmitisādhanaṃ /
sargaḥ svabhāvanirmokṣaniś cayādhyāyasmṛṣṭiṣu //
361.d:
शालावृकौ कपिश्वानौ मानं स्यान्मितिसाधनं /
सर्गः स्वभावनिर्मोक्षनिश् चयाध्यायस्मृष्टिषु //
361.m:
The two *śālāvṛka*s are monkey and dog; *māna* is a means of measuring;
*sarga* [is used] for natural disposition, relinquishment, determination, chapter, and creation.

361.s:
yogaḥ sannahanopāyadhyānasaṅgatiyuktiṣu /
:p 276
bhogaḥ sukhe stryādibhṛtāvabjau śaṅkaniśākarau //
361.d:
योगः सन्नहनोपायध्यानसङ्गतियुक्तिषु /
:प् 276
भोगः सुखे स्त्र्यादिभृतावब्जौ शङ्कनिशाकरौ //

361.s:
kāke bhagaṇḍau karaṭau duś carmā śipiviṣṭakaḥ /
riṣṭaṃ kṣemāśubhābhāveṣvariṣṭe tu śubhāśubhe //
361.d:
काके भगण्डौ करटौ दुश् चर्मा शिपिविष्टकः /
रिष्टं क्षेमाशुभाभावेष्वरिष्टे तु शुभाशुभे //
361.m:
The two *karaṭa*s are crow and elephant's temple; *śipiviṣṭa* means one with skin disease;
*riṣṭa* means welfare and absence of inauspiciousness; but the two *ariṣṭa*s mean auspicious and inauspicious.

361.s:
vyuṣṭiḥ phale samṛddhau ca dṛṣṭirjñāne 'kṣṇi darśane /
niṣṭhāniṣpattināśāntāḥ kāṣṭhotkarṣe sthitau diśi //
361.d:
व्युष्टिः फले समृद्धौ च दृष्टिर्ज्ञाने ऽक्ष्णि दर्शने /
निष्ठानिष्पत्तिनाशान्ताः काष्ठोत्कर्षे स्थितौ दिशि //
361.m:
*Vyuṣṭi* means fruit and prosperity; *dṛṣṭi* means knowledge, eye, and sight;
*niṣṭhā* means accomplishment, destruction, and end; *kāṣṭhā* [is used] for excellence, fixed state, and direction.

361.s:
bhūgovācastviḍā ilāḥ pragāḍhaṃ bhṛṣakṛcchrayoḥ /
bhṛśapratijñayorvāḍhaṃ śaktasthūlau dṛḍhau triṣu //
361.d:
भूगोवाचस्त्विडा इलाः प्रगाढं भृषकृच्छ्रयोः /
भृशप्रतिज्ञयोर्वाढं शक्तस्थूलौ दृढौ त्रिषु //
361.m:
*Iḍā* and *ilā* mean earth, cow, and speech; *pragāḍha* means excessive and difficult;
*bāḍha* means excessive and affirmative promise; the two *dṛḍha*s in three genders mean capable and stout.

361.s:
vinyastasaṃhatau vyūḍhau kṛṣṇo vyāse 'rjune harau /
paṇo dūyatādiṣūtsṛṣṭe bhṛtau mūlye dhane 'pi ca //
361.d:
विन्यस्तसंहतौ व्यूढौ कृष्णो व्यासे ऽर्जुने हरौ /
पणो दूयतादिषूत्सृष्टे भृतौ मूल्ये धने ऽपि च //
361.m:
The two *vyūḍha*s mean arranged and compact; *kṛṣṇa* is used for Vyāsa, Arjuna, and Hari;
*paṇa* means a stake in gambling, wages, price, and wealth.

361.s:
maurvyāṃ dravyāśrite satvaśuklasandhyādike guṇaḥ /
śreṣṭhe 'dhipe grāmaṇīḥ syāt jugpsākaruṇe ghṛṇe //
361.d:
मौर्व्यां द्रव्याश्रिते सत्वशुक्लसन्ध्यादिके गुणः /
श्रेष्ठे ऽधिपे ग्रामणीः स्यात् जुग्प्साकरुणे घृणे //
361.m:
*Guṇa* is used for a bowstring, quality residing in substance, sattva, white, sandhi, and so forth;
*grāmaṇī* means eminent and chief; *ghṛṇā* is used for revulsion and compassion.

361.s:
tṛṣṇā spṛhāpipāse dve vipaṇiḥ syādvaṇikpathe /
viṣābhimaraloheṣu tīkṣṇaṃ klīve khare triṣu //
361.d:
तृष्णा स्पृहापिपासे द्वे विपणिः स्याद्वणिक्पथे /
विषाभिमरलोहेषु तीक्ष्णं क्लीवे खरे त्रिषु //
361.m:
*Tṛṣṇā* means longing and thirst, both; *vipaṇi* is a merchant's shop;
*tīkṣṇa* in the neuter means poison, weapon, iron; in three genders it means sharp.

361.s:
pramāṇaṃ hetumaryādāśāstreyattāpramātṛṣu /
karaṇaṃ kṣetragātrādāvīriṇaṃ śūnyamūṣaraṃ //
361.d:
प्रमाणं हेतुमर्यादाशास्त्रेयत्ताप्रमातृषु /
करणं क्षेत्रगात्रादावीरिणं शून्यमूषरं //
361.m:
*Pramāṇa* is used for cause, limit, scripture, dimension, and knower;
*karaṇa* for organ, field, body, and so forth; *īriṇa* for barren land and saline soil.

361.s:
yantā hastipake sūte vahnijvālā ca hetayaḥ /
srutaṃ śāstrāvadhṛtayoryugaparyāptayoḥ kṛtaṃ //
361.d:
यन्ता हस्तिपके सूते वह्निज्वाला च हेतयः /
स्रुतं शास्त्रावधृतयोर्युगपर्याप्तयोः कृतं //
361.m:
*Yantṛ* means an elephant-driver and charioteer; *heti*s are firebrands and weapons;
*śruta* [is used] for scripture and what is heard; *kṛta* for an age and what is sufficient.

361.s:
khyāte hṛṣṭe pratīto 'bhijātastu kulaje budhe /
viviktau pūtavijanau mūrchitau mūḍsocchayau //
361.d:
ख्याते हृष्टे प्रतीतो ऽभिजातस्तु कुलजे बुधे /
विविक्तौ पूतविजनौ मूर्छितौ मूड्सोच्छयौ //
361.m:
*Pratīta* means famous and delighted; *abhijāta* means well-born and wise;
*vivikta* means pure and solitary; *mūrcchita* means unconscious and grown dense.

361.s:
artho 'bhidheyaraivastuprayojananivṛttiṣu /
nidānāgamayostīrthamṛṣijuṣṭajale gurau //
361.d:
अर्थो ऽभिधेयरैवस्तुप्रयोजननिवृत्तिषु /
निदानागमयोस्तीर्थमृषिजुष्टजले गुरौ //
361.m:
*Artha* [is used] for signified meaning, wealth, thing, purpose, and cessation;
*tīrtha* for cause, sacred text, water visited by sages, and spiritual preceptor.

361.s:
prādhānye rājaliṅge ca vṛṣāṅge kakudo 'striyāṃ /
strī sambijjñānasambhāṣākriyākārājināmasu //
:p 277
361.d:
प्राधान्ये राजलिङ्गे च वृषाङ्गे ककुदो ऽस्त्रियां /
स्त्री सम्बिज्ज्ञानसम्भाषाक्रियाकाराजिनामसु //
:प् 277

361.s:
dharme rahasyupaniṣat syādṛtau vatsare śarat /
padaṃ vyavasititrāṇasthānalakṣmāṅghrivastuṣu //
361.d:
धर्मे रहस्युपनिषत् स्यादृतौ वत्सरे शरत् /
पदं व्यवसितित्राणस्थानलक्ष्माङ्घ्रिवस्तुषु //
361.m:
*Upaniṣad* means virtue and secret; *śarad* means the season and a year;
*pada* is used for enterprise, protection, place, mark, foot, and thing.

361.s:
triṣvaṣṭamadhurau svādū mṛdū cātīkṣṇakomalau /
satye sādhau vidyamāne praśaste 'bhyarhite ca sat //
361.d:
त्रिष्वष्टमधुरौ स्वादू मृदू चातीक्ष्णकोमलौ /
सत्ये साधौ विद्यमाने प्रशस्ते ऽभ्यर्हिते च सत् //
361.m:
In three genders *svādu* means sweet; *mṛdu* means gentle and tender;
*sat* means true, virtuous, existing, praiseworthy, and venerable.

361.s:
vidhirvidhāne daive 'pi praṇidhiḥ prārthane care /
vadhūrjāyā snuṣā ca sudhālepo 'mṛtaṃ snuhī //
361.d:
विधिर्विधाने दैवे ऽपि प्रणिधिः प्रार्थने चरे /
वधूर्जाया स्नुषा च सुधालेपो ऽमृतं स्नुही //
361.m:
*Vidhi* means rule and also destiny; *praṇidhi* means solicitation and spy;
*vadhū* means young wife and daughter-in-law; *sudhā* means plaster, nectar, and euphorbia.

361.s:
spṛhā sampratyayaḥ śraddhā paṇḍitammanyagarvitau /
brahmabandhuradhikṣepe bhānū raṣmidivākarau //
361.d:
स्पृहा सम्प्रत्ययः श्रद्धा पण्डितम्मन्यगर्वितौ /
ब्रह्मबन्धुरधिक्षेपे भानू रष्मिदिवाकरौ //
361.m:
*Śraddhā* means desire and firm trust; *paṇḍitammanya* means conceited;
*brahmabandhu* is used in censure; *bhānu* means ray and sun.

361.s:
grāvāṇau śailapāṣānau mūrkhanīcau pṛthagjanau /
taruśailau śikhariṇau tanustvagdehayorapi //
361.d:
ग्रावाणौ शैलपाषानौ मूर्खनीचौ पृथग्जनौ /
तरुशैलौ शिखरिणौ तनुस्त्वग्देहयोरपि //
361.m:
The two *grāvan*s are rock and stone; *pṛthagjana* means fool and base man;
*śikharin* means tree and mountain; *tanu* means skin and body.

361.s:
ātmā yatno dhṛtirvuddhiḥ svabhāvo brahmavarṣma ca /
utthānaṃ pauruṣe tantre vyutthānaṃ pratirodhane //
361.d:
आत्मा यत्नो धृतिर्वुद्धिः स्वभावो ब्रह्मवर्ष्म च /
उत्थानं पौरुषे तन्त्रे व्युत्थानं प्रतिरोधने //
361.m:
*Ātman* means effort, firmness, intellect, nature, Brahman, and body;
*utthāna* means manly effort and army; *vyutthāna* means opposition.

361.s:
niryātanaṃ vairaśuddhau dāne nyāsārpaṇe 'pi ca /
vyasanaṃ vipadi bhraśe doṣe kāmajakopaje //
361.d:
निर्यातनं वैरशुद्धौ दाने न्यासार्पणे ऽपि च /
व्यसनं विपदि भ्रशे दोषे कामजकोपजे //
361.m:
*Niryātana* means requital of enmity, gift, and returning a deposit;
*vyasana* means misfortune, lapse, and vices born of desire and anger.

361.s:
mṛgayākṣo divāsvapnaḥ parivādaḥ striyo madaḥ /
tauryatrikaṃ vṛthāṭyā ca kāmajo daśako gaṇaḥ //
361.d:
मृगयाक्षो दिवास्वप्नः परिवादः स्त्रियो मदः /
तौर्यत्रिकं वृथाट्या च कामजो दशको गणः //
361.m:
Hunting, gambling with dice, sleeping by day, slander, women, drunkenness,
the musical triad, and aimless wandering are the group of ten born of desire.

361.s:
paiśūnyaṃ sāhasaṃ droha īrṣyāsūyārthadūṣaṇam /
vāgdaṇḍaś caiva pāruṣyaṃ krodhajo 'pi gaṇo 'ṣṭakaḥ //
361.d:
पैशून्यं साहसं द्रोह ईर्ष्यासूयार्थदूषणम् /
वाग्दण्डश् चैव पारुष्यं क्रोधजो ऽपि गणो ऽष्टकः //
361.m:
Calumny, violence, malice, envy, jealousy, destruction of property,
verbal abuse, and physical assault are the group of eight born of wrath.

361.s:
akarmaguhye kaupīnaṃ maithunaṃ saṅgatau ratau /
pradhānaṃ paramārthā dhīḥ prajñānaṃ buddhicihnayoḥ //
361.d:
अकर्मगुह्ये कौपीनं मैथुनं सङ्गतौ रतौ /
प्रधानं परमार्था धीः प्रज्ञानं बुद्धिचिह्नयोः //
361.m:
*Kaupīna* means improper act and the pudenda; *maithuna* means union and sexual pleasure;
*pradhāna* means highest truth and intellect; *prajñāna* means intellect and mark.

361.s:
krandane rodanāhvāne varṣma dehapramāṇayoḥ /
ārādhanaṃ sādhane syādavāptau toṣaṇe 'pi ca //
361.d:
क्रन्दने रोदनाह्वाने वर्ष्म देहप्रमाणयोः /
आराधनं साधने स्यादवाप्तौ तोषणे ऽपि च //
361.m:
*Krandana* means weeping and calling out; *varṣman* means body and stature;
*ārādhana* is used for accomplishment, attainment, and pleasing.

361.s:
ratnaṃ svajātiśreṣṭhe 'pi lakṣma cihnapradhānayoḥ /
:p 278
kalāpo bhūṣaṇe varhe tūṇīre saṃhate 'pi ca //
361.d:
रत्नं स्वजातिश्रेष्ठे ऽपि लक्ष्म चिह्नप्रधानयोः /
:प् 278
कलापो भूषणे वर्हे तूणीरे संहते ऽपि च //

361.s:
talpaṃ śayyāṭṭāreṣu ḍimbhau tu śiśuvāliśau /
stambhau sthūṇājaḍībhāvau sabhye saṃsadi vai sabhā //
361.d:
तल्पं शय्याट्टारेषु डिम्भौ तु शिशुवालिशौ /
स्तम्भौ स्थूणाजडीभावौ सभ्ये संसदि वै सभा //
361.m:
*Talpa* means bed and turret; the two *ḍimbha*s are child and fool;
*stambha* means post and paralysis; *sabhā* means assembly-hall and council.

361.s:
kiraṇapragrahau raśmī dharmāḥ puṇyayamādayaḥ /
lalāmaṃ pucchapuṇḍrāśvabhūṣāprādhānyaketuṣu //
361.d:
किरणप्रग्रहौ रश्मी धर्माः पुण्ययमादयः /
ललामं पुच्छपुण्ड्राश्वभूषाप्राधान्यकेतुषु //
361.m:
*Raśmi* means ray and rein; *dharma*s are merit, Yama, and the rest;
*lalāma* is used for a tail, forehead-mark, horse's ornament, eminence, and banner.

361.s:
pratyayo 'dhīnaśapathajñānaviśvāsahetuṣu /
samayāḥ śapathācārakālasiddhāntasaṃvidaḥ //
361.d:
प्रत्ययो ऽधीनशपथज्ञानविश्वासहेतुषु /
समयाः शपथाचारकालसिद्धान्तसंविदः //
361.m:
*Pratyaya* is used for dependence, oath, knowledge, trust, and cause;
*samaya*s are oath, custom, time, doctrine, and agreement.

361.s:
atyayo 'tikrame kṛcchre satyaṃ śapathatathyayoḥ /
vīryaṃ balaprabhāvau ca rūpyaṃ rūpe praśastake //
361.d:
अत्ययो ऽतिक्रमे कृच्छ्रे सत्यं शपथतथ्ययोः /
वीर्यं बलप्रभावौ च रूप्यं रूपे प्रशस्तके //
361.m:
*Atyaya* means transgression and distress; *satya* means oath and truth;
*vīrya* means strength and prowess; *rūpya* means beautiful form.

361.s:
durodaro dyūtakāre paṇe dyūte durodaraṃ /
mahāraṇye durgapathe kāntāraḥ punnapuṃsakaṃ //
361.d:
दुरोदरो द्यूतकारे पणे द्यूते दुरोदरं /
महारण्ये दुर्गपथे कान्तारः पुन्नपुंसकं //
361.m:
*Durodara* in the masculine means gambler, and in the neuter a stake and gambling;
*kāntāra* in masculine and neuter means a vast forest and difficult road.

361.s:
yamānilendracandrārkaviṣṇusiṃhādike hariḥ /
daro 'striyāṃ bhaye śvabhre jaṭharaḥ kaṭhine 'pi ca //
361.d:
यमानिलेन्द्रचन्द्रार्कविष्णुसिंहादिके हरिः /
दरो ऽस्त्रियां भये श्वभ्रे जठरः कठिने ऽपि च //
361.m:
*Hari* [is used] for Yama, wind, Indra, moon, sun, Viṣṇu, lion, and others;
*dara* not in the feminine means fear and pit; *jaṭhara* also means hard.

361.s:
udāro dātṛmahatoritarastvanyanīcayoḥ /
cūḍā kirīṭaṃ keśāś ca saṃyatā maulayastrayaḥ //
361.d:
उदारो दातृमहतोरितरस्त्वन्यनीचयोः /
चूडा किरीटं केशाश् च संयता मौलयस्त्रयः //
361.m: Udāra denotes generous and great; itara denotes other and low; / cūḍā, kirīṭa, and keśāḥ (bound hair) are the three [meanings of] mauli.

361.s:
baliḥ karopahārādau sainyasthair yādike balaṃ /
strīkaṭīvastrabandhe 'pi nīvī paripaṇe 'pi ca //
361.d:
बलिः करोपहारादौ सैन्यस्थैर् यादिके बलं /
स्त्रीकटीवस्त्रबन्धे ऽपि नीवी परिपणे ऽपि च //
361.m: Bali is used for tax, offering, and so forth; bala denotes army, firmness, and so forth; / nīvī denotes a woman's waist-cloth tie and also a stake in gambling.

361.s:
śukrale mūṣike śreṣṭhe sukṛte vṛṣabhe vṛṣaḥ /
dyūtākṣe sāriphalake 'pyākarṣo 'thākṣamindriye //
361.d:
शुक्रले मूषिके श्रेष्ठे सुकृते वृषभे वृषः /
द्यूताक्षे सारिफलके ऽप्याकर्षो ऽथाक्षमिन्द्रिये //
361.m: Vṛṣa is used for semen-producing, a mouse, the best, merit, and a bull; / ākarṣa denotes a gaming die and a game board; then akṣa denotes an organ of sense,

361.s:
nā dyūtāṅge ca karṣe ca vyavahāre kalidrume /
ūṣṇīṣaḥ syāt kirīṭādau karṣūḥ kulyābhidhāyinī //
361.d:
ना द्यूताङ्गे च कर्षे च व्यवहारे कलिद्रुमे /
ऊष्णीषः स्यात् किरीटादौ कर्षूः कुल्याभिधायिनी //
361.m: a die (masculine), the weight of a karṣa, a legal dispute, and the bibhītaka tree; / uṣṇīṣa is used for a diadem and the like; karṣū denotes a canal.

361.s:
pratyakṣe 'dhikṛte 'dhyakṣaḥ sūryavahnī vibhāvasū /
śṛṅgārādau viṣe vīrye guṇe rāge drave rasaḥ //
:p 279
361.d:
प्रत्यक्षे ऽधिकृते ऽध्यक्षः सूर्यवह्नी विभावसू /
शृङ्गारादौ विषे वीर्ये गुणे रागे द्रवे रसः //
:प् 279
361.m:
Adhyakṣa is used for perceived directly and a superintendent; vibhāvasu means the sun and fire; / rasa denotes sentiment in the erotic and the like, poison, vigor, quality, passion, and liquid.
[Page 279]

361.s:
tejaḥpurīṣayorvarca āgaḥ pāpāparādhayoḥ /
chandaḥ padye 'bhilāse ca sādhīyān sādhuvāḍhayoḥ /
vyūho vṛnde 'pyahirvṛtre 'pyagnīndvarkāstamonudaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nānārthavargā
namaikaṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha dviṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
bhūmivanauṣadhyādivargāḥ
361.d:
तेजःपुरीषयोर्वर्च आगः पापापराधयोः /
छन्दः पद्ये ऽभिलासे च साधीयान् साधुवाढयोः /
व्यूहो वृन्दे ऽप्यहिर्वृत्रे ऽप्यग्नीन्द्वर्कास्तमोनुदः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नानार्थवर्गा
नमैकषष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ द्विषष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
भूमिवनौषध्यादिवर्गाः
361.m:
Varcas is used for brilliance and feces; āgas for sin and offense; / chandas for verse and desire; sādhīyas for better and very much; / vyūha also for an assemblage; ahi for Vṛtra; agni, indu, and arka are dispellers of darkness.
Thus ends the three hundred and sixty-first chapter, named the Group of Homonyms, in the great Purāṇa of Agni.
Now, the three hundred and sixty-second chapter:
The groups of words for the earth, forests, medicinal herbs, and so forth.

362.s:
agnir uvāca
vakṣye bhūpurādrivanauṣadhisiṃhādinargakān /
bhūranantā kakṣamā dhātrī kṣmāpyākuḥ syāddharitryapi //
362.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
वक्ष्ये भूपुराद्रिवनौषधिसिंहादिनर्गकान् /
भूरनन्ता कक्षमा धात्री क्ष्माप्याकुः स्याद्धरित्र्यपि //
362.m: Agni said: / I will proclaim the groups of words for the earth, cities, mountains, forests, medicinal herbs, lions, and so forth. / Bhū, anantā, kṣamā, dhātrī, kṣmā, and urvī, as well as dharitrī, [denote the earth].

362.s:
mṛnmṛttikā praśastā tu mṛtsā mṛtsnā ca mṛttikā /
jagattrapiṣṭapaṃ lokaṃ bhuvanaṃ jagatī samā //
362.d:
मृन्मृत्तिका प्रशस्ता तु मृत्सा मृत्स्ना च मृत्तिका /
जगत्त्रपिष्टपं लोकं भुवनं जगती समा //
362.m: Mṛd and mṛttikā [denote earth or clay], but praiseworthy [earth] is mṛtsā and mṛtsnā; / jagat, trapiṣṭapa, loka, bhuvana, and jagatī are equivalent [for the world].

362.s:
ayanaṃ vartma mārgādhvapanthānaḥ padavī sṛtiḥ /
saraṇiḥ paddhattiḥ padyā vartanyekapadīti ca //
362.d:
अयनं वर्त्म मार्गाध्वपन्थानः पदवी सृतिः /
सरणिः पद्धत्तिः पद्या वर्तन्येकपदीति च //
362.m: Ayana, vartman, mārga, adhvan, panthan, padavī, sṛti, / saraṇi, paddhati, padyā, vartani, and ekapadī [denote a path].

362.s:
pūḥ strī purīnagaryau vā pāttanaṃ puṭabhedanam /
sthānīyaṃ nigamo 'nyattu yanmūlanagarātpuram //
362.d:
पूः स्त्री पुरीनगर्यौ वा पात्तनं पुटभेदनम् /
स्थानीयं निगमो ऽन्यत्तु यन्मूलनगरात्पुरम् //
362.m: Pūḥ (feminine), purī, nagarī, pattana, puṭabhedana, / sthānīya, and nigama [denote a city]; but a town apart from the main city

362.s:
tacchākhānagaraṃ veśo veśyājanasamāśrayaḥ /
āpaṇastu niṣadyāyāṃ vipaṇiḥ paṇyavīthikā //
362.d:
तच्छाखानगरं वेशो वेश्याजनसमाश्रयः /
आपणस्तु निषद्यायां विपणिः पण्यवीथिका //
362.m: is called a branch-city (śākhānagara); veśa is the dwelling of courtesans; / āpaṇa and niṣadyā [denote a shop]; vipaṇi is a market street.

362.s:
rathyā pratolī viśikhā syāccayo vapramastriyāṃ /
prākāro varaṇaḥ śālaḥ prācīraṃ prāntato vṛtiḥ //
:p 280
362.d:
रथ्या प्रतोली विशिखा स्याच्चयो वप्रमस्त्रियां /
प्राकारो वरणः शालः प्राचीरं प्रान्ततो वृतिः //
:प् 280
362.m:
Rathyā, pratolī, and viśikhā [mean a street]; caya and vapra (non-feminine) [mean an earthen mound]; / prākāra, varaṇa, śāla, and prācīra [denote a rampart]; an outer enclosure is a vṛti.
[Page 280]

362.s:
bhittiḥ strī kuhyameḍūkaṃ yadantarnastakīkasaṃ /
vāsaḥ kūṭo dvayoḥ śālā sabhā sañjavanantvidam //
362.d:
भित्तिः स्त्री कुह्यमेडूकं यदन्तर्नस्तकीकसं /
वासः कूटो द्वयोः शाला सभा सञ्जवनन्त्विदम् //
362.m: Bhitti (feminine) and kudya [denote a wall]; an eḍūka is that inside which bones are placed; / vāsa and kūṭa are of two genders [for a house]; śālā and sabhā [denote a hall]; sañjavana

362.s:
catuḥśālaṃ munīnāntu parṇaśāloṭajo 'striyāṃ /
caityamāyatanantulye vājiśālā tu mandurā //
362.d:
चतुःशालं मुनीनान्तु पर्णशालोटजो ऽस्त्रियां /
चैत्यमायतनन्तुल्ये वाजिशाला तु मन्दुरा //
362.m: is a four-winged mansion; for sages, a hut of leaves is uṭaja (non-feminine); / caitya and āyatana are equivalent [for a shrine]; a horse stable is mandurā.

362.s:
harmyādi dhanināṃ vāsaḥprāsādo devabhūbhujāṃ /
strī dvārdvāraṃ pratīhāraḥ syādvitardistu vedikā //
362.d:
हर्म्यादि धनिनां वासःप्रासादो देवभूभुजां /
स्त्री द्वार्द्वारं प्रतीहारः स्याद्वितर्दिस्तु वेदिका //
362.m: A mansion (harmya) and the like is the residence of the wealthy; a palace (prāsāda) belongs to gods and kings; / dvār (feminine), dvāra, and pratīhāra [mean a doorway]; a vitardi is an altar-platform (vedikā).

362.s:
kapotapālikāyantu viṭaṅkaṃ puṃ napuṃsakaṃ /
kavāṭamavarantulye niḥśreṇistvadhirohiṇī //
362.d:
कपोतपालिकायन्तु विटङ्कं पुं नपुंसकं /
कवाटमवरन्तुल्ये निःश्रेणिस्त्वधिरोहिणी //
362.m: A dove-cot is viṭaṅka (masculine and neuter); / kavāṭa and ara are equivalent [for a door-leaf]; niḥśreṇi and adhirohiṇī [denote a ladder].

362.s:
sammārjanī śodhanī syāt saṅkaro 'vakaras tathā /
adrigotrigirigrāvā gahanaṃ kānanaṃ vanaṃ //
362.d:
सम्मार्जनी शोधनी स्यात् सङ्करो ऽवकरस् तथा /
अद्रिगोत्रिगिरिग्रावा गहनं काननं वनं //
362.m: Sammārjanī and śodhanī [mean a broom]; saṅkara and avakara [mean sweepings or rubbish]; / adri, gotra, giri, and grāvan [mean a mountain]; gahana, kānana, and vana [mean a forest].

362.s:
ārāmaḥ syādupavanaṃ kṛtrimaṃ vanameva yat /
syādetadeva pramadavanamantaḥpurocitaṃ //
362.d:
आरामः स्यादुपवनं कृत्रिमं वनमेव यत् /
स्यादेतदेव प्रमदवनमन्तःपुरोचितं //
362.m: An ārāma is an upavana, which is an artificial grove; / the very same, when suited for the inner apartments, is a pleasure grove (pramadavana).

362.s:
vīthyālirāvaliḥ paṅktiśreṇīlekhāstu rājayaḥ /
vānaspatyaḥ phalaiḥ puṣpāttairapuṣpādvanaspatiḥ(?) //
362.d:
वीथ्यालिरावलिः पङ्क्तिश्रेणीलेखास्तु राजयः /
वानस्पत्यः फलैः पुष्पात्तैरपुष्पाद्वनस्पतिः(?) //
362.m: Vīthi, āli, āvali, paṅkti, śreṇī, lekhā, and rāji [mean a row]; / vānaspatya bears fruit from blossoms, while a vanaspati bears fruit without flowers.

362.s:
oṣadhyaḥ phalapākāntāḥ palāśī drudrumāgamāḥ /
sthāṇu vā nā dhruvaḥ śaṅkuḥ praphullotphullasaṃsphuṭāḥ //
362.d:
ओषध्यः फलपाकान्ताः पलाशी द्रुद्रुमागमाः /
स्थाणु वा ना ध्रुवः शङ्कुः प्रफुल्लोत्फुल्लसंस्फुटाः //
362.m: Oṣadhis perish upon ripening of fruit; palāśin, dru, druma, and āgama [mean a tree]; / a trunk without branches is sthāṇu (masculine), dhruva, or śaṅku; praphulla, utphulla, and saṃsphuṭa [mean fully blossomed].

362.s:
palāśaṃ chadanaṃ parṇamidhmamedhaḥ samit striyāṃ /
bodhidrumaś caladalo dadhitthagrāhimanmathāḥ //
362.d:
पलाशं छदनं पर्णमिध्ममेधः समित् स्त्रियां /
बोधिद्रुमश् चलदलो दधित्थग्राहिमन्मथाः //
362.m: Palāśa, chadana, and parṇa [mean a leaf]; idhma, edhas, and samidh (feminine) [mean firewood]; / bodhidruma and caladala [mean the sacred fig]; dadhittha, grāhin, and manmatha [mean the wood-apple tree];

362.s:
tasmin dadhiphalaḥ puṣpaphaladantaśaṭhāvapi /
uḍumbare hemadugdhaḥ kovidāre dvipatrakaḥ //
362.d:
तस्मिन् दधिफलः पुष्पफलदन्तशठावपि /
उडुम्बरे हेमदुग्धः कोविदारे द्विपत्रकः //
362.m: for that tree, dadhiphala, puṣpaphala, and dantaśaṭha are also used; / for the uḍumbara: hemadugdha; for the kovidāra: dvipatraka;

362.s:
saptaparṇo viśālatvak kṛtamālaṃ suvarṇakaḥ /
ārevatavyādhighātasampākacaturaṅgulāḥ //
362.d:
सप्तपर्णो विशालत्वक् कृतमालं सुवर्णकः /
आरेवतव्याधिघातसम्पाकचतुरङ्गुलाः //
362.m: for the saptaparṇa: viśālatvac; kṛtamāla and suvarṇaka, / ārevata, vyādhighāta, sampāka, and caturaṅgula [all denote the Cassia fistula];

362.s:
syājjambīre dantaśaṭho varuṇe tiktaśāvakaḥ /
:p 281
putrāge puruṣastuṅgaḥ keśaro devavallabhaḥ //
362.d:
स्याज्जम्बीरे दन्तशठो वरुणे तिक्तशावकः /
:प् 281
पुत्रागे पुरुषस्तुङ्गः केशरो देववल्लभः //

362.s:
pāribhadre nimbatarurmandāraḥ pārijātakaḥ /
vañjulaścitrakṛccātha dvau pītanakapītanau //
362.d:
पारिभद्रे निम्बतरुर्मन्दारः पारिजातकः /
वञ्जुलश्चित्रकृच्चाथ द्वौ पीतनकपीतनौ //
362.m: for the pāribhadra: nimbataru, mandāra, and pārijātaka; / vañjula and citrakṛt, and then the two words pītanaka and pītana [denote the hog-plum],

362.s:
āmrātake madhūke tu guḍapuṣpamadhudrumau /
pīlau guḍaphalaḥ sraṃsī nādeyī cāmbuvetasaḥ //
362.d:
आम्रातके मधूके तु गुडपुष्पमधुद्रुमौ /
पीलौ गुडफलः स्रंसी नादेयी चाम्बुवेतसः //
362.m: also āmrātaka; for the madhūka: guḍapuṣpa and madhudruma; / for the pīlu: guḍaphala and sraṃsin; and the water-cane (ambuvetasa) is nādeyī;

362.s:
śobhāñjane śigrutīkṣṇagandhakākṣīramocakāḥ /
rakto 'sau madhuśigruḥ syādariṣṭaḥ pheṇilaḥ samau //
362.d:
शोभाञ्जने शिग्रुतीक्ष्णगन्धकाक्षीरमोचकाः /
रक्तो ऽसौ मधुशिग्रुः स्यादरिष्टः फेणिलः समौ //
362.m: for the śobhāñjana: śigru, tīkṣṇagandha, akṣīva, and mocaka; / when red, it is madhuśigru; ariṣṭa and pheṇila are equivalent [for the soapberry];

362.s:
gālavaḥśāvaro lodhrastirīṭastilvamārjanau /
śeluḥ śleṣmātakaḥ śīta uddālo bahuvārakaḥ //
362.d:
गालवःशावरो लोध्रस्तिरीटस्तिल्वमार्जनौ /
शेलुः श्लेष्मातकः शीत उद्दालो बहुवारकः //
362.m: gālava, śāvara, lodhra, tirīṭa, tilva, and mārjana [denote the lodh tree]; / śelu, śleṣmātaka, śīta, uddāla, and bahuvāraka [denote the Cordia myxa];

362.s:
vaikaṅkataḥ śruvāvṛkṣo granthilo vyāghrapādapi /
tindukaḥ sphūrjakaḥ kālo nādeyī bhūmijambukaḥ //
362.d:
वैकङ्कतः श्रुवावृक्षो ग्रन्थिलो व्याघ्रपादपि /
तिन्दुकः स्फूर्जकः कालो नादेयी भूमिजम्बुकः //
362.m: vaikaṅkata, śruvāvṛkṣa, granthila, and also vyāghrapād [denote the Flacourtia]; / tinduka, sphūrjaka, and kāla [denote the ebony]; nādeyī and bhūmijambuka [denote the ground jambu];

362.s:
kākatindau pīlukaḥ syāt pāṭalirmokṣamuṣkakau /
kramukaḥ paṭṭikākhyaḥ syātkumbhī kaiṭaryakaṭphale //
362.d:
काकतिन्दौ पीलुकः स्यात् पाटलिर्मोक्षमुष्ककौ /
क्रमुकः पट्टिकाख्यः स्यात्कुम्भी कैटर्यकट्फले //
362.m: for the kākatindu: pīluka; pāṭali, mokṣa, and muṣkaka [are synonymous]; / kramuka is named paṭṭikā; kumbhī and kaiṭarya denote the kaṭphala;

362.s:
vīravṛkṣo 'ruṣkaro 'gnimukhī bhallātakīṃ triṣu /
savarjakāsanajīvāś ca pītasāle 'tha mālake //
362.d:
वीरवृक्षो ऽरुष्करो ऽग्निमुखी भल्लातकीं त्रिषु /
सवर्जकासनजीवाश् च पीतसाले ऽथ मालके //
362.m: vīravṛkṣa, aruṣkara, agnimukhī, and bhallātakī (in three genders) [denote the marking-nut]; / sarvajarja, āsana, and jīva denote the pītasāla; then for the mālaka:

362.s:
sarjāśvakarṇau vīrendrau indradruḥ kakubho 'rjunaḥ /
iṅgudī tāpasatarurmocā śālmalireva ca //
362.d:
सर्जाश्वकर्णौ वीरेन्द्रौ इन्द्रद्रुः ककुभो ऽर्जुनः /
इङ्गुदी तापसतरुर्मोचा शाल्मलिरेव च //
362.m: sarja, aśvakarṇa, and vīrendra; indradru, kakubha, and arjuna [denote the arjuna tree]; / iṅgudī and tāpasataru [are synonyms]; mocā and śālmali [denote the silk-cotton tree];

362.s:
ciravilvo naktamālaḥ karajaś ca karañjake /
prakīryaḥ pūtikarajo markaṭyaṅgāravallarī //
362.d:
चिरविल्वो नक्तमालः करजश् च करञ्जके /
प्रकीर्यः पूतिकरजो मर्कट्यङ्गारवल्लरी //
362.m: ciravilva, naktamāla, and karaja denote the karañjaka; / prakīrya, pūtikaraja, markaṭī, and aṅgāravallarī [are varieties];

362.s:
rohī rohitakaḥ plīhaśatrurdāḍimapuṣpakaḥ /
gāyatrī bālatanayaḥ khadiro dantadhāvanaḥ //
362.d:
रोही रोहितकः प्लीहशत्रुर्दाडिमपुष्पकः /
गायत्री बालतनयः खदिरो दन्तधावनः //
362.m: rohī, rohitaka, plīhaśatru, and dāḍimapuṣpaka [denote the rohitaka tree]; / gāyatrī, bālatanaya, khadira, and dantadhāvana [denote the catechu tree];

362.s:
arimedo viṭkhadire kadaraḥ khadire site /
pañcāṅgulo vardhamānaś cañcurgandharvahastakaḥ //
:p 282
362.d:
अरिमेदो विट्खदिरे कदरः खदिरे सिते /
पञ्चाङ्गुलो वर्धमानश् चञ्चुर्गन्धर्वहस्तकः //
:प् 282
362.m:
arimeda denotes the viṭkhadira; kadara denotes the white khadira; / pañcāṅgula, vardhamāna, cañcu, and gandharvahastaka [denote the castor-oil plant];
[Page 282]

362.s:
piṇḍītako maruvakaḥ pītadāru ca dāru ca /
devadāruḥ pūtikāṣṭhaṃ śyāmā tu mahilāhvayā //
362.d:
पिण्डीतको मरुवकः पीतदारु च दारु च /
देवदारुः पूतिकाष्ठं श्यामा तु महिलाह्वया //
362.m: piṇḍītaka and maruvaka [are synonyms]; pītadāru, dāru, / devadāru, and pūtikāṣṭha [denote the deodar cedar]; śyāmā is named mahilā;

362.s:
latā govandanī gundā priyaṅguḥ phalinī phalī /
maṇḍūkaparṇapatrorṇanaṭakaṭvaṅgaṭuṇṭukāḥ //
362.d:
लता गोवन्दनी गुन्दा प्रियङ्गुः फलिनी फली /
मण्डूकपर्णपत्रोर्णनटकट्वङ्गटुण्टुकाः //
362.m: latā, govandanī, gundā, priyaṅgu, phalinī, and phalī [denote the priyaṅgu creepers]; / maṇḍūkaparṇa, patrorṇa, naṭa, kaṭvaṅga, ṭuṇṭuka,

362.s:
śyonākaśukanāsarkṣadīrghavṛntakuṭannaṭāḥ /
pītadruḥ saralaścātha niculo 'mbuja ijjalaḥ //
362.d:
श्योनाकशुकनासर्क्षदीर्घवृन्तकुटन्नटाः /
पीतद्रुः सरलश्चाथ निचुलो ऽम्बुज इज्जलः //
362.m: śyonāka, śukanāsa, ṛkṣa, dīrghavṛnta, and kuṭannaṭa [denote the Oroxylum]; / pītadru and sarala [denote the pine]; nicula, ambuja, and ijjala [denote the Barringtonia];

362.s:
kākoḍumbarikā phalgurariṣṭaḥ picumardakaḥ /
sarvatobhadrako nimbe śirīṣastu kapītanaḥ //
362.d:
काकोडुम्बरिका फल्गुररिष्टः पिचुमर्दकः /
सर्वतोभद्रको निम्बे शिरीषस्तु कपीतनः //
362.m: kākoḍumbarikā and phalgu [are synonyms]; ariṣṭa, picumardaka, / and sarvatobhadraka denote the neem; śirīṣa and kapītana [denote the acacia];

362.s:
vakulo vañjulaḥ proktaḥ picchilāguruśiṃśapāḥ /
jayā jayantī tarkārī kaṇikā gaṇikārikā //
362.d:
वकुलो वञ्जुलः प्रोक्तः पिच्छिलागुरुशिंशपाः /
जया जयन्ती तर्कारी कणिका गणिकारिका //
362.m: vakula is declared to be vañjula; picchilā, aguru, and śiṃśapā [are associated terms]; / jayā, jayantī, tarkārī, kaṇikā, and gaṇikārikā [denote the Premna];

362.s:
āparṇamagnamanthaḥ syādvatsako girimallikā /
kālaskandhastamālaḥ syāt taṇḍulīyo 'lpamāriṣaḥ //
362.d:
आपर्णमग्नमन्थः स्याद्वत्सको गिरिमल्लिका /
कालस्कन्धस्तमालः स्यात् तण्डुलीयो ऽल्पमारिषः //
362.m: āparṇa and agnimantha are synonyms; vatsaka and girimallikā [denote the Wrightia]; / kālaskandha and tamāla [are synonyms]; taṇḍulīya and alpamāriṣa [denote the amaranth];

362.s:
sindhuvārastu nirguṇḍī saivāsphotā vanodbhavā /
gaṇikā yūthikāmbaṣṭhā saptalā navamālikā //
362.d:
सिन्धुवारस्तु निर्गुण्डी सैवास्फोता वनोद्भवा /
गणिका यूथिकाम्बष्ठा सप्तला नवमालिका //
362.m: sindhuvāra and nirguṇḍī [are synonyms]; the forest variety is āsphotā; / gaṇikā, yūthikā, ambaṣṭhā, saptalā, and navamālikā [denote types of jasmine];

362.s:
atimuktaḥ puṇḍrakaḥ syātkumārī taraṇiḥ sahā /
tatra śoṇe kuruvakastatra pīte kuruṇṭakaḥ //
362.d:
अतिमुक्तः पुण्ड्रकः स्यात्कुमारी तरणिः सहा /
तत्र शोणे कुरुवकस्तत्र पीते कुरुण्टकः //
362.m: atimukta and puṇḍraka [are synonyms]; kumārī, taraṇi, and sahā [denote the aloe or related herbs]; / among them, the red one is kuruvaka, and the yellow one is kuruṇṭaka;

362.s:
nīlā jhiṇṭī dvayorvāṇā bhiṇṭī sairīyakas tathā /
tasminrakte kuruvakaḥ pīte sahacarī dvayoḥ //
362.d:
नीला झिण्टी द्वयोर्वाणा भिण्टी सैरीयकस् तथा /
तस्मिन्रक्ते कुरुवकः पीते सहचरी द्वयोः //
362.m: nīlā, jhiṇṭī, and in two genders bāṇā, bhiṇṭī, and sairīyaka [denote the blue barleria]; / when red, it is kuruvaka; when yellow, sahacarī (in two genders);

362.s:
dhustūraḥ kitavo dhūrto rucako mātulaṅgake /
samīraṇo maruvakaḥ prasthapuṣpaḥ phaṇijjhakaḥ //
362.d:
धुस्तूरः कितवो धूर्तो रुचको मातुलङ्गके /
समीरणो मरुवकः प्रस्थपुष्पः फणिज्झकः //
362.m: dhustūra, kitava, and dhūrta [denote the thorn-apple]; rucaka denotes the citron; / samīraṇa and maruvaka [are synonyms]; prasthapuṣpa and phaṇijjhaka [denote a variety of basil];

362.s:
kuṭherakastu parṇāse 'thāsphoto vasukārkake /
śivamallī pāśupato vṛndā vṛkṣādanī tathā //
362.d:
कुठेरकस्तु पर्णासे ऽथास्फोतो वसुकार्कके /
शिवमल्ली पाशुपतो वृन्दा वृक्षादनी तथा //
362.m: kuṭheraka denotes the leaf-basil; āsphota denotes the calotropis (vasuka and arka); / śivamallī, pāśupata, vṛndā, and vṛkṣādanī [denote parasitic creepers and sacred basil].

362.s:
jīvantikā vṛkṣaruhā guḍūcī tantrikāmṛtā /
:p 283
somavallī madhurṇī mūrvā tu moraṭī tathā //
362.d:
जीवन्तिका वृक्षरुहा गुडूची तन्त्रिकामृता /
:प् 283
सोमवल्ली मधुर्णी मूर्वा तु मोरटी तथा //
362.m:
Jīvantikā, vṛkṣaruhā; guḍūcī, tantrikā, amṛtā,
[Page 283]
somavallī, madhurṇī; while mūrvā is moraṭī,

362.s:
madhulikā madhuśreṇī gokarṇī pīluparṇyapi /
pāṭhāmbaṣṭhā viddhakarṇī prācīnā vanatiktikā //
362.d:
मधुलिका मधुश्रेणी गोकर्णी पीलुपर्ण्यपि /
पाठाम्बष्ठा विद्धकर्णी प्राचीना वनतिक्तिका //
362.m: madhulikā, madhuśreṇī, gokarṇī, and pīluparṇī; / pāṭhā is ambaṣṭhā, viddhakarṇī, prācīnā, vanatiktikā;

362.s:
kaṭuḥ kaṭumbharā cātha cakrāṅgī śakulādanī /
ātmaguptā prāvṛṣāyī kapikacchuś ca markaṭī //
362.d:
कटुः कटुम्भरा चाथ चक्राङ्गी शकुलादनी /
आत्मगुप्ता प्रावृषायी कपिकच्छुश् च मर्कटी //
362.m: kaṭu, kaṭumbharā, cakrāṅgī, and śakulādanī; / ātmaguptā is prāvṛṣāyī, kapikacchu, and markaṭī;

362.s:
apāmārgaḥ śaikharikaḥ pratyakparṇī mayūrakaḥ /
phañjikā brāhmaṇī bhārgī dravanti śambarī vṛṣā //
362.d:
अपामार्गः शैखरिकः प्रत्यक्पर्णी मयूरकः /
फञ्जिका ब्राह्मणी भार्गी द्रवन्ति शम्बरी वृषा //
362.m: apāmārga is śaikharika, pratyakparṇī, [and] mayūraka; / phañjikā, brāhmaṇī, bhārgī; dravantī, śambarī, vṛṣā;

362.s:
maṇḍūkaparṇī bhaṇḍīrī samaṅgā kālameṣikā /
rodanī kacchurānantā samudrāntā durālabhā //
362.d:
मण्डूकपर्णी भण्डीरी समङ्गा कालमेषिका /
रोदनी कच्छुरानन्ता समुद्रान्ता दुरालभा //
362.m: maṇḍūkaparṇī, bhaṇḍīrī; samaṅgā, kālameṣikā; / rodanī, kacchurā, anantā, samudrāntā, durālabhā;

362.s:
pṛśniparṇī pṛthakparṇī kalaśirdhāvanirguhā /
nidigdhikā spṛśī vyāghrī kṣudrā dusparśayā saha //
362.d:
पृश्निपर्णी पृथक्पर्णी कलशिर्धावनिर्गुहा /
निदिग्धिका स्पृशी व्याघ्री क्षुद्रा दुस्पर्शया सह //
362.m: pṛśniparṇī, pṛthakparṇī, kalaśī, dhāvanī, guhā; / nidigdhikā, spṛśī, vyāghrī, kṣudrā together with dusparśā;

362.s:
avalgujaḥ somarājī suvalliḥ somavallikā /
kālameṣī kṛṣṇaphalā vakucī pūtiphaly api //
362.d:
अवल्गुजः सोमराजी सुवल्लिः सोमवल्लिका /
कालमेषी कृष्णफला वकुची पूतिफल्य् अपि //
362.m: avalguja, somarājī, suvalli, somavallikā, / kālameṣī, kṛṣṇaphalā, vākucī, and pūtiphalī;

362.s:
kaṇoṣaṇopakulyā syācchreyasī gajapippalī /
cavyantu cavikā kākaciñcī guñje tu kṛṣṇalā //
362.d:
कणोषणोपकुल्या स्याच्छ्रेयसी गजपिप्पली /
चव्यन्तु चविका काकचिञ्ची गुञ्जे तु कृष्णला //
362.m: kaṇā, ūṣaṇā, upakulyā; śreyasī is gajapippalī; / cavya is cavikā; kākaciñcī and kṛṣṇalā are guñjā;

362.s:
viśvā viṣā prativiṣā vanaśṛṅgāṭagokṣurau /
nārāyaṇī śatamūlī kāleyakaharidravaḥ //
362.d:
विश्वा विषा प्रतिविषा वनशृङ्गाटगोक्षुरौ /
नारायणी शतमूली कालेयकहरिद्रवः //
362.m: viśvā, viṣā, prativiṣā; vanaśṛṅgāṭa and gokṣura; / nārāyaṇī and śatamūlī; kāleyaka and haridrava;

362.s:
dārvī pacampacā dāru śuklā haimavatī vacā /
vacogragandhā ṣaḍgranthā golomī śataparvikā //
362.d:
दार्वी पचम्पचा दारु शुक्ला हैमवती वचा /
वचोग्रगन्धा षड्ग्रन्था गोलोमी शतपर्विका //
362.m: dārvī, pacampacā, dāru; śuklā, haimavatī, vacā; / vacā, ugagrandhā, ṣaḍgranthā, golomī, śataparvikā;

362.s:
āsphotā girikarṇī syāt siṃhāsyo vāsako vṛṣaḥ /
miśī madhurikācchatrā kokilākṣekṣurakṣurā //
362.d:
आस्फोता गिरिकर्णी स्यात् सिंहास्यो वासको वृषः /
मिशी मधुरिकाच्छत्रा कोकिलाक्षेक्षुरक्षुरा //
362.m: āsphotā is girikarṇī; siṃhāsya is vāsaka, vṛṣa; / miśī, madhurikā, chatrā; kokilākṣa, ikṣurakṣurā;

362.s:
viḍaṅgo 'strī kṛmighnaḥ syāt vajradrusnuksnuhī sudhā /
mṛdvīkā gostanī drākṣā valā vāṭyālakas tathā //
:p 284
362.d:
विडङ्गो ऽस्त्री कृमिघ्नः स्यात् वज्रद्रुस्नुक्स्नुही सुधा /
मृद्वीका गोस्तनी द्राक्षा वला वाट्यालकस् तथा //
:प् 284
362.m:
viḍaṅga, non-feminine, is kṛmighna; vajradru, snuk, snuhī, sudhā; / mṛdvīkā, gostanī, drākṣā; and balā is vāṭyālaka;
[Page 284]

362.s:
kālā masūravidalā tripuṭā trivṛtā trivṛt /
madhukaṃ klītakaṃ yaṣṭimadhukā madhuyaṣṭikā //
362.d:
काला मसूरविदला त्रिपुटा त्रिवृता त्रिवृत् /
मधुकं क्लीतकं यष्टिमधुका मधुयष्टिका //
362.m: kālā, masūravidalā, tripuṭā, trivṛtā, trivṛt; / madhuka, klītaka, yaṣṭimadhukā, madhuyaṣṭikā;

362.s:
vidārī kṣīraśuklekṣugandhā kroṣṭrī ca yā sitā /
gopī śyāmā śārivā syādanantotpalaśārivā //
362.d:
विदारी क्षीरशुक्लेक्षुगन्धा क्रोष्ट्री च या सिता /
गोपी श्यामा शारिवा स्यादनन्तोत्पलशारिवा //
362.m: vidārī, kṣīraśuklā, ikṣugandhā, kroṣṭrī, and that which is sitā; / gopī, śyāmā, śārivā, anantā, utpalaśārivā;

362.s:
mocā rambhā ca kadalī bhaṇṭākī duṣpradharṣiṇī /
sthirā dhruvā sālaparṇī śṛṅgī tu vṛṣabho vṛṣaḥ //
362.d:
मोचा रम्भा च कदली भण्टाकी दुष्प्रधर्षिणी /
स्थिरा ध्रुवा सालपर्णी शृङ्गी तु वृषभो वृषः //
362.m: mocā, rambhā, kadalī; bhaṇṭākī, duṣpradharṣiṇī; / sthirā, dhruvā, śālaparṇī; while śṛṅgī is vṛṣabha, vṛṣa;

362.s:
gāṅgerukī nāgabalā muṣalī tālamūlikā /
jyotsnī paṭolikā jālī ajaśṛṅgī viṣāṇikā //
362.d:
गाङ्गेरुकी नागबला मुषली तालमूलिका /
ज्योत्स्नी पटोलिका जाली अजशृङ्गी विषाणिका //
362.m: gāṅgerukī, nāgabalā; muṣalī, tālamūlikā; / jyotsnī, paṭolikā, jālī; ajaśṛṅgī, viṣāṇikā;

362.s:
syāllāṅgalikyagniśikhā tāmbūlī nāgavallyapi /
hareṇū reṇukā kauntī hrīvero divyanāgaraṃ //
362.d:
स्याल्लाङ्गलिक्यग्निशिखा ताम्बूली नागवल्ल्यपि /
हरेणू रेणुका कौन्ती ह्रीवेरो दिव्यनागरं //
362.m: lāṅgalikī is agniśikhā; tāmbūlī is nāgavallī; / hareṇu, reṇukā, kauntī; hrīvera, divyanāgara;

362.s:
kālānusāryavṛddhāśmapuṣpaśītaśivāni tu /
śaileyaṃ tālaparṇī tu daityā gandhakuṭī murā //
362.d:
कालानुसार्यवृद्धाश्मपुष्पशीतशिवानि तु /
शैलेयं तालपर्णी तु दैत्या गन्धकुटी मुरा //
362.m: kālānusārya, vṛddha, aśmapuṣpa, śīta, śivā / are śaileya; while tālaparṇī is daityā, gandhakuṭī, murā;

362.s:
granthiparṇaṃ śukaṃ varhi valā tu tripuṭā truṭiḥ /
śivā tāmalakī cātha hanurhaṭṭavilāsinī //
362.d:
ग्रन्थिपर्णं शुकं वर्हि वला तु त्रिपुटा त्रुटिः /
शिवा तामलकी चाथ हनुर्हट्टविलासिनी //
362.m: granthiparṇa, śuka, barhi; and valā, tripuṭā, truṭi; / śivā, tāmalakī; and hanu, haṭṭavilāsinī;

362.s:
kuṭaṃ naṭaṃ daśapuraṃ vāneyaṃ paripelavam /
tapasvanī jaṭāmāṃsī pṛkkā devī latā laśūḥ //
362.d:
कुटं नटं दशपुरं वानेयं परिपेलवम् /
तपस्वनी जटामांसी पृक्का देवी लता लशूः //
362.m: kuṭa, naṭa, daśapura, vāneya, paripelava; / tapasvanī, jaṭāmāṃsī; pṛkkā, devī, latā, laśū;

362.s:
karcurako drāviḍako gandhamūlī śaṭhī smṛtā /
syaddṛkṣagandhā chagalāntrā vegī vṛddhadārakaḥ //
362.d:
कर्चुरको द्राविडको गन्धमूली शठी स्मृता /
स्यद्दृक्षगन्धा छगलान्त्रा वेगी वृद्धदारकः //
362.m: karcuraka, drāviḍaka, gandhamūlī are remembered as śaṭhī; / vṛkṣagandhā, chagalāntrā, vegī, vṛddhadāraka;

362.s:
tuṇḍikerī raktaphalā vimbikā pīluparṇy api /
cāṅgerī cukrikāmbaṣṭā svarṇakṣīrī himāvatī //
362.d:
तुण्डिकेरी रक्तफला विम्बिका पीलुपर्ण्य् अपि /
चाङ्गेरी चुक्रिकाम्बष्टा स्वर्णक्षीरी हिमावती //
362.m: tuṇḍikerī, raktaphalā, bimbikā, pīluparṇī; / cāṅgerī, cukrikā, ambaṣṭhā; svarṇakṣīrī, himāvatī;

362.s:
sahasravedhī cukro 'mlavetasaḥ śatavedhyapi /
jīvantī jīvanī jīvā bhūminimvaḥ kirātakaḥ //
362.d:
सहस्रवेधी चुक्रो ऽम्लवेतसः शतवेध्यपि /
जीवन्ती जीवनी जीवा भूमिनिम्वः किरातकः //
362.m: sahasravedhī, cukra, amlavetasa, śatavedhī; / jīvantī, jīvanī, jīvā; bhūnimba, kirātaka;

362.s:
kūrcaśīrṣo madhukaraś candraḥ kapivṛkas tathā /
:p 285
dadrughnaḥ syādeḍagajo varṣābhūḥ śīthahāniṇī //
362.d:
कूर्चशीर्षो मधुकरश् चन्द्रः कपिवृकस् तथा /
:प् 285
दद्रुघ्नः स्यादेडगजो वर्षाभूः शीथहानिणी //

362.s:
kunandatī nikumbhastrā(1) yamānī vārṣikā tathā /
laśunaṅgṛñcanāriṣṭamahākandarasonakāḥ //
362.d:
कुनन्दती निकुम्भस्त्रा(1) यमानी वार्षिका तथा /
लशुनङ्गृञ्चनारिष्टमहाकन्दरसोनकाः //
362.m: kunandatī, nikumbhā, yamānī, vārṣikā; / laśuna, gṛñjana, ariṣṭa, mahākanda, rasonaka;

362.s:
vārāhī vadarā gṛṣṭiḥ kākamācī tu vāyasī /
śatapuṣpā sitacchatrāticchatrā madhurā misiḥ //
362.d:
वाराही वदरा गृष्टिः काकमाची तु वायसी /
शतपुष्पा सितच्छत्रातिच्छत्रा मधुरा मिसिः //
362.m: vārāhī, badarā, gṛṣṭi; kākamācī is vāyasī; / śatapuṣpā, sitacchatrā, aticchatrā, madhurā, misi;

362.s:
avākpuṣpī kāravī ca saraṇā tu prasāraṇī /
kaṭambharā bhadravalā karvūraś ca śaṭī hy atha //
362.d:
अवाक्पुष्पी कारवी च सरणा तु प्रसारणी /
कटम्भरा भद्रवला कर्वूरश् च शटी ह्य् अथ //
362.m: avākpuṣpī, kāravī; saraṇā is prasāraṇī; / kaṭambharā, bhadravalā; karvūra and śaṭī;

362.s:
paṭolaḥ kulakastiktaḥ kāravellaḥ kaṭillakaḥ /
kuṣmāṇḍakastu karkārurirvāruḥ karkaṭī striyau //
362.d:
पटोलः कुलकस्तिक्तः कारवेल्लः कटिल्लकः /
कुष्माण्डकस्तु कर्कारुरिर्वारुः कर्कटी स्त्रियौ //
362.m: paṭola, kulaka, tikta; kāravella, kaṭillaka; / kuṣmāṇḍaka is karkāru; irvāru and karkaṭī are both feminine;

362.s:
ikṣvākuḥ kaṭutumbī syādviśālā tvindravāruṇī /
arśeghnaḥ śūraṇaḥ kando mustakaḥ kuruvindakaḥ //
362.d:
इक्ष्वाकुः कटुतुम्बी स्याद्विशाला त्विन्द्रवारुणी /
अर्शेघ्नः शूरणः कन्दो मुस्तकः कुरुविन्दकः //
362.m: ikṣvāku is kaṭutumbī; viśālā is indravāruṇī; / arśoghna, śūraṇa, kanda; mustaka, kuruvindaka;

362.s:
vaṃśe tvaksārakarmāraveṇumaskaratejanāḥ /
chatrāticchatrapālaghnau mālātṛṇakabhūstṛṇe //
362.d:
वंशे त्वक्सारकर्मारवेणुमस्करतेजनाः /
छत्रातिच्छत्रपालघ्नौ मालातृणकभूस्तृणे //
362.m: for bamboo [the synonyms are] tvaksāra, karmāra, veṇu, maskara, tejana; / chatrā, aticchatrā, pālaghna for mālātṛṇa and bhūstṛṇa;

362.s:
tṛṇarājāhvayastālo ghoṇṭā kramukapugakau /
śārdūladvīpinau vyaghre haryakṣaḥ keśarī hariḥ //
362.d:
तृणराजाह्वयस्तालो घोण्टा क्रमुकपुगकौ /
शार्दूलद्वीपिनौ व्यघ्रे हर्यक्षः केशरी हरिः //
362.m: the palmyra palm is named tṛṇarāja; ghoṇṭā, kramuka, pūgaka [for the betel palm]; / śārdūla and dvīpin for a tiger; haryakṣa, keśarin, hari [for a lion];

362.s:
kolaḥ pautrī varāhaḥ syāt koka īhāmṛgo vṛkaḥ /
lūtorṇanābhau tu samau tantuvāyaś ca markaṭe //
362.d:
कोलः पौत्री वराहः स्यात् कोक ईहामृगो वृकः /
लूतोर्णनाभौ तु समौ तन्तुवायश् च मर्कटे //
362.m: kola, potrin, varāha [for a boar]; koka, īhāmṛga, vṛka [for a wolf]; / lūtā and ūrṇanābha are equivalent, and tantuvāya for a spider;

362.s:
vṛścikaḥ śūkakīṭaḥ syātsāraṅgastokakau samau /
kṛkavākustāmracūḍaḥ pikaḥ kokila ity api //
362.d:
वृश्चिकः शूककीटः स्यात्सारङ्गस्तोककौ समौ /
कृकवाकुस्ताम्रचूडः पिकः कोकिल इत्य् अपि //
362.m: vṛścika is śūkakīṭa; sāraṅga and stokaka are identical; / kṛkavāku and tāmracūḍa [for a rooster]; pika and kokila [for a cuckoo];

362.s:
kake tu karaṭāriṣṭau vakaḥ kahva udāhṛtaḥ /
kokaś cakraś cakravāko kādambaḥ kalahaṃsakaḥ //
362.d:
कके तु करटारिष्टौ वकः कह्व उदाहृतः /
कोकश् चक्रश् चक्रवाको कादम्बः कलहंसकः //
362.m: for a crow [the terms are] karaṭa and ariṣṭa; baka is said to be kahva; / koka, cakra, cakravāka; kādamba, kalahaṃsa;

362.s:
pataṅgikā puttikā syātsaraghā madhumakṣikā /
:n
1 sakuladantī nirdaṃṣṭreti kha..
:p 286
dvirephapuṣpaliḍbhṛṅgaṣaṭpadabhramarā.alayaḥ //
362.d:
पतङ्गिका पुत्तिका स्यात्सरघा मधुमक्षिका /
:न्
1 सकुलदन्ती निर्दंष्ट्रेति ख..
:प् 286
द्विरेफपुष्पलिड्भृङ्गषट्पदभ्रमरा.अलयः //

362.s:
kekī śikhyasya vākkekā śakuntiśakunidvijāḥ /
strī pakṣatiḥ pakṣamūlañcañcustoṭirubhe striyau //
362.d:
केकी शिख्यस्य वाक्केका शकुन्तिशकुनिद्विजाः /
स्त्री पक्षतिः पक्षमूलञ्चञ्चुस्तोटिरुभे स्त्रियौ //
362.m: kekin, śikhin, [and] its cry is kekā; śakunti, śakuni, dvija; / the feminine is pakṣati, [meaning] the root of a wing; cañcu and toṭi are both feminine [for a beak];

362.s:
gatiruḍḍinasaṇḍīnau kulāyo nīḍamastriyāṃ /
peśī koṣo dvihīne 'ṇḍaṃ pṛthukaḥ śāvakaḥ śiśuḥ //
362.d:
गतिरुड्डिनसण्डीनौ कुलायो नीडमस्त्रियां /
पेशी कोषो द्विहीने ऽण्डं पृथुकः शावकः शिशुः //
362.m: modes of flight are uḍḍīna and saṇḍīna; kulāya and nīḍa are non-feminine [for a nest]; / peśī, koṣa; egg is non-dual and neuter; pṛthuka, śāvaka, śiśu [for the young];

362.s:
potaḥ pāko 'rbhako ḍimbhaḥ sandohavyūhako gaṇaḥ /
stomaughanikaravrātā nikurambaṃ kadambakaṃ /
saṅghātasañcayau vṛndaṃ puñjarāśī tu kūṭakaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe bhūmivanauṣadhyādivargā nāma
dviṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha triṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nṛbrahmakṣatraviṭśūdravargāḥ
362.d:
पोतः पाको ऽर्भको डिम्भः सन्दोहव्यूहको गणः /
स्तोमौघनिकरव्राता निकुरम्बं कदम्बकं /
सङ्घातसञ्चयौ वृन्दं पुञ्जराशी तु कूटकं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे भूमिवनौषध्यादिवर्गा नाम
द्विषष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ त्रिषष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
नृब्रह्मक्षत्रविट्शूद्रवर्गाः
362.m:
pota, pāka, arbhaka, ḍimbha; sandoha, vyūhaka, gaṇa, / stoma, ogha, nikara, vrāta, nikuramba, kadambaka, / saṅghāta, sañcaya, vṛnda, puñja, rāśi, and kūṭaka [for an assemblage];
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the section on the earth, forest herbs, and related items, being the three hundred and sixty-second chapter.
Now the three hundred and sixty-third chapter.
The groups of terms for humans, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras.

363.s:
agnir uvāca
nṛbrahmakṣatraviṭśūdravargānvakṣye 'tha nāmataḥ /
naraḥ pañcajanā martya yadyoṣāvaṃlā vadhūḥ //
363.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
नृब्रह्मक्षत्रविट्शूद्रवर्गान्वक्ष्ये ऽथ नामतः /
नरः पञ्चजना मर्त्य यद्योषावंला वधूः //
363.m: Agni said: / Now I shall explain by name the groups [of terms] for humans, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras: / nara, pañcajana, martya; yoṣā, avalā, vadhū;

363.s:
kāntārthinī tu yā yāti saṅketaṃ sābhisārikā /
kulaṭā puṃś calyasatī nagnikā strī ca koṭavī //
363.d:
कान्तार्थिनी तु या याति सङ्केतं साभिसारिका /
कुलटा पुंश् चल्यसती नग्निका स्त्री च कोटवी //
363.m: she who goes to a rendezvous seeking her lover is an abhisārikā; / kulaṭā, puṃścalī, asatī; and nagnikā and koṭavī are [names for a girl];

363.s:
kātyāyanyardhavṛddhā yā sairindhrī paraveśmagā /
asikrī syādavṛddhā yā malinī tu rajasvalā //
363.d:
कात्यायन्यर्धवृद्धा या सैरिन्ध्री परवेश्मगा /
असिक्री स्यादवृद्धा या मलिनी तु रजस्वला //
363.m: kātyāyanī is a middle-aged woman; sairindhrī is one who goes to another's house; / asiknī is one who is not aged; malinī is a menstruating woman;

363.s:
vārastrī gaṇikā veśyā bhrātṛjāyāstu yātaraḥ /
nanāndā tu svasā patyuḥ sapiṇḍāstu sanābhayaḥ //
:p 287
363.d:
वारस्त्री गणिका वेश्या भ्रातृजायास्तु यातरः /
ननान्दा तु स्वसा पत्युः सपिण्डास्तु सनाभयः //
:प् 287
363.m:
vārastrī, gaṇikā, veśyā; wives of brothers are yātaraḥ; / nanāndṛ is a husband's sister; sapiṇḍas are sanābhis;
[Page 287]

363.s:
samānodaryasodaryasagarbhasahajāssamāḥ /
sagotrabāndhavajñātibandhusvasvajanāḥ samāḥ //
363.d:
समानोदर्यसोदर्यसगर्भसहजास्समाः /
सगोत्रबान्धवज्ञातिबन्धुस्वस्वजनाः समाः //
363.m: samānodarya, sodarya, sagarbha, and sahaja are equal; / sagotra, bāndhava, jñāti, bandhu, sva, and svajana are identical;

363.s:
dampatī jampatī bhāryāpatī jāyāpatī ca tau /
garbhāśayo jarāyuḥ syādulvañca kalalo 'striyāṃ //
363.d:
दम्पती जम्पती भार्यापती जायापती च तौ /
गर्भाशयो जरायुः स्यादुल्वञ्च कललो ऽस्त्रियां //
363.m: dampatī, jampatī, bhāryāpatī, and jāyāpatī [for husband and wife]; / the womb is garbhāśaya, jarāyu, and ulva; kalala is non-feminine [for an embryo];

363.s:
garbho bhruṇa imau tulyau klīvaṃ śaṇḍo napuṃsakam /
syāduttānaśayā ḍimbhā bālo māṇavakaḥ smṛtaḥ //
363.d:
गर्भो भ्रुण इमौ तुल्यौ क्लीवं शण्डो नपुंसकम् /
स्यादुत्तानशया डिम्भा बालो माणवकः स्मृतः //
363.m: garbha and bhrūṇa are equivalent; klība, śaṇḍa, napuṃsaka [for a eunuch]; / uttānaśayā and ḍimbhā [for a suckling infant]; bāla and māṇavaka are remembered [for a child];

363.s:
piciṇḍilo vṛhatkukṣiravabhraṭo natanāsike /
vikalāṅgastu pogaṇḍa ārogyaṃ syādanāmayam //
363.d:
पिचिण्डिलो वृहत्कुक्षिरवभ्रटो नतनासिके /
विकलाङ्गस्तु पोगण्ड आरोग्यं स्यादनामयम् //
363.m: piciṇḍila and bṛhatkukṣi [for a pot-bellied person]; avabhraṭa [and] natanāsika [for a flat-nosed person]; / vikalāṅga and pogaṇḍa [for one of impaired limbs]; health is ārogya and anāmaya.

363.s:
syādeḍe vadhiraḥ kubje gaḍulaḥ kukare kuniḥ /
kṣayaḥ śoṣaś ca yakṣmā ca pratiśyāyustu pīnasaḥ //
363.d:
स्यादेडे वधिरः कुब्जे गडुलः कुकरे कुनिः /
क्षयः शोषश् च यक्ष्मा च प्रतिश्यायुस्तु पीनसः //
363.m:
[The word] *vadhira* refers to a deaf person (*eḍa*); *gaḍula* to a hunchback (*kubja*); *kuni* to one with a deformed hand (*kukara*).
*Kṣaya*, *śoṣa*, and *yakṣman* [mean consumption]; while *pratiśyāya* and *pīnasa* [mean catarrh].

363.s:
strī kṣutkṣutaṃ kṣayaṃ puṃsi kāsastu kṣavathuḥ pumān /
śothastu śvayathuḥ śophaḥ pādasphoṭo vipādikā //
363.d:
स्त्री क्षुत्क्षुतं क्षयं पुंसि कासस्तु क्षवथुः पुमान् /
शोथस्तु श्वयथुः शोफः पादस्फोटो विपादिका //
363.m:
*Kṣut* is feminine and *kṣuta* neuter [for sneezing]; *kṣaya* is masculine [for consumption]; *kāsa* and *kṣavathu* are masculine [for coughing and sneezing].
*Śotha*, *śvayathu*, and *śopha* [mean swelling]; and *vipādikā* is a foot-fissure (*pādasphoṭa*).

363.s:
kilāsaṃ sidhnakacchāntu pāma pāmā vicarcikā /
koṭho maṇḍalakaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ śvitre drur nāmakārśasī //
363.d:
किलासं सिध्नकच्छान्तु पाम पामा विचर्चिका /
कोठो मण्डलकं कुष्ठं श्वित्रे द्रुर् नामकार्शसी //
363.m:
*Kilāsa* and *sidhma* [mean white leprosy]; *kacchū*, *pāman* (masculine/feminine), and *vicarcikā* [mean scabies];
*koṭha*, *maṇḍalaka*, and *kuṣṭha* [mean leprosy or ringworm]; *drū* is another name for *śvitra* [leucoderma]; [and *arśas* means hemorrhoids].

363.s:
anāhastu vibandhaḥ syādgrahaṇī rukpravāhikā /
vījavīryendrayaṃ śukraṃ palalaṃ kravyamāmiṣaṃ //
363.d:
अनाहस्तु विबन्धः स्याद्ग्रहणी रुक्प्रवाहिका /
वीजवीर्येन्द्रयं शुक्रं पललं क्रव्यमामिषं //
363.m:
*Anāha* is constipation (*vibandha*); *grahaṇī* and *pravāhikā* are ailments [of dysentery].
*Bīja*, *vīrya*, *indriya*, and *śukra* [denote semen]; *palala*, *kravya*, and *āmiṣa* [denote flesh].

363.s:
vukkāgramāṃsaṃ hṛdayaṃ hanmedastu vapā vasā /
paścādgrīvā śirā manyā nāḍī tu dhamaniḥ śirā //
363.d:
वुक्काग्रमांसं हृदयं हन्मेदस्तु वपा वसा /
पश्चाद्ग्रीवा शिरा मन्या नाडी तु धमनिः शिरा //
363.m:
*Vukkā* is the heart-meat (*agramāṃsa*); *hṛdaya* [is the heart]; *medas*, *vapā*, and *vasā* are fat.
*Manyā* is the back of the neck or carotid artery (*paścādgrīvāśirā*); *dhamanī* and *śirā* mean a blood-vessel (*nāḍī*).

363.s:
tilakaṃ ktoma mastiṣkaṃ drūṣikā netrayormalam /
antraṃ purī tadgulmastu plīhā puṃsy atha vasnasā //
363.d:
तिलकं क्तोम मस्तिष्कं द्रूषिका नेत्रयोर्मलम् /
अन्त्रं पुरी तद्गुल्मस्तु प्लीहा पुंस्य् अथ वस्नसा //
363.m:
*Tilaka* [and] *kloman* [are internal organs]; *mastiṣka* is brain-matter; *dūṣikā* is rheum of the eyes.
*Antra* and *purītat* [mean intestines]; *gulma* and *plīhan* are masculine [denoting the spleen]; then *vasnasā*

363.s:
snāyuḥ striyāṃ kālakhaṇḍayakṛtī tu same ime /
syāt karpūraḥ kapālo 'strī kīkasaṅkulyamasthi ca //
363.d:
स्नायुः स्त्रियां कालखण्डयकृती तु समे इमे /
स्यात् कर्पूरः कपालो ऽस्त्री कीकसङ्कुल्यमस्थि च //
363.m:
and *snāyu* are feminine [for sinew]; *kālakhaṇḍa* and *yakṛt* are equivalent [for the liver].
*Karpūra* and *kapāla* (non-feminine) [denote the skull]; *kīkasa*, *kulya*, and *asthi* denote bone.

363.s:
syāccharīrāsthni kaṅkālaḥ pṛṣṭhāsthni tu kaśerukā /
:p 288
śiro 'sthani karoṭiḥ strī pārśvāsthani tu parśukā //
363.d:
स्याच्छरीरास्थ्नि कङ्कालः पृष्ठास्थ्नि तु कशेरुका /
:प् 288
शिरो ऽस्थनि करोटिः स्त्री पार्श्वास्थनि तु पर्शुका //
363.m:
*Kaṅkāla* refers to the skeleton of the body; *kaśerukā* refers to the back-bone.
[Page 288]
*Karoṭi* (feminine) refers to the head-bone [cranium]; *parśukā* refers to the side-bone [rib].

363.s:
aṅgaṃ pratīko 'vayavaḥ śarīraṃ varṣma vigrahaḥ /
kaṭo nā śroṇiphalakaṃ kaṭiḥ śroṇiḥ kakudmatī //
363.d:
अङ्गं प्रतीको ऽवयवः शरीरं वर्ष्म विग्रहः /
कटो ना श्रोणिफलकं कटिः श्रोणिः ककुद्मती //
363.m:
*Aṅga*, *pratīka*, and *avayava* [mean limb or part]; *śarīra*, *varṣman*, and *vigraha* [mean body].
*Kaṭa* (masculine) and *śroṇiphalaka* [mean the pelvic bone]; *kaṭi*, *śroṇi*, and *kakudmatī* [mean hip or loins].

363.s:
paścānnitambaḥ strīkaṭyāḥ klīve tu jaghanaṃ puraḥ /
kūpakau tu nitambasthau dvayahīne kakundare //
363.d:
पश्चान्नितम्बः स्त्रीकट्याः क्लीवे तु जघनं पुरः /
कूपकौ तु नितम्बस्थौ द्वयहीने ककुन्दरे //
363.m:
*Nitamba* is the rear of a woman's hips; *jaghana* in the neuter is the front.
*Kūpaka* (dual) are the two depressions situated on the buttocks; in the dual, *kakundara* [is synonymous].

363.s:
striyāṃ sphicau kaṭiprothāvupastho vakṣyamāṇayoḥ /
bhagaṃ yonirdvayoḥ śiśno meḍhro mehanaśephasī //
363.d:
स्त्रियां स्फिचौ कटिप्रोथावुपस्थो वक्ष्यमाणयोः /
भगं योनिर्द्वयोः शिश्नो मेढ्रो मेहनशेफसी //
363.m:
*Sphici* (dual, feminine) and *kaṭiprotha* [denote the buttocks]; *upastha* denotes the two genitals about to be mentioned:
*bhaga* and *yoni* are [used] for the two [female organs]; *śiśna*, *meḍhra*, *mehana*, and *śephas* [denote the penis].

363.s:
piciṇḍakukṣī jaṭharodaraṃ tundaṃ kucau stanau /
cūcukantu kucāgraṃ syānna nā kroḍaṃ bhujāntaram //
363.d:
पिचिण्डकुक्षी जठरोदरं तुन्दं कुचौ स्तनौ /
चूचुकन्तु कुचाग्रं स्यान्न ना क्रोडं भुजान्तरम् //
363.m:
*Piciṇḍa*, *kukṣi*, *jaṭhara*, *udara*, and *tunda* [mean belly]; *kuca* and *stana* [mean breast].
*Cūcuka* is the tip of the breast [nipple]; *kroḍa* (masculine or neuter) and *bhujāntara* [mean chest].

363.s:
skandho bhujaśiro 'ṃśo 'strī sandhī tasyaiva jatruṇī /
punarbhavaḥ kararuho nakho 'strī nakharo 'striyāṃ //
363.d:
स्कन्धो भुजशिरो ऽंशो ऽस्त्री सन्धी तस्यैव जत्रुणी /
पुनर्भवः कररुहो नखो ऽस्त्री नखरो ऽस्त्रियां //
363.m:
*Skandha*, *bhujaśiras*, and *aṃsa* (non-feminine) [mean shoulder]; *jartu* (dual) are its joints [collarbones].
*Punarbhava*, *kararuha*, *nakha* (non-feminine), and *nakhara* (non-feminine) [mean fingernail].

363.s:
pradeśatālagokarṇāstarjanyādiyute tate /
aṅguṣṭhe sakaniṣṭhe syādvitastirdvādaśāṅgulaḥ //
363.d:
प्रदेशतालगोकर्णास्तर्जन्यादियुते तते /
अङ्गुष्ठे सकनिष्ठे स्याद्वितस्तिर्द्वादशाङ्गुलः //
363.m:
*Pradeśa*, *tāla*, and *gokarṇa* are [the spans of] the extended thumb with the forefinger and following [fingers] respectively;
with the little finger, it is a *vitasti*, [measuring] twelve finger-breadths.

363.s:
pāṇau ca peṭapratalaprahastā vistṛtāṅgulau /
baddhamuṣṭikaro ratniraratniḥ sa kaniṣṭhavān //
363.d:
पाणौ च पेटप्रतलप्रहस्ता विस्तृताङ्गुलौ /
बद्धमुष्टिकरो रत्निररत्निः स कनिष्ठवान् //
363.m:
On the hand with outstretched fingers, the terms are *peṭa*, *pratala*, and *prahasta*;
a hand with a clenched fist is a *ratni*; with the little finger extended it is an *aratni*.

363.s:
kambugrīvā trirekhā sāvaṭurghāṭā kṛkāṭikā /
adhaḥ syāccivukañcauṣṭhādatha gaṇḍau galo hanuḥ //
363.d:
कम्बुग्रीवा त्रिरेखा सावटुर्घाटा कृकाटिका /
अधः स्याच्चिवुकञ्चौष्ठादथ गण्डौ गलो हनुः //
363.m:
*Kambugrīvā* is a neck with three folds; *avaṭu*, *ghāṭā*, and *kṛkāṭikā* [mean the nape of the neck].
Below the lip is the chin (*civuka*); then the two cheeks (*gaṇḍa*), the throat (*gala*), and the jaw (*hanu*).

363.s:
apāṅgau netrayorantau kaṭākṣo 'pāṅgadarśane /
cikuraḥ kuntalo bālaḥ pratikarma prasādhanam //
363.d:
अपाङ्गौ नेत्रयोरन्तौ कटाक्षो ऽपाङ्गदर्शने /
चिकुरः कुन्तलो बालः प्रतिकर्म प्रसाधनम् //
363.m:
*Apāṅga* (dual) are the outer corners of the eyes; a glance from the corner of the eye is a *kaṭākṣa*.
*Cikura*, *kuntala*, and *vāla* [mean hair]; *pratikarma* and *prasādhana* [mean adornment or toilet].

363.s:
ākālpaveśau nepathyaṃ pratyakṣaṃ khelayogajam /
cūḍāmaṇiḥ śiroratnaṃ taralo hāramadhyagaḥ //
363.d:
आकाल्पवेशौ नेपथ्यं प्रत्यक्षं खेलयोगजम् /
चूडामणिः शिरोरत्नं तरलो हारमध्यगः //
363.m:
*Ākalpa*, *veśa*, and *nepathya* [mean costume or dress]; visible [ornamentation] arises from playful elegance.
*Cūḍāmaṇi* and *śiroratna* [mean crest-jewel]; *tarala* is the central gem of a necklace.

363.s:
karṇikā tālapatraṃ syāllambanaṃ syāllalantikā /
mañjīro nūpuraṃ pāde kiṅkiṇī kṣudraghaṇṭikā //
:p 289
363.d:
कर्णिका तालपत्रं स्याल्लम्बनं स्याल्ललन्तिका /
मञ्जीरो नूपुरं पादे किङ्किणी क्षुद्रघण्टिका //
:प् 289
363.m:
*Karṇikā* and *tālapatra* [mean ear-ornament]; *lambana* and *lalantikā* [mean pendant].
*Mañjīra* and *nūpura* [mean anklet] on the foot; *kiṅkiṇī* and *kṣudraghaṇṭikā* [mean small tinkling bell].
[Page 289]

363.s:
dairghyamāyāma ārohaḥ pariṇāho viśālatā /
paṭaccaraṃ jīrṇavastraṃ saṃvyānañcottarīyakam //
363.d:
दैर्घ्यमायाम आरोहः परिणाहो विशालता /
पटच्चरं जीर्णवस्त्रं संव्यानञ्चोत्तरीयकम् //
363.m:
*Dairghya*, *āyāma*, and *āroha* [mean length]; *pariṇāha* and *viśālatā* [mean circumference or breadth].
*Paṭaccara* and *jīrṇavastra* [mean rags]; *saṃvyāna* and *uttarīyaka* [mean upper garment].

363.s:
racanā syāt parispanda ābhogaḥ paripūrṇatā /
samudgakaḥ sampuṭakaḥ pratigrāhaḥ patadgrahaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nṛvargo nāma triṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha catuḥṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
brahmavargaḥ
363.d:
रचना स्यात् परिस्पन्द आभोगः परिपूर्णता /
समुद्गकः सम्पुटकः प्रतिग्राहः पतद्ग्रहः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नृवर्गो नाम त्रिषष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो
ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ चतुःषष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
ब्रह्मवर्गः
363.m:
*Racanā* and *parispanda* [mean arrangement or composition]; *ābhoga* and *paripūrṇatā* [mean fullness].
*Samudgaka* and *sampuṭaka* [mean casket or small round box]; *pratigrāha* and *patadgraha* [mean spittoon].
Thus ends the three hundred and sixty-third chapter, entitled "The Class of Human Beings," in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the three hundred and sixty-fourth chapter.
The Class of Brahmins

364.s:
agnir uvāca
vaṃśo 'nvavāyo gotraṃ syāt kulānyabhijanānvayau /
mantravyākhyākṛdācārya ādeṣṭā tvadhvare vratī //
364.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
वंशो ऽन्ववायो गोत्रं स्यात् कुलान्यभिजनान्वयौ /
मन्त्रव्याख्याकृदाचार्य आदेष्टा त्वध्वरे व्रती //
364.m:
Agni said:
*Vaṃśa*, *anvavāya*, *gotra*, *kula*, *abhijana*, and *anvaya* [mean lineage or family].
One who explains the mantras is an *ācārya*; the director in a sacrifice is a *vratin*.

364.s:
yaṣṭā ca yajamānaḥ syāt jñātvārambha upakramaḥ /
satīrthyāś caikaguravaḥ sabhyāḥ sāmājikās tathā //
364.d:
