यष्टा च यजमानः स्यात् ज्ञात्वारम्भ उपक्रमः /
सतीर्थ्याश् चैकगुरवः सभ्याः सामाजिकास् तथा //
364.m:
The sacrificer is the *yaṣṭṛ* and *yajamāna*; an undertaking commenced after knowing is an *upakrama*.
Fellow students under the same teacher are *satīrthya*; members of an assembly are *sabhya* and *sāmājika*.

364.s:
sabhāsadaḥ sabhāstārā ṛtvijo yājakāś ca te /
adhvaryūdgātṛhotāro yajuḥsāmargvidaḥ kramāt //
364.d:
सभासदः सभास्तारा ऋत्विजो याजकाश् च ते /
अध्वर्यूद्गातृहोतारो यजुःसामर्ग्विदः क्रमात् //
364.m:
[They are also called] *sabhāsad* and *sabhāstāra*; the sacrificial priests are *ṛtvij* and *yājaka*.
The *adhvaryu*, *udgātṛ*, and *hotṛ* are the knowers of the Yajus, Sāman, and Ṛg [Vedas] respectively.

364.s:
caṣālo yūpakaṭakaḥ same sthaṇḍilacatvare /
āmikṣā sā śṛtoṣṇe yā kṣīre syāddadhiyogataḥ //
364.d:
चषालो यूपकटकः समे स्थण्डिलचत्वरे /
आमिक्षा सा शृतोष्णे या क्षीरे स्याद्दधियोगतः //
364.m:
*Caṣāla* and *yūpakaṭaka* [denote the sacrificial post's ring]; *sthaṇḍila* and *catvara* are equivalent [for bare sacrificial ground].
*Āmikṣā* is that which is formed in hot boiled milk by the addition of curd.

364.s:
pṛṣadājyaṃ sadadhyājye paramānnantu pāyasam /
upākṛtaḥ paśurasau yo 'bhimantrya kratau hataḥ //
364.d:
पृषदाज्यं सदध्याज्ये परमान्नन्तु पायसम् /
उपाकृतः पशुरसौ यो ऽभिमन्त्र्य क्रतौ हतः //
364.m:
*Pṛṣadājya* is clarified butter mixed with curd; *paramānna* is milk-rice (*pāyasa*).
The sacrificial animal is called *upākṛta* when it is consecrated with mantras and killed in the rite.

364.s:
paramparākaṃ samanaṃ prokṣaṇañca badhārthakam /
:p 290
pūjā namasyāpicitiḥ saparyārcārhaṇāḥ samāḥ //
364.d:
परम्पराकं समनं प्रोक्षणञ्च बधार्थकम् /
:प् 290
पूजा नमस्यापिचितिः सपर्यार्चार्हणाः समाः //
364.m:
*Paramparāka*, *śamana*, and *prokṣaṇa* [denote ritual slaughter] for the purpose of killing.
[Page 290]
*Pūjā*, *namasyā*, *apaciti*, *saparyā*, *arcā*, and *arhaṇā* are synonymous [for worship].

364.s:
varivasyā tu śuśrūṣā paricaryāpyupāsanam /
niyamo bratamastrī taccopavāsādi puṇyakam //
364.d:
वरिवस्या तु शुश्रूषा परिचर्याप्युपासनम् /
नियमो ब्रतमस्त्री तच्चोपवासादि पुण्यकम् //
364.m:
*Varivasyā*, *śuśrūṣā*, *paricaryā*, and *upāsana* [denote service or attendance].
*Niyama* and *vrata* (non-feminine) are that meritorious act consisting of fasting and the like.

364.s:
mukhyaḥ syāt prathamaḥ kalpo 'nukalpastu tato 'dhamaḥ /
kalpe vidhikramau jñeyau vivekaḥ pṛthagātmatā //
364.d:
मुख्यः स्यात् प्रथमः कल्पो ऽनुकल्पस्तु ततो ऽधमः /
कल्पे विधिक्रमौ ज्ञेयौ विवेकः पृथगात्मता //
364.m:
The principal rule is the *mukhya* or primary alternative (*prathamakalpa*); an *anukalpa* is inferior to that.
In the rule (*kalpa*), order and injunction are to be known; *viveka* is distinct nature [or discernment].

364.s:
saṃskārapūrvaṃ grahaṇaṃ syādupākaraṇaṃ śruteḥ /
bhikṣuḥ parivrāṭ karmandī pārāśaryapi maskarī //
364.d:
संस्कारपूर्वं ग्रहणं स्यादुपाकरणं श्रुतेः /
भिक्षुः परिव्राट् कर्मन्दी पाराशर्यपि मस्करी //
364.m:
The reception of the scripture preceded by ritual consecration is *upākaraṇa*.
*Bhikṣu*, *parivrāj*, *karmandin*, *pārāśarin*, and *maskarin* [denote an ascetic mendicant].

364.s:
ṛṣayaḥ satyavacasaḥsnātakaścāplutavratī /
ye nirjitendriyagrāmā yatino yatayaś ca te //
364.d:
ऋषयः सत्यवचसःस्नातकश्चाप्लुतव्रती /
ये निर्जितेन्द्रियग्रामा यतिनो यतयश् च ते //
364.m:
*Ṛṣi*s are those whose speech is truth; a *snātaka* is one who has bathed after fulfilling his vows.
Those who have conquered the collection of the senses are *yatin*s and *yati*s.

364.s:
śarīrasādhanāpekṣaṃ nityaṃ yat karma tadyamaḥ /
niyamastu sa yat karmānityamāgantusādhanam /
syād brahmabhūyaṃ brahmatvaṃ brahmasāyujyamityapi //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe brahmavargo nāma
catuḥṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha pañcaṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
kṣatraviṭśūdravargāḥ
364.d:
शरीरसाधनापेक्षं नित्यं यत् कर्म तद्यमः /
नियमस्तु स यत् कर्मानित्यमागन्तुसाधनम् /
स्याद् ब्रह्मभूयं ब्रह्मत्वं ब्रह्मसायुज्यमित्यपि //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे ब्रह्मवर्गो नाम
चतुःषष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ पञ्चषष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
क्षत्रविट्शूद्रवर्गाः
364.m:
That daily duty which depends on bodily means is *yama*;
whereas *niyama* is that non-constant duty which requires external instruments.
*Brahmabhūya*, *brahmatva*, and *brahmasāyujya* [mean union with Brahman].
Thus ends the three hundred and sixty-fourth chapter, entitled "The Class of Brahmins," in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the three hundred and sixty-fifth chapter.
The Classes of Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras

365.s:
agnir uvāca
mūrdhābhiśikto rājanyo bāhujaḥ kṣatriyo virāṭ /
rājā tu praṇatāśeṣasāmantaḥ syādadhīśvaraḥ //
365.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
मूर्धाभिशिक्तो राजन्यो बाहुजः क्षत्रियो विराट् /
राजा तु प्रणताशेषसामन्तः स्यादधीश्वरः //
365.m:
Agni said:
An anointed sovereign is a *rājanya*, *bāhuja*, *kṣatriya*, and *virāj*.
A *rājā* to whom all feudatories have bowed down is a supreme lord (*adhīśvara*).

365.s:
cakravartī sārvabhaumo nṛpo 'nyo maṇḍaleśvaraḥ /
mantrī dhīsacivo 'mātyo mahāmātrāḥ pradhānakāḥ //
:p 291
365.d:
चक्रवर्ती सार्वभौमो नृपो ऽन्यो मण्डलेश्वरः /
मन्त्री धीसचिवो ऽमात्यो महामात्राः प्रधानकाः //
:प् 291
365.m:
An emperor is a *cakravartin* and *sārvabhauma*; another king is a *maṇḍaleśvara* [ruler of a province].
A *mantrin* is a counselor (*dhīsaciva*) and *amātya*; *mahāmātra*s are chief officers.
[Page 291]

365.s:
draṣṭari vyavahārāṇāṃ prāḍvivākākṣadarśakau /
bhaurikaḥ kanakādhyakṣo 'thādhyakṣādhikṛtau samau //
365.d:
द्रष्टरि व्यवहाराणां प्राड्विवाकाक्षदर्शकौ /
भौरिकः कनकाध्यक्षो ऽथाध्यक्षाधिकृतौ समौ //
365.m:
For an overseer of judicial affairs, [the terms are] *prāḍvivāka* and *akṣadarśaka*.
A *bhaurika* is a superintendent of gold; and *adhyakṣa* and *adhikṛta* are synonymous [for superintendent].

365.s:
antaḥpure tvadhikṛtaḥ syādantarvaṃśiko janaḥ /
sauvidallāḥ kañcukinaḥ sthāpatyāḥ sauvidāś ca te //
365.d:
अन्तःपुरे त्वधिकृतः स्यादन्तर्वंशिको जनः /
सौविदल्लाः कञ्चुकिनः स्थापत्याः सौविदाश् च ते //
365.m:
A person appointed over the inner apartments is an *antarvaṃśika*.
They are [also called] *sauvidalla*, *kañcukin*, *sthāpatya*, and *sauvida*.

365.s:
ṣaṇḍo varṣavarastulyāḥ sevakārthyanujīvinaḥ /
viṣayānantaro rājā śatrurmitramataḥ paraṃ //
365.d:
षण्डो वर्षवरस्तुल्याः सेवकार्थ्यनुजीविनः /
विषयानन्तरो राजा शत्रुर्मित्रमतः परं //
365.m:
*Ṣaṇḍa* and *varṣavara* are equivalent [for eunuchs]; *sevaka*, *arthin*, and *anujīvin* [mean attendants or dependants].
The king of the immediately adjacent territory is an enemy (*śatru*); one beyond him is an ally (*mitra*).

365.s:
udāsīnaḥ parataraḥ pārṣṇigrāhastu pṛṣṭhataḥ /
caraḥ sparśaḥ syātpraṇidhiruttaraḥ kāla āyatiḥ //
365.d:
उदासीनः परतरः पार्ष्णिग्राहस्तु पृष्ठतः /
चरः स्पर्शः स्यात्प्रणिधिरुत्तरः काल आयतिः //
365.m:
One situated farther beyond is neutral (*udāsīna*); an enemy in the rear is a *pārṣṇigrāha*.
A secret agent is a *cara*, *sparśa*, and *praṇidhi*; future time is *āyati*.

365.s:
tatkālastu tadātvaṃ syādudarkaḥ phalamuttaraṃ /
adṛṣṭaṃ vahnitoyādi dṛṣṭaṃ svaparacakrajam //
365.d:
तत्कालस्तु तदात्वं स्यादुदर्कः फलमुत्तरं /
अदृष्टं वह्नितोयादि दृष्टं स्वपरचक्रजम् //
365.m:
The present time is *tadātva*; *udarka* is future consequence.
Providential danger (*adṛṣṭa*) arises from fire, water, and the like; seen danger (*dṛṣṭa*) arises from one's own or an enemy's army.

365.s:
bhadrakumbhaḥ pūrṇakumbho bhṛṅgāraḥ kanakālukā /
prabhinno garjito māto vamathuḥ karaśīkaraḥ //
365.d:
भद्रकुम्भः पूर्णकुम्भो भृङ्गारः कनकालुका /
प्रभिन्नो गर्जितो मातो वमथुः करशीकरः //
365.m:
*Bhadrakumbha* and *pūrṇakumbha* [denote an auspicious full pitcher]; *bhṛṅgāra* and *kanakālukā* [denote a golden water-jar].
An elephant in rut is *prabhinna*, *garjita*, and *māta*; its nasal spray is *vamathu* and *karaśīkara*.

365.s:
striyāṃ śṛṇistvaṅkuśo 'strī paristomaḥ kutho dvayoḥ /
karṇīrathaḥ pravahaṇaṃ dolā preṅkhādikā striyāṃ //
365.d:
स्त्रियां शृणिस्त्वङ्कुशो ऽस्त्री परिस्तोमः कुथो द्वयोः /
कर्णीरथः प्रवहणं दोला प्रेङ्खादिका स्त्रियां //
365.m:
*Śṛṇi* (feminine) and *aṅkuśa* (non-feminine) [mean elephant-goad]; *paristoma* and *kutha* (both genders) [mean elephant-blanket].
*Karṇīratha* and *pravahaṇa* [mean litter or covered carriage]; *dolā* and *preṅkhā* (feminine) [mean swing or litter].

365.s:
ādhoraṇā hastipakā hastyārohā niṣādinaḥ /
bhaṭā yodhāś ca yoddhāraḥ kañcuko vāraṇo 'striyāṃ //
365.d:
आधोरणा हस्तिपका हस्त्यारोहा निषादिनः /
भटा योधाश् च योद्धारः कञ्चुको वारणो ऽस्त्रियां //
365.m:
*Ādhoraṇa*, *hastipaka*, *hastyāroha*, and *niṣādin* [mean elephant-driver].
*Bhaṭa*, *yodha*, and *yoddhṛ* [mean warrior or soldier]; *kañcuka* and *vāraṇa* (non-feminine) [mean armor or mail].

365.s:
śīrṣaṇyañca śirastre 'tha tanutraṃ varma daṃśanaṃ /
āmuktaḥ pratimuktaś ca pinaddhaścāpinaddhavat //
365.d:
शीर्षण्यञ्च शिरस्त्रे ऽथ तनुत्रं वर्म दंशनं /
आमुक्तः प्रतिमुक्तश् च पिनद्धश्चापिनद्धवत् //
365.m:
Helmet is *śīrṣaṇya* and *śirastra*; then body armor is *tanutra*, *varma*, and *daṃśana*;
*āmukta*, *pratimukta*, and *pinaddha* mean "accoutred" or "armored".

365.s:
vyūhastu balavinyāsaś cakrañcānīkamastriyāṃ /
ekebhaikarathā tryaśvāḥ pattiḥ pañcapadātikāḥ //
365.d:
व्यूहस्तु बलविन्यासश् चक्रञ्चानीकमस्त्रियां /
एकेभैकरथा त्र्यश्वाः पत्तिः पञ्चपदातिकाः //
365.m:
Battle array is *vyūha* and *balavinyāsa*; *cakra* and *anīka* are not feminine.
A *patti* consists of one elephant, one chariot, three horses, and five foot-soldiers.

365.s:
pattyaṅgaistriguṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ kramādākhyā yathottaraṃ /
senāmukhaṃ gulmagaṇau vāhinī pṛtanā camūḥ //
365.d:
पत्त्यङ्गैस्त्रिगुणैः सर्वैः क्रमादाख्या यथोत्तरं /
सेनामुखं गुल्मगणौ वाहिनी पृतना चमूः //
365.m:
With all components of a *patti* tripled in successive order, the names are:
*senāmukha*, *gulma*, *gaṇa*, *vāhinī*, *pṛtanā*, *camū*,

365.s:
anīkinī daśānīkinyo 'kṣohiṇyo gajādibhiḥ /
:p 292
dhanuḥ kodaṇḍa+iṣvāsau koṭirasyāṭanī smṛtā //
365.d:
अनीकिनी दशानीकिन्यो ऽक्षोहिण्यो गजादिभिः /
:प् 292
धनुः कोदण्ड+इष्वासौ कोटिरस्याटनी स्मृता //
365.m:
and *anīkinī*. Ten *anīkinī*s constitute an *akṣauhiṇī* with elephants and the rest.
[page 292]
A bow is *dhanus*, *kodaṇḍa*, and *iṣvāsa*; its notched tip is known as *aṭanī*.

365.s:
nastakastu dhanurmadhyaṃ maurvī jyā śiñjinī guṇaḥ /
pṛṣatkavāṇaviśikhā ajihmagakhagāśugāḥ //
365.d:
नस्तकस्तु धनुर्मध्यं मौर्वी ज्या शिञ्जिनी गुणः /
पृषत्कवाणविशिखा अजिह्मगखगाशुगाः //
365.m:
The middle of the bow is *nastaka*; bowstring is *maurvī*, *jyā*, *śiñjinī*, and *guṇa*.
Arrow is *pṛṣatka*, *bāṇa*, *viśikha*, *ajihmaga*, *khaga*, and *āśuga*.

365.s:
tūṇopāsaṅgatūṇīraniṣaṅgā iṣudhirdvayoḥ /
asirṛṣṭiś ca nistriṃśaḥ karavālaḥ kṛpālaḥkṛpāṇavat //
365.d:
तूणोपासङ्गतूणीरनिषङ्गा इषुधिर्द्वयोः /
असिरृष्टिश् च निस्त्रिंशः करवालः कृपालःकृपाणवत् //
365.m:
Quiver is *tūṇa*, *upāsaṅga*, *tūṇīra*, and *niṣaṅga*; *iṣudhi* occurs in both [masculine and feminine].
A sword is *asi*, *ṛṣṭi*, *nistriṃśa*, *karavāla*, and *kṛpāla*, like *kṛpāṇa*.

365.s:
saruḥ khaḍgasya suṣṭau syādīlī tu karapālikā /
dvayoḥ kuṭhāraḥ sudhitiḥ churikā cāsiputrikā //
365.d:
सरुः खड्गस्य सुष्टौ स्यादीली तु करपालिका /
द्वयोः कुठारः सुधितिः छुरिका चासिपुत्रिका //
365.m:
The hilt of a sword is *tsaru*; a dagger is *īlī* and *karapālikā*;
an axe is *kuṭhāra* and *svadhiti* in both [masculine and feminine]; and a small knife is *churikā* and *asiputrikā*.

365.s:
prāsastu kunto vijñeyaḥ sarvalā tomaro 'striyāṃ /
vaitālikā bodhakarā māgadhā vandinastutau //
365.d:
प्रासस्तु कुन्तो विज्ञेयः सर्वला तोमरो ऽस्त्रियां /
वैतालिका बोधकरा मागधा वन्दिनस्तुतौ //
365.m:
A dart is understood to be *prāsa* and *kunta*; an iron club is *sarvalā* and *tomara*, not feminine.
Bards are *vaitālika*s, *bodhakara*s, *māgadha*s, and *vandin*s in eulogy.

365.s:
saṃśaptakāstu samayātsaṅgrāmādanivartinaḥ /
patākā vaijayantī syātketanaṃ dhajamistriyāṃ //
365.d:
संशप्तकास्तु समयात्सङ्ग्रामादनिवर्तिनः /
पताका वैजयन्ती स्यात्केतनं धजमिस्त्रियां //
365.m:
*Saṃśaptaka*s are those who, by vow, do not retreat from battle.
A flag is *patākā*, *vaijayantī*, *ketana*, and *dhvaja*, not feminine.

365.s:
ahaṃ pūrvamahaṃ pūrvamityahaṃpūrvikā striyāṃ /
ahamahamikā sāsyādyo 'haṅkāraḥ parasparam //
365.d:
अहं पूर्वमहं पूर्वमित्यहंपूर्विका स्त्रियां /
अहमहमिका सास्याद्यो ऽहङ्कारः परस्परम् //
365.m:
The cry "I first, I first!" is *ahaṃpūrvikā* in the feminine;
mutual rivalry is *ahamahamiyā*, which is [a form of] egotism.

365.s:
śaktiḥ parākramaḥ prāṇaḥ śauryaṃ sthānasahobalaṃ /
mūrchā tu kaśmalaṃ moho 'pyavarmaddastu pīḍanaṃ //
365.d:
शक्तिः पराक्रमः प्राणः शौर्यं स्थानसहोबलं /
मूर्छा तु कश्मलं मोहो ऽप्यवर्मद्दस्तु पीडनं //
365.m:
Power is *śakti*, *parākrama*, *prāṇa*, *śaurya*, *sthāman*, *sahas*, and *bala*.
Fainting is *mūrcchā*, *kaśmala*, and *moha*; oppression is *avamardana* and *pīḍana*.

365.s:
abhyavaskandanantvabhyāsādanaṃ vijayo jayaḥ /
nirvāsanaṃ saṃjñapanaṃ sāraṇaṃ pratighātanaṃ //
365.d:
अभ्यवस्कन्दनन्त्वभ्यासादनं विजयो जयः /
निर्वासनं संज्ञपनं सारणं प्रतिघातनं //
365.m:
Assault is *abhyavaskandana* and *abhyāsādana*; victory is *vijaya* and *jaya*.
Banishing or slaying is *nirvāsana*, *saṃjñapana*, *sāraṇa*, and *pratighātana*.

365.s:
syātpañcatā kāladharmo diṣṭāntaḥ pralayo 'tyayaḥ /
viśo bhūmispṛṣo vaiśyā vṛttirvartanajīvane //
365.d:
स्यात्पञ्चता कालधर्मो दिष्टान्तः प्रलयो ऽत्ययः /
विशो भूमिस्पृषो वैश्या वृत्तिर्वर्तनजीवने //
365.m:
Death is *pañcatā*, *kāladharma*, *diṣṭānta*, *pralaya*, and *atyaya*.
*Viś*, *bhūmispṛś*, and *vaiśya* [denote that class]; livelihood is *vṛtti*, *vartana*, and *jīvana*.

365.s:
kṛṣyādivṛttayo jñeyāḥ kusīdaṃ vṛddhijīvikā /
uddharo 'rthaprayogaḥ syātkaṇiśaṃ sasyamañjarī //
365.d:
कृष्यादिवृत्तयो ज्ञेयाः कुसीदं वृद्धिजीविका /
उद्धरो ऽर्थप्रयोगः स्यात्कणिशं सस्यमञ्जरी //
365.m:
Agriculture and so forth are understood as means of livelihood; money-lending is *kusīda* and living on interest;
lending of money is *uddhara* and *arthaprayoga*; an ear of grain is *kaṇiśa* and *sasyamañjarī*.

365.s:
kiṃśāruḥ sasyaśūkaṃ syāt stambo gutsastṛṇādinaḥ /
dhāmyaṃ vrīhiḥ stambakariḥ kaḍaṅgaro vupaṃ smṛtaṃ //
:p 293
365.d:
किंशारुः सस्यशूकं स्यात् स्तम्बो गुत्सस्तृणादिनः /
धाम्यं व्रीहिः स्तम्बकरिः कडङ्गरो वुपं स्मृतं //
:प् 293
365.m:
The beard of grain is *kiṃśāru* and *sasyaśūka*; a clump of grass or the like is *stamba* and *gutsa*.
Grain is *dhānya* and *vrīhi*; what forms clumps is *stambakari*; straw or fodder is recorded as *kaḍaṅgara* and *busa*.
[page 293]

365.s:
māṣādayaḥ śamīdhānye śukadhānye yavādayaḥ /
tṛṇadhānyāni nīvārāḥ śūrpaṃ prasphoṭanaṃ smṛtaṃ //
365.d:
माषादयः शमीधान्ये शुकधान्ये यवादयः /
तृणधान्यानि नीवाराः शूर्पं प्रस्फोटनं स्मृतं //
365.m:
*Māṣa* beans and the like are legume grains; barley and the like are bearded grains;
wild grains are *nīvāra*s; a winnowing basket is recorded as *śūrpa* and *prasphoṭana*.

365.s:
syūtaprasevau kaṇḍolapiṭau kaṭakiniñjakau /
samānau rasavatyāntu pākasthānamahānase //
365.d:
स्यूतप्रसेवौ कण्डोलपिटौ कटकिनिञ्जकौ /
समानौ रसवत्यान्तु पाकस्थानमहानसे //
365.m:
*Syūta* and *praseva* [mean sack]; *kaṇḍola* and *piṭa* [mean basket]; *kaṭa* and *kiliñja* [mean mat];
synonymous for kitchen are *rasavatī*, *pākasthāna*, and *mahānasa*.

365.s:
paurogavastadadhyakṣaḥ sūpakārāstu vallavāḥ /
ārālikā āndhasikāḥ sūdā audanikā guṇāḥ //
365.d:
पौरोगवस्तदध्यक्षः सूपकारास्तु वल्लवाः /
आरालिका आन्धसिकाः सूदा औदनिका गुणाः //
365.m:
The superintendent thereof is *paurogava*; cooks are *sūpakāra*s and *vallava*s;
*ārālika*s, *āndhasika*s, *sūda*s, and *audanika*s are [their] categories.

365.s:
klīve 'mbarīṣaṃ bhrāṣṭo nā karkaryālurgalantikā /
āliñjaraḥ syānmaṇikaṃ suṣavī kṛṣajīrake //
365.d:
क्लीवे ऽम्बरीषं भ्राष्टो ना कर्कर्यालुर्गलन्तिका /
आलिञ्जरः स्यान्मणिकं सुषवी कृषजीरके //
365.m:
A frying pan is neuter *ambarīṣa* and masculine *bhrāṣṭra*; a water-pitcher is *karkarī*, *ālu*, and *galantikā*;
a large earthen jar is *āliñjara* and *maṇika*; black cumin is *suṣavī* and *kṛṣṇajīraka*.

365.s:
āranālastu kulmāṣaṃ vāhlīkaṃ hiṅgu rāmaṭhaṃ /
niśā haridrā pītā strī khaṇḍe matsyaṇḍiphāṇite //
365.d:
आरनालस्तु कुल्माषं वाह्लीकं हिङ्गु रामठं /
निशा हरिद्रा पीता स्त्री खण्डे मत्स्यण्डिफाणिते //
365.m:
Sour gruel is *āranāla* and *kulmāṣa*; asafoetida is *bāhlīka*, *hiṅgu*, and *rāmaṭha*;
turmeric is feminine *niśā*, *haridrā*, and *pītā*; candied sugar is *matsyaṇḍī* and *phāṇita*.

365.s:
kūrcikā kṣiravikṛtiḥ snigdhaṃ masṛṇacikkaṇaṃ /
pṛthukaḥ syāccipiṭako dhānā bhraṣṭayavāstriyaḥ //
365.d:
कूर्चिका क्षिरविकृतिः स्निग्धं मसृणचिक्कणं /
पृथुकः स्याच्चिपिटको धाना भ्रष्टयवास्त्रियः //
365.m:
Inspissated milk is *kūrcikā*, an alteration of milk; unctuous is *snigdha*, *masṛṇa*, and *cikkaṇa*;
flattened rice is *pṛthuka* and *cipiṭaka*; parched barley grains are feminine *dhānā*s.

365.s:
jemanaṃ lepa āhāro māheyī saurabhī ca gauḥ /
yugādīnāñca boḍhāro yugyaprasāṅgyaśāṭakāḥ //
365.d:
जेमनं लेप आहारो माहेयी सौरभी च गौः /
युगादीनाञ्च बोढारो युग्यप्रसाङ्ग्यशाटकाः //
365.m:
Eating or food is *jemana*, *lepa*, and *āhāra*; a cow is *māheyī* and *saurabhī*;
and beasts of burden for the yoke and the like are *yugya*, *prāsaṅgya*, and *śākaṭa*.

365.s:
cirasūtā vaṣkayaṇī dhenuḥ syānnavasūtikā /
sandhinī vṛṣabhākrāntā vehadgarbhopaghātinī //
365.d:
चिरसूता वष्कयणी धेनुः स्यान्नवसूतिका /
सन्धिनी वृषभाक्रान्ता वेहद्गर्भोपघातिनी //
365.m:
A cow that calved long ago is *vaṣkayaṇī*; one recently calved is *dhenu*;
a cow seeking the bull is *sandhinī*; a cow that miscarries is *vehat*.

365.s:
paṇyājīvo hy āpaṇiko nyāsaścopanidhiḥ pumān /
vipaṇo vikrayaḥ saṅkhyā saṅkhyeye hy ādaśa triṣu //
365.d:
पण्याजीवो ह्य् आपणिको न्यासश्चोपनिधिः पुमान् /
विपणो विक्रयः सङ्ख्या सङ्ख्येये ह्य् आदश त्रिषु //
365.m:
A trader living by merchandise is *āpaṇika*; a deposit is masculine *nyāsa* and *upanidhi*;
sale is *vipaṇa* and *vikraya*; numbers up to ten are used in all three genders for the thing numbered.

365.s:
viṃśatyādyāḥ sadaikatve sarvāḥ saṃkhyeyasaṃkhyayoḥ /
saṃkhyārthe dvibahutve stastāsu cānavateḥ striyaḥ //
365.d:
विंशत्याद्याः सदैकत्वे सर्वाः संख्येयसंख्ययोः /
संख्यार्थे द्विबहुत्वे स्तस्तासु चानवतेः स्त्रियः //
365.m:
From twenty onwards, all are always in the singular, both for the number and the numbered;
in the sense of the number, they can be dual or plural; among these, up to ninety, they are feminine.

365.s:
paṅkteḥ śatasahasrādi kramāddaśaguṇottaraṃ /
mānantu lāṅguliprasthair guñjāḥ pañcādyamāṣakaḥ //
365.d:
पङ्क्तेः शतसहस्रादि क्रमाद्दशगुणोत्तरं /
मानन्तु लाङ्गुलिप्रस्थैर् गुञ्जाः पञ्चाद्यमाषकः //
365.m:
From ten (*paṅkti*), hundred, thousand, and so forth increase successively tenfold.
As for measures, by *guñjā*s, five are the first weight, a *māṣaka*.

365.s:
te ṣoḍaśākṣaḥ karṣo 'strī palaṃ karṣacatuṣṭayam /
:p 294
suvarṇavistau hemno 'kṣe kuruvistastu tatpale //
365.d:
ते षोडशाक्षः कर्षो ऽस्त्री पलं कर्षचतुष्टयम् /
:प् 294
सुवर्णविस्तौ हेम्नो ऽक्षे कुरुविस्तस्तु तत्पले //
365.m:
Sixteen of these are an *akṣa* and *karṣa*, not feminine; a *pala* is four *karṣa*s.
[page 294]
*Suvarṇa* and *bista* denote an *akṣa* weight of gold; a *kuruvista* denotes a *pala* thereof.

365.s:
tulā striyāṃ palaśataṃ bhāraḥ syādviṃśatistulāḥ /
kārṣāpaṇaḥ kārṣikaḥ syāt kārṣike tāmrike paṇaḥ //
365.d:
तुला स्त्रियां पलशतं भारः स्याद्विंशतिस्तुलाः /
कार्षापणः कार्षिकः स्यात् कार्षिके ताम्रिके पणः //
365.m:
A *tulā* is feminine, equal to a hundred *pala*s; a *bhāra* is twenty *tulā*s.
A *kārṣāpaṇa* is of a *karṣa* weight; a *karṣa* weight in copper is a *paṇa*.

365.s:
dravyaṃ vittaṃ svāpateyaṃ rikthamṛthakthaṃ dhanaṃ vasu /
rītiḥ striyāmārakūṭo na striyāmatha tāmrakam //
365.d:
द्रव्यं वित्तं स्वापतेयं रिक्थमृथक्थं धनं वसु /
रीतिः स्त्रियामारकूटो न स्त्रियामथ ताम्रकम् //
365.m:
Property and wealth are *dravya*, *vitta*, *svāpateya*, *riktha*, *ṛktha*, *dhana*, and *vasu*.
Brass is feminine *rīti* and non-feminine *ārakūṭa*; then copper is *tāmra*,

365.s:
śulvamaudumbaraṃ lauhe tīkṣṇaṃ kālāṃyasāyasī /
kṣāraḥ kāco 'tha capalo rasaḥ sūtaś ca pārade //
365.d:
शुल्वमौदुम्बरं लौहे तीक्ष्णं कालांयसायसी /
क्षारः काचो ऽथ चपलो रसः सूतश् च पारदे //
365.m:
*śulva*, and *audumbara*; among irons, steel is *tīkṣṇa*, *kālāyasa*, and *āyasa*.
Alkali is *kṣāra*; glass is *kāca*; then quicksilver is *capala*, *rasa*, *sūta*, and *pārada*.

365.s:
garalaṃ māhiṣaṃ śṛṅgaṃ trapusīsakapiccaṭaṃ /
hiṇḍīro 'bdhikaphaḥ pheṇo madhūcchiṣṭantu sikthakam //
365.d:
गरलं माहिषं शृङ्गं त्रपुसीसकपिच्चटं /
हिण्डीरो ऽब्धिकफः फेणो मधूच्छिष्टन्तु सिक्थकम् //
365.m:
Venom is *garala*; a buffalo horn is *māhiṣa śṛṅga*; tin and lead are *trapu*, *sīsaka*, and *piccaṭa*;
cuttlefish bone is *hiṇḍīra*, *abdhikapha*, and *phena*; and beeswax is *sikthaka*.

365.s:
raṅgavaṅge picusthūlo kūlaṭī tu manaḥśilā /
yavakṣāraś ca pākyaḥ syāt tvakkṣīrā vaṃśalocanāḥ //
365.d:
रङ्गवङ्गे पिचुस्थूलो कूलटी तु मनःशिला /
यवक्षारश् च पाक्यः स्यात् त्वक्क्षीरा वंशलोचनाः //
365.m:
Tin is *raṅga* and *vaṅga*; coarse cotton is *picu*; realgar is *manaḥśilā* and *kūlaṭī*;
potash is *yavakṣāra* and *pākya*; bamboo manna is *tvakkṣīrā* and *vaṃśalocanā*.

365.s:
vṛṣalā jadhanyajāḥ śūdrāścāṇḍālāntyāś caśaṅkarāḥ /
kāruḥ śilpī saṃhataistair dvayoḥ śreṇiḥ sajātibhiḥ //
365.d:
वृषला जधन्यजाः शूद्राश्चाण्डालान्त्याश् चशङ्कराः /
कारुः शिल्पी संहतैस्तैर् द्वयोः श्रेणिः सजातिभिः //
365.m:
Low-born people are *vṛṣala*s, *jaghanyaja*s, and *śūdra*s; outcastes are *caṇḍāla*s, *antya*s, and *saṅkara*s.
An artisan is *kāru* and *śilpin*; an association of such craftsmen of the same class is a *śreṇi* in two genders.

365.s:
raṅgājīvaścitrakarastvaṣṭā takṣā ca vardhakiḥ /
nāḍindhamaḥ svarṇakāro nāpitāntāvasāyinaḥ //
365.d:
रङ्गाजीवश्चित्रकरस्त्वष्टा तक्षा च वर्धकिः /
नाडिन्धमः स्वर्णकारो नापितान्तावसायिनः //
365.m:
A painter is *raṅgājīva* and *citrakara*; a carpenter is *tvaṣṭṛ*, *takṣan*, and *vardhaki*;
a goldsmith is *nāḍindhama* and *svarṇakāra*; barbers are *antāvasāyin*s.

365.s:
jāvālaḥ syādajājīvo devājīvastu devalaḥ /
jāyājīvastu śailūṣā bhṛtako bhṛtibhuktathā //
365.d:
जावालः स्यादजाजीवो देवाजीवस्तु देवलः /
जायाजीवस्तु शैलूषा भृतको भृतिभुक्तथा //
365.m:
A goat-herd is *jāvāla*; one who lives by serving idols is a *devala*;
an actor living by his wife is a *śailūṣa*; a servant or wage-earner is *bhṛtaka* and *bhṛtibhuk*.

365.s:
vivarṇaḥ pāmaro nīcaḥ prākṛtaś ca pṛthagjanaḥ /
vihīnopasado jālmo bhṛtye dāseraceṭakāḥ //
365.d:
विवर्णः पामरो नीचः प्राकृतश् च पृथग्जनः /
विहीनोपसदो जाल्मो भृत्ये दासेरचेटकाः //
365.m:
Base and vulgar men are *vivarṇa*, *pāmara*, *nīca*, *prākṛta*, *pṛthagjana*,
*vihīna*, *upasada*, and *jālma*; for servant, the words are *dāsera* and *ceṭaka*.

365.s:
paṭustu peśalo dakṣo mṛgayurlubdhakaḥ smṛtaḥ /
cāṇḍālastu divākīrtiḥ pustaṃ lepyādikarmaṇi //
365.d:
पटुस्तु पेशलो दक्षो मृगयुर्लुब्धकः स्मृतः /
चाण्डालस्तु दिवाकीर्तिः पुस्तं लेप्यादिकर्मणि //
365.m:
Clever is *paṭu*, *peśala*, and *dakṣa*; a hunter is recorded as *mṛgayu* and *lubdhaka*;
a *caṇḍāla* is *divākīrti*; modelled work in plaster and the like is *pusta*.

365.s:
pañcālikā putrikā syādvarkarastaruṇaḥ paśuḥ /
mañjūṣā peṭakaḥ peḍā tulyasādhāraṇau samau /
:p 295
pratimā syāt pratikṛtirvargā brahmādayaḥ smṛtāḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe kṣatraviṭśīdravargā māma
pañcaṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha ṣaṭṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sāmānyanāmaliṅgāni
365.d:
पञ्चालिका पुत्रिका स्याद्वर्करस्तरुणः पशुः /
मञ्जूषा पेटकः पेडा तुल्यसाधारणौ समौ /
:प् 295
प्रतिमा स्यात् प्रतिकृतिर्वर्गा ब्रह्मादयः स्मृताः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे क्षत्रविट्शीद्रवर्गा माम
पञ्चषष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ षट्षष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
सामान्यनामलिङ्गानि
365.m:
A doll or puppet is *pañcālikā* and *putrikā*; a young animal is *varkara*;
a chest or box is *mañjūṣā*, *peṭaka*, and *peḍā*; *tulya*, *sādhāraṇa*, and *sama* mean equal.
[page 295]
An image or likeness is *pratimā* and *pratikṛti*; the classes of words beginning with Brahmā have thus been taught.
Thus ends the three hundred and sixty-fifth chapter, named "Classes of Words on Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras", in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the three hundred and sixty-sixth chapter:
Common Nouns and Genders.

366.s:
agnir uvāca
sāmānyāny atha vakṣyāmi nāmaliṅgāni tacchṛṇu /
sukṛtī puṇyavān dhnayo mahecchastu mahāśayaḥ //
366.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
सामान्यान्य् अथ वक्ष्यामि नामलिङ्गानि तच्छृणु /
सुकृती पुण्यवान् ध्नयो महेच्छस्तु महाशयः //
366.m:
Agni said:
I shall now declare the common nouns and their genders; listen to that.
One who has done good deeds is *sukṛtin*, *puṇyavat*, and *dhanya*; magnanimous is *maheccha* and *mahāśaya*.

366.s:
pravīṇanipuṇābhijñavijñaniṣṇātaśikṣitāḥ /
syurvadānyasthūlalakṣadānaśauṇḍā bahuprade //
366.d:
प्रवीणनिपुणाभिज्ञविज्ञनिष्णातशिक्षिताः /
स्युर्वदान्यस्थूललक्षदानशौण्डा बहुप्रदे //
366.m:
*Pravīṇa*, *nipuṇa*, *abhijña*, *vijña*, *niṣṇāta*, and *śikṣita* [mean skilled].
For one who gives abundantly, the words are *vadānya*, *sthūlalakṣa*, and *dānaśauṇḍa*.

366.s:
kṛtī kṛtajñaḥ kuśala āsaktodyukta utsukaḥ /
ibhya āḍhyaḥ parivṛḍho hy adhibhūrnāyako 'dhipaḥ //
366.d:
कृती कृतज्ञः कुशल आसक्तोद्युक्त उत्सुकः /
इभ्य आढ्यः परिवृढो ह्य् अधिभूर्नायको ऽधिपः //
366.m:
Competent is *kṛtin*; grateful is *kṛtajña*; clever is *kuśala*; devoted and zealous is *āsakta*, *udyukta*, and *utsuka*;
wealthy is *ibhya* and *āḍhya*; a lord or leader is *parivṛḍha*, *adhibhū*, *nāyaka*, and *adhipa*.

366.s:
lakṣmīvān lakṣmaṇaḥ śrīlaḥ svatantraḥ svairyapāvṛtaḥ /
khalapūḥ syādvahukaro dīrghasūtraścirakriyaḥ //
366.d:
लक्ष्मीवान् लक्ष्मणः श्रीलः स्वतन्त्रः स्वैर्यपावृतः /
खलपूः स्याद्वहुकरो दीर्घसूत्रश्चिरक्रियः //
366.m:
Fortunate is *lakṣmīvat*, *lakṣmaṇa*, and *śrīla*; independent is *svatantra*, *svairin*, and *apāvṛta*;
a scavenger is *khalapū* and *bahukara*; procrastinating is *dīrghasūtra* and *cirakriya*.

366.s:
jālmo 'samīkṣyakārī syāt kuṇṭho mandaḥ kriyāsu yaḥ /
karmaśūraḥ karmaṭhaḥ syādbhakṣako ghasmaro 'dmaraḥ //
366.d:
जाल्मो ऽसमीक्ष्यकारी स्यात् कुण्ठो मन्दः क्रियासु यः /
कर्मशूरः कर्मठः स्याद्भक्षको घस्मरो ऽद्मरः //
366.m:
*Jālma* is one who acts without reflection; *kuṇṭha* and *manda* mean dull in actions;
one skilled in action is *karmaśūra* and *karmaṭha*; voracious is *bhakṣaka*, *ghasmara*, and *admara*.

366.s:
lolupo gardhalo gṛdhrurvinītapraśritau tathā /
dhṛṣṭe dhṛṣṇurviyātaś ca nibhṛtaḥ pratibhānvite //
366.d:
लोलुपो गर्धलो गृध्रुर्विनीतप्रश्रितौ तथा /
धृष्टे धृष्णुर्वियातश् च निभृतः प्रतिभान्विते //
366.m:
Covetous is *lolupa*, *gardhala*, and *gṛdhnu*; humble is *vinīta* and *praśrita*;
for bold, the words are *dhṛṣṭa*, *dhṛṣṇu*, and *viyāta*; modest or ready-witted is *nibhṛta* and *pratibhānvita*.

366.s:
pragalbho bhīruko bhīrurvandārurabhivādake /
bhūṣṇurbhaviṣṇurbhavitā jñātā vidurabindukau //
366.d:
प्रगल्भो भीरुको भीरुर्वन्दारुरभिवादके /
भूष्णुर्भविष्णुर्भविता ज्ञाता विदुरबिन्दुकौ //
366.m: Bold is [denoted by] *pragalbha*; cowardly by *bhīruka* and *bhīru*; saluting by *vandāru* and *abhivādaka*; / thriving by *bhūṣṇu*, *bhaviṣṇu*, and *bhavitā*; knowing by *jñātṛ*, *vidura*, and *binduka*.

366.s:
mattaśauṇḍotkaṭakṣīvāś caṇḍastvatyantakopanaḥ /
:p 296
devānañcati devadryaṅviśvadryaṅviśvagañcati //
366.d:
मत्तशौण्डोत्कटक्षीवाश् चण्डस्त्वत्यन्तकोपनः /
:प् 296
देवानञ्चति देवद्र्यङ्विश्वद्र्यङ्विश्वगञ्चति //
366.m:
Intoxicated [is expressed by] *matta*, *śauṇḍa*, *utkaṭa*, and *kṣība*; while extremely wrathful is *caṇḍa*.
[Page 296]
One who turns toward the gods is *devadryañc*; one who turns everywhere is *viśvadryañc*.

366.s:
yaḥ sahāñcati sa sadhryaṅ sa tiryaṅ yastiro 'ñcati /
vācoyuktiḥ paṭurvāgmī vāvadūkaś ca vaktari //
366.d:
यः सहाञ्चति स सध्र्यङ् स तिर्यङ् यस्तिरो ऽञ्चति /
वाचोयुक्तिः पटुर्वाग्मी वावदूकश् च वक्तरि //
366.m: He who moves together is *sadhryañc*; he who moves crookedly is *tiryañc*. / *Vācoyukti*, *paṭu*, *vāgmin*, and *vāvadūka* denote a speaker [who is eloquent].

366.s:
syājjalpakastu vācālo vācāṭo bahugarhyavāk /
apadhvasto dhikkṛtaḥ syādbaddhe kīlitasaṃyatau //
366.d:
स्याज्जल्पकस्तु वाचालो वाचाटो बहुगर्ह्यवाक् /
अपध्वस्तो धिक्कृतः स्याद्बद्धे कीलितसंयतौ //
366.m: A babbler, speaking much contemptible speech, is *jalpaka*, *vācāla*, and *vācāṭa*. / Despised is *apadhvasta* and *dhikkṛta*; bound is *kīlita* and *saṃyata*.

366.s:
varaṇaḥ śabdano nāndīvādī nānvīkaraḥ samāḥ /
vyasanārtoparakrau dvau baddhe kīlitasaṃyatau(1) //
366.d:
वरणः शब्दनो नान्दीवादी नान्वीकरः समाः /
व्यसनार्तोपरक्रौ द्वौ बद्धे कीलितसंयतौ(1) //
366.m: *Varaṇa*, *śabdana*, *nāndīvādī*, and *nānvīkara* are synonymous. / Afflicted with calamity is *uparakta*; bound is *kīlita* and *saṃyata*.

366.s:
vihistavyākulau tulyau nṛśaṃsakrūraghātukāḥ /
pāpo dhūrto vañcakaḥ syānmūrkhe vaidehavāliśau //
366.d:
विहिस्तव्याकुलौ तुल्यौ नृशंसक्रूरघातुकाः /
पापो धूर्तो वञ्चकः स्यान्मूर्खे वैदेहवालिशौ //
366.m: *Vihista* and *vyākula* are equal; cruel, harsh, and destructive are *nṛśaṃsa*, *krūra*, and *ghātuka*. / Sinful, rogue, and deceiver are *pāpa*, *dhūrta*, and *vañcaka*; foolish are *vaideha* and *bāliśa*.

366.s:
kadarye kṛpaṇakṣudrau mārgaṇo yācakārthinau /
ahaṅkāravānahaṃyuḥ syācchubhaṃyustu śubhānvitaḥ //
366.d:
कदर्ये कृपणक्षुद्रौ मार्गणो याचकार्थिनौ /
अहङ्कारवानहंयुः स्याच्छुभंयुस्तु शुभान्वितः //
366.m: Miserly are *kadarya*, *kṛpaṇa*, and *kṣudra*; a petitioner is *mārgaṇa*, *yācaka*, and *arthin*. / One possessing egotism is *ahaṃyu*; one endowed with auspiciousness is *śubhaṃyu*.

366.s:
kāntaṃ manoramaṃ rucyaṃ hṛdyābhīṣṭe hy abhīpsite /
asāraṃ phalgu śūnyaṃ vai mukhyavaryavareṇyakāḥ //
366.d:
कान्तं मनोरमं रुच्यं हृद्याभीष्टे ह्य् अभीप्सिते /
असारं फल्गु शून्यं वै मुख्यवर्यवरेण्यकाः //
366.m: Pleasing and charming are *kānta*, *manorama*, and *rucya*; desired and wished-for are *hṛdya*, *abhīṣṭa*, and *abhīpsita*. / Unsubstantial is *asāra*, *phalgu*, and *śūnya*; foremost and best are *mukhya*, *varya*, and *vareṇya*.

366.s:
śreyān śreṣṭhaḥ puṣkalaḥ syātprāgryāgryagrīyamagrimaṃ /
vaḍroru vipulaṃ pīnapīvnī tu sthūlapīvare //
366.d:
श्रेयान् श्रेष्ठः पुष्कलः स्यात्प्राग्र्याग्र्यग्रीयमग्रिमं /
वड्रोरु विपुलं पीनपीव्नी तु स्थूलपीवरे //
366.m: Better and superior is *śreyas*, *śreṣṭha*, and *puṣkala*; first and foremost are *prāgrya*, *agrya*, *agrīya*, and *agrima*. / Great and extensive are *vaḍra*, *uru*, and *vipula*; fat and stout are *pīna*, *pīvan*, *sthūla*, and *pīvara*.

366.s:
stokālpakṣullakāḥ sūkṣmaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ dabhraṃkṛśantanu /
mātrākuṭīlavakaṇā bhūyiṣṭhaṃ puruhaṃ puru //
366.d:
स्तोकाल्पक्षुल्लकाः सूक्ष्मं श्लक्ष्णं दभ्रंकृशन्तनु /
मात्राकुटीलवकणा भूयिष्ठं पुरुहं पुरु //
366.m: A little and small are *stoka*, *alpa*, and *kṣullaka*; fine, smooth, scanty, thin, and slender are *sūkṣma*, *ślakṣṇa*, *dabhra*, *kṛśa*, and *tanu*. / A measure, particle, and drop are *mātrā*, *kuṭī*, *lava*, and *kaṇa*; abundant and much are *bhūyiṣṭha*, *puruha*, and *puru*.

366.s:
akhaṇḍaṃ pūrṇasakalamupakaṇṭhāntikābhitaḥ /
samīpe sannidhābhyāsau nediṣṭaṃ susamīpakaṃ //
366.d:
अखण्डं पूर्णसकलमुपकण्ठान्तिकाभितः /
समीपे सन्निधाभ्यासौ नेदिष्टं सुसमीपकं //
366.m: Unbroken and complete is *akhaṇḍa*, *pūrṇa*, and *sakala*; neighboring, near, and on both sides are *upakaṇṭha*, *antika*, and *abhitas*. / Near are *samīpa*, *sannidhā*, and *abhyāsa*; closest is *nediṣṭha* and *susamīpaka*.

366.s:
sudūre tu daviṣṭhaṃ syādvṛttaṃ nistalavartule /
uccaprāṃśūnnatodagrā dhruvo nityaḥ sanātanaḥ //
366.d:
सुदूरे तु दविष्ठं स्याद्वृत्तं निस्तलवर्तुले /
उच्चप्रांशून्नतोदग्रा ध्रुवो नित्यः सनातनः //
366.m: Very far is *daviṣṭha*; round is *vṛtta*, *nistala*, and *vartula*. / High, tall, elevated, and lofty are *ucca*, *prāṃśu*, *unnata*, and *udagra*; constant, eternal, and perpetual are *dhruva*, *nitya*, and *sanātana*.

366.s:
āviddhaṃ kuṭilaṃ bhugnaṃ vellitaṃ vakramityapi /
:n
1 pāṭho 'yaṃ puraruktidoṣeṇa duṣṭaḥ
:p 297
cañcalaṃ taralañcaiva kaṭhoraṃ jaṭharaṃ dṛḍhaṃ //
366.d:
आविद्धं कुटिलं भुग्नं वेल्लितं वक्रमित्यपि /
:न्
1 पाठो ऽयं पुररुक्तिदोषेण दुष्टः
:प् 297
चञ्चलं तरलञ्चैव कठोरं जठरं दृढं //
366.m:
Crooked, curved, bent, twisted, and tortuous are *āviddha*, *kuṭila*, *bhugna*, *vellita*, and *vakra*.
[Note]
[1. This reading is corrupt due to the fault of repetition.] / [Page 297]
Fickle and trembling are *cañcala* and *tarala*; hard, stiff, and firm are *kaṭhora*, *jaṭhara*, and *dṛḍha*.

366.s:
pratyagro 'bhinavo navyo navīno nūtano navaḥ /
ekatāno 'nanyavṛttiruccaṇḍamavilambitaṃ //
366.d:
प्रत्यग्रो ऽभिनवो नव्यो नवीनो नूतनो नवः /
एकतानो ऽनन्यवृत्तिरुच्चण्डमविलम्बितं //
366.m: Fresh, novel, modern, recent, and new are *pratyagra*, *abhinava*, *navya*, *navīna*, *nūtana*, and *nava*. / Intent on one object is *ekatāna* and *ananyavṛtti*; speedy is *uccaṇḍa* and *avilambita*.

366.s:
uccāvacaṃ naikabhedaṃ sambādhakalilaṃ tathā /
timitaṃ stimitaṃ klinnamabhiyogatvabhigrahaḥ //
366.d:
उच्चावचं नैकभेदं सम्बाधकलिलं तथा /
तिमितं स्तिमितं क्लिन्नमभियोगत्वभिग्रहः //
366.m: High and low, or multiform, is *uccāvaca* and *naikabheda*; crowded and dense are *sambādha* and *kalila*. / Moist, damp, and wet are *timita*, *stimita*, and *klinna*; attack is *abhiyoga* and *abhigraha*.

366.s:
sphātirvṛddhau prathā khyātau samāhāraḥ samuccayaḥ /
apahārastvapacayo vihārastu parikramaḥ //
366.d:
स्फातिर्वृद्धौ प्रथा ख्यातौ समाहारः समुच्चयः /
अपहारस्त्वपचयो विहारस्तु परिक्रमः //
366.m: *Sphāti* is in [the sense of] increase; *prathā* in renown; *samāhāra* is combination. / *Apahāra* is diminishment; *vihāra* is roaming about.

366.s:
pratyāhāra upādānaṃ nirhāro 'bhyavakarṣaṇaṃ /
vighno 'ntarāyaḥ pratyūhaḥ syādāsyātvāsanā sthitiḥ //
366.d:
प्रत्याहार उपादानं निर्हारो ऽभ्यवकर्षणं /
विघ्नो ऽन्तरायः प्रत्यूहः स्यादास्यात्वासना स्थितिः //
366.m: *Pratyāhāra* is taking back; *nirhāra* is drawing out. / An obstacle is *vighna*, *antarāya*, and *pratyūha*; *āsyā*, *āsanā*, and *sthiti* mean staying.

366.s:
sannidhiḥ sannikarṣaḥ syātmaṃkramo durgasañcaraḥ /
upalambhastvanubhavaḥ pratyādeśo nirākṛtiḥ //
366.d:
सन्निधिः सन्निकर्षः स्यात्मंक्रमो दुर्गसञ्चरः /
उपलम्भस्त्वनुभवः प्रत्यादेशो निराकृतिः //
366.m: Proximity is *sannidhi* and *sannikarṣa*; *saṅkrama* is difficult passage. / Perception is *upalambha* and *anubhava*; rejection is *pratyādeśa* and *nirākṛti*.

366.s:
parirambhaḥpariṣvaṅgaḥ saṃśleṣa upagūhanaṃ /
anumā pakṣahetvādyair ḍimbe bhramaraviplavau //
366.d:
परिरम्भःपरिष्वङ्गः संश्लेष उपगूहनं /
अनुमा पक्षहेत्वाद्यैर् डिम्बे भ्रमरविप्लवौ //
366.m: Embrace is *parirambha*, *pariṣvaṅga*, *saṃśleṣa*, and *upagūhana*. / Inference is by thesis, reason, and so on; in [the sense of] affray are *ḍimba*, *bhramara*, and *viplava*.

366.s:
asannikṛṣtārthajñānaṃ śabdāddhi śābdamīritaṃ /
sādṛśyadarśanāttulye buddhiḥ syādupamānakaṃ //
366.d:
असन्निकृष्तार्थज्ञानं शब्दाद्धि शाब्दमीरितं /
सादृश्यदर्शनात्तुल्ये बुद्धिः स्यादुपमानकं //
366.m: Cognition of an object not in sensory contact through verbal testimony is indeed declared as verbal testimony (*śābda*). / Cognition of similarity based on perceiving likeness is comparison (*upamāna*).

366.s:
kāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā vinā nasyādarthāpattiḥ parārthadhīḥ /
pratiyoginyāgṛhīte bhuvi nāstītyabhāvakaḥ /
ityādināmaliṅgo hi harirukto nṛbuddhaye //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe sāmānyanāmaliṅgāni nāma
ṣaṭṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 298
:ś atha saptaṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nityanaimīttikaprākṛtapralayāḥ
366.d:
कार्यं दृष्ट्वा विना नस्यादर्थापत्तिः परार्थधीः /
प्रतियोगिन्यागृहीते भुवि नास्तीत्यभावकः /
इत्यादिनामलिङ्गो हि हरिरुक्तो नृबुद्धये //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सामान्यनामलिङ्गानि नाम
षट्षष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 298
:श् अथ सप्तषष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
नित्यनैमीत्तिकप्राकृतप्रलयाः
366.m:
Seeing an effect that could not be without [another fact] is postulation (*arthāpatti*), the cognition of that other thing. / When a counter-correlate is grasped, [the cognition] that it is not on the ground is non-existence (*abhāva*). / In this manner, Hari is spoken of by the genders of nominal words for the understanding of men.
Thus ends the three hundred and sixty-sixth chapter, named 'Common Nouns and Genders', in the Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni.
[Page 298]
Now, the three hundred and sixty-seventh chapter.
The Constant, Occasional, and Elemental Dissolutions.

367.s:
agnir uvāca
caturvidhastu pralayo nityo yaḥ prāṇināṃ layaḥ /
sadā vināśo jātānāṃ brāhmo naimittiko layaḥ //
367.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
चतुर्विधस्तु प्रलयो नित्यो यः प्राणिनां लयः /
सदा विनाशो जातानां ब्राह्मो नैमित्तिको लयः //
367.m: Agni said: / Fourfold is the dissolution: the constant, which is the dissolution of living beings, / the continuous destruction of things born; the occasional dissolution belonging to Brahmā;

367.s:
caturyugasahasrānte prākṛtaḥ prākṛto layaḥ /
laya ātyantiko jñānādātmanaḥ paramātmani //
367.d:
चतुर्युगसहस्रान्ते प्राकृतः प्राकृतो लयः /
लय आत्यन्तिको ज्ञानादात्मनः परमात्मनि //
367.m: at the end of a thousand cycles of four ages, the elemental dissolution belonging to Prakṛti; / and the absolute dissolution through knowledge of the individual self in the Supreme Self.

367.s:
naimittikasya kalpānte vakṣye rūpaṃ layasya te /
caturyugasahasrānte kṣīṇaprāye mahītale //
367.d:
नैमित्तिकस्य कल्पान्ते वक्ष्ये रूपं लयस्य ते /
चतुर्युगसहस्रान्ते क्षीणप्राये महीतले //
367.m: I shall describe to you the nature of the occasional dissolution at the end of a kalpa: / At the end of a thousand cycles of four ages, when the surface of the earth is mostly exhausted,

367.s:
anāvṛṣṭiratīvogrā jāyate śatavārṣikī /
tataḥ sattvakṣayaḥ syācca tato viṣṇurjagatpatiḥ //
367.d:
अनावृष्टिरतीवोग्रा जायते शतवार्षिकी /
ततः सत्त्वक्षयः स्याच्च ततो विष्णुर्जगत्पतिः //
367.m: an exceedingly terrible drought lasting for a hundred years occurs. / Then occurs the destruction of living beings, and thereupon Viṣṇu, Lord of the Universe,

367.s:
sthito jalāni pivati bhānoḥ saptasu raśmiṣu /
bhūpātālasamudrāditoyaṃ nayati saṃkṣayaṃ //
367.d:
स्थितो जलानि पिवति भानोः सप्तसु रश्मिषु /
भूपातालसमुद्रादितोयं नयति संक्षयं //
367.m: standing [in the sun], drinks up the waters through the seven rays of the sun. / He brings the waters of the earth, the netherworlds, the oceans, and so forth to extinction.

367.s:
tatastasyānubhāvena toyāhāropavṛṃhitāḥ /
ta eva raśmayaḥ sapta jāyante sapta bhāskarāḥ //
367.d:
ततस्तस्यानुभावेन तोयाहारोपवृंहिताः /
त एव रश्मयः सप्त जायन्ते सप्त भास्कराः //
367.m: Then, through His majesty, nourished by the consumption of water, / those very seven rays become seven suns.

367.s:
dahanty aśeṣaṃ trailokyaṃ sapātālatalaṃ dvija /
kūrmapṛṣṭhasamā bhūḥ syāttataḥ kālāgnirudrakaḥ //
367.d:
दहन्त्य् अशेषं त्रैलोक्यं सपातालतलं द्विज /
कूर्मपृष्ठसमा भूः स्यात्ततः कालाग्निरुद्रकः //
367.m: They burn up the entire three worlds along with the realms of the netherworld, O twice-born one. / The earth becomes like the back of a tortoise; then Rudra as the Fire of Time,

367.s:
śeṣāhiśvāsasampātāt pātālāni dahatyadhaḥ /
pātālebhyo bhuvaṃ viṣṇurbhuvaḥ svargaṃ dahatyataḥ //
367.d:
शेषाहिश्वाससम्पातात् पातालानि दहत्यधः /
पातालेभ्यो भुवं विष्णुर्भुवः स्वर्गं दहत्यतः //
367.m: from the blast of the breath of the serpent Śeṣa, burns the netherworlds below. / From the netherworlds Viṣṇu burns the earth, and from the earth He burns heaven.

367.s:
ambarīṣamivābhāti trailokyamakhilaṃ tathā /
tatastāparītāstu lokadvayanivāsinaḥ //
:p 299
367.d:
अम्बरीषमिवाभाति त्रैलोक्यमखिलं तथा /
ततस्तापरीतास्तु लोकद्वयनिवासिनः //
:प् 299
367.m:
The entire three worlds then glow like a frying pan. / Then, overwhelmed by heat, the inhabitants of the two worlds
[Page 299]

367.s:
gācanti te maharlokaṃ maharlokājjanaṃ tataḥ /
rudrarūpī jagaddagdhvā mukhaniśvāsato hareḥ //
367.d:
गाचन्ति ते महर्लोकं महर्लोकाज्जनं ततः /
रुद्ररूपी जगद्दग्ध्वा मुखनिश्वासतो हरेः //
367.m: go to Maharloka, and from Maharloka then to Janaloka. / Having burned the universe in the form of Rudra, from the exhalation of Hari's mouth

367.s:
uttiṣṭanti tato medhā nānārūpāḥ savidyutaḥ /
śataṃ varṣāṇi varṣantaḥ śamayantyagnimutthitam //
367.d:
उत्तिष्टन्ति ततो मेधा नानारूपाः सविद्युतः /
शतं वर्षाणि वर्षन्तः शमयन्त्यग्निमुत्थितम् //
367.m: there arise clouds of various forms accompanied by lightning. / Raining for a hundred years, they extinguish the arisen fire.

367.s:
saptarṣisthānamākramya sthite 'mbhasi śataṃ marut /
mukhaniśvāsato viṣṇornāśaṃ nayati tānghanān //
367.d:
सप्तर्षिस्थानमाक्रम्य स्थिते ऽम्भसि शतं मरुत् /
मुखनिश्वासतो विष्णोर्नाशं नयति तान्घनान् //
367.m: When the water, inundating up to the abode of the Seven Sages, stands for a hundred [years], the wind / from the exhalation of Viṣṇu's mouth brings those clouds to destruction.

367.s:
vāyuṃ pītvā hariḥ śeṣe śete caikārṇave prabhuḥ /
brahmarūpadharaḥ siddhair jalagair munibhistutaḥ //
367.d:
वायुं पीत्वा हरिः शेषे शेते चैकार्णवे प्रभुः /
ब्रह्मरूपधरः सिद्धैर् जलगैर् मुनिभिस्तुतः //
367.m: Drinking the wind, Lord Hari lies on Śeṣa in the single vast ocean, / bearing the form of Brahmā, praised by the Siddhas and water-dwelling sages,

367.s:
ātmamāyāmayīṃ divyāṃ yoganidrāṃ samāsthitaḥ /
ātmānaṃ vasidevākhyaṃ cintayanmadhusūdanaḥ //
367.d:
आत्ममायामयीं दिव्यां योगनिद्रां समास्थितः /
आत्मानं वसिदेवाख्यं चिन्तयन्मधुसूदनः //
367.m: having resorted to the divine yogic sleep consisting of His own māyā, / contemplating Himself whose name is Vāsudeva, Madhusūdana

367.s:
kalpaṃ śete prabuddho 'tha brahmarūpī sṛjaty asau /
dviparārdhantato vyaktaṃ prakṛtau līyate dvija //
367.d:
कल्पं शेते प्रबुद्धो ऽथ ब्रह्मरूपी सृजत्य् असौ /
द्विपरार्धन्ततो व्यक्तं प्रकृतौ लीयते द्विज //
367.m: sleeps for a kalpa; awakened then, in the form of Brahmā He creates. / After two parārdhas, the manifest merges into Prakṛti, O twice-born one.

367.s:
sthānāt sthānaṃ daśaguṇamekasmādguṇyate sthale /
tato 'ṣṭādaśame bhāge parārdhamabhidhīyate //
367.d:
स्थानात् स्थानं दशगुणमेकस्माद्गुण्यते स्थले /
ततो ऽष्टादशमे भागे परार्धमभिधीयते //
367.m: From place to place on the surface [of computation], each is multiplied tenfold from the one before; / then, at the eighteenth place, a parārdha is declared.

367.s:
parārdhaṃ dviguṇaṃ yattu prākṛtaḥ pralayaḥ smṛtaḥ /
anāvṛṣṭyāgnisamparkāt kṛte saṃjvalane dvija //
367.d:
परार्धं द्विगुणं यत्तु प्राकृतः प्रलयः स्मृतः /
अनावृष्ट्याग्निसम्पर्कात् कृते संज्वलने द्विज //
367.m: Two parārdhas is what is remembered as the elemental dissolution. / When blazing has been caused by the contact of drought and fire, O twice-born one,

367.s:
mahadādervikārasya viśeṣāntasya saṃkṣaye /
kṛṣṇecchākārite tasmin samprāpte pratisañcare //
367.d:
महदादेर्विकारस्य विशेषान्तस्य संक्षये /
कृष्णेच्छाकारिते तस्मिन् सम्प्राप्ते प्रतिसञ्चरे //
367.m: at the destruction of the transformations beginning with the intellect and ending with the specific elements, / when that cosmic dissolution caused by Kṛṣṇa's will has arrived,

367.s:
āpo grasanti vai pūrvaṃ bhūmirgandhādikaṃ guṇaṃ /
ātmagandhāttato bhūmiḥ pralayatvāya kalpate //
367.d:
आपो ग्रसन्ति वै पूर्वं भूमिर्गन्धादिकं गुणं /
आत्मगन्धात्ततो भूमिः प्रलयत्वाय कल्पते //
367.m: the waters first swallow the quality of odor and the rest of the earth. / Deprived of its own odor, the earth then prepares for dissolution.

367.s:
rasātmikāś ca tiṣṭhanti hy āpastāsāṃ raso guṇaḥ /
pīyate jyotiṣā tāsu naṣṭāsvagniś ca dīpyate //
367.d:
रसात्मिकाश् च तिष्ठन्ति ह्य् आपस्तासां रसो गुणः /
पीयते ज्योतिषा तासु नष्टास्वग्निश् च दीप्यते //
367.m: And the waters, consisting of taste, remain; their quality of taste / is drunk by light, and when they are destroyed, the fire blazes.

367.s:
jyotiṣo 'pi guṇaṃ rūpaṃ vāyurgrasati bhāskaraṃ /
:p 300
naṣṭe jyotiṣi vāyuś cabalī dodhūyate mahān //
367.d:
ज्योतिषो ऽपि गुणं रूपं वायुर्ग्रसति भास्करं /
:प् 300
नष्टे ज्योतिषि वायुश् चबली दोधूयते महान् //

367.s:
vāyorapi guṇaṃ sparśamākāśaṃ grasate tataḥ /
vāyau naṣṭe tu cākāśannīravaṃ tiṣṭhati dvija //
367.d:
वायोरपि गुणं स्पर्शमाकाशं ग्रसते ततः /
वायौ नष्टे तु चाकाशन्नीरवं तिष्ठति द्विज //
367.m: Space then swallows the quality of touch belonging to the wind. / When the wind is destroyed, space remains soundless, O twice-born one.

367.s:
ākāśasyātha vai śabdaṃ bhūtādirgrasate ca khaṃ /
abhimānātmakaṃ khañca bhūtādiṃ grasate mahān //
367.d:
आकाशस्याथ वै शब्दं भूतादिर्ग्रसते च खं /
अभिमानात्मकं खञ्च भूतादिं ग्रसते महान् //
367.m: Then the origin of the elements swallows sound and space as the void; / and the Intellect swallows that origin of the elements whose nature is ego-sense.

367.s:
bhūmiryāti layañcāpsu āpo jyotiṣi tadbrajet /
vāyau vāyuś ca khe khañca ahaṅkāre layaṃ sa ca //
367.d:
भूमिर्याति लयञ्चाप्सु आपो ज्योतिषि तद्ब्रजेत् /
वायौ वायुश् च खे खञ्च अहङ्कारे लयं स च //
367.m: Earth dissolves into water, and water dissolves into fire; / [fire] into wind, wind into space, and space dissolves into ego;

367.s:
mahāttatve mahāntañca prakṛtirgrasate dvija /
vyaktāvyaktā ca prakṛtirvyaktasyāvyaktake layaḥ //
367.d:
महात्तत्वे महान्तञ्च प्रकृतिर्ग्रसते द्विज /
व्यक्ताव्यक्ता च प्रकृतिर्व्यक्तस्याव्यक्तके लयः //
367.m: and [ego dissolves] into the cosmic intellect; and primordial nature devours the cosmic intellect, O twice-born! / Primordial nature is manifest and unmanifest; the dissolution of the manifest is into the unmanifest.

367.s:
pumāne kākṣaraḥ śuddhaḥ so 'pyaṃśaḥ paramātmanaḥ /
prakṛtiḥ puruṣaś caitau līyete paramātmani //
367.d:
पुमाने काक्षरः शुद्धः सो ऽप्यंशः परमात्मनः /
प्रकृतिः पुरुषश् चैतौ लीयेते परमात्मनि //
367.m: The spirit is imperishable, pure, and even it is a portion of the Supreme Self; / primordial nature and spirit both dissolve into the Supreme Self,

367.s:
na santi yatra sarveśe nāmajātyādikalpanāḥ /
sattāmātrātmake jñeye jñānātmanyātmahaḥ pare //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nityanaimittikaprākṛtapralayā nāma
saptaṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś athāṣṭaṣaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
ātyantikalayagarbhotpattinirūpaṇaṃ
367.d:
न सन्ति यत्र सर्वेशे नामजात्यादिकल्पनाः /
सत्तामात्रात्मके ज्ञेये ज्ञानात्मन्यात्महः परे //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नित्यनैमित्तिकप्राकृतप्रलया नाम
सप्तषष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथाष्टषष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
आत्यन्तिकलयगर्भोत्पत्तिनिरूपणं
367.m:
in whom, the Lord of all, there are no conceptualisations of name, genus, and the like; / [dissolve] into the highest [reality], whose nature is sheer existence, to be known, whose nature is consciousness.
Thus, in the great Agni Purāṇa, the three hundred and sixty-seventh chapter, entitled “The Constant, Occasional, and Elemental Dissolutions.”
Now, the three hundred and sixty-eighth chapter.
The description of the absolute dissolution and the origin of the embryo.

368.s:
agnir uvāca
ātyantikaṃ layaṃ vakṣye jñānādātyantiko layaḥ /
ādhyātmikādisantāpaṃ jñātvā svasya virāgataḥ //
:p 301
368.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
आत्यन्तिकं लयं वक्ष्ये ज्ञानादात्यन्तिको लयः /
आध्यात्मिकादिसन्तापं ज्ञात्वा स्वस्य विरागतः //
:प् 301
368.m:
Agni said: / I shall explain the absolute dissolution; absolute dissolution comes from knowledge / after one has realised one's own internal and other afflictions through detachment.
[Page 301]

368.s:
ādhyātmikastu santāpaḥśārīro mānaso dvidhā /
śārīro bahubhirbhedaistāpo 'sau śrūyatāṃ dvija //
368.d:
आध्यात्मिकस्तु सन्तापःशारीरो मानसो द्विधा /
शारीरो बहुभिर्भेदैस्तापो ऽसौ श्रूयतां द्विज //
368.m: Internal affliction is twofold: bodily and mental. / Hear now, O twice-born, of that bodily affliction through its many varieties.

368.s:
tyaktvā jīvo bhogadehaṃ garbhamāproti karmabhiḥ /
ātivāhikasaṃjñastu deho bhavati vai dvija //
368.d:
त्यक्त्वा जीवो भोगदेहं गर्भमाप्रोति कर्मभिः /
आतिवाहिकसंज्ञस्तु देहो भवति वै द्विज //
368.m: Having cast off the body of enjoyment, the individual soul enters the womb through its past deeds. / Its body is then named the vehicular [body], O twice-born.

368.s:
kevalaṃ sa manuṣyāṇāṃ mṛtyukāla upasthite /
yāmyaiḥ puṃbhirmanuṣyāṇāṃ taccharīraṃ dvijottamāḥ //
368.d:
केवलं स मनुष्याणां मृत्युकाल उपस्थिते /
याम्यैः पुंभिर्मनुष्याणां तच्छरीरं द्विजोत्तमाः //
368.m: For human beings alone, when the time of death arrives, / that body of human beings, O best of the twice-born,

368.s:
nīyate yāmyamārgeṇa prāṇināṃ mune /
tataḥ svaryāti narakaṃ sa bhramedghaṭayantravat //
368.d:
नीयते याम्यमार्गेण प्राणिनां मुने /
ततः स्वर्याति नरकं स भ्रमेद्घटयन्त्रवत् //
368.m: is led along Yama's path by the men of Yama, O sage of living beings. / Then it goes to heaven or hell; it revolves like a water-wheel.

368.s:
karmabhūmiriyaṃ brahman phalabhūmirasau smṛtā /
yamo yonīś ca narakaṃ nirūpayati karmaṇā //
368.d:
कर्मभूमिरियं ब्रह्मन् फलभूमिरसौ स्मृता /
यमो योनीश् च नरकं निरूपयति कर्मणा //
368.m: This is known as the realm of action, O brāhmaṇa, and that as the realm of fruit. / Yama assigns wombs and hell according to past action.

368.s:
pūraṇīyāś ca tenaiva yamañcaivānupaśyatāṃ /
vāyubhūtāḥ prāṇinaś ca garbhante prāpnuvanti hi //
368.d:
पूरणीयाश् च तेनैव यमञ्चैवानुपश्यतां /
वायुभूताः प्राणिनश् च गर्भन्ते प्राप्नुवन्ति हि //
368.m: And by him alone are those who behold Yama [assigned] to be filled; / becoming wind, living beings indeed attain the womb.

368.s:
yamadūtair manuṣyastu nīyate tañca paśyati /
dharmī ca pūjyate tena pāpiṣṭhastāḍyate gṛhe //
368.d:
यमदूतैर् मनुष्यस्तु नीयते तञ्च पश्यति /
धर्मी च पूज्यते तेन पापिष्ठस्ताड्यते गृहे //
368.m: A person is led by the messengers of Yama and sees him; / the righteous is honoured by him, and the sinner is beaten in his abode.

368.s:
śubhāśubhaṃ karma tasya citragupto nirūpayet /
bāndhavānāmaśauce tu dehe khalvātivāhike //
368.d:
शुभाशुभं कर्म तस्य चित्रगुप्तो निरूपयेत् /
बान्धवानामशौचे तु देहे खल्वातिवाहिके //
368.m: Citragupta ascertains his auspicious and inauspicious deeds. / During the ritual impurity of relatives, while remaining indeed in the vehicular body,

368.s:
tiṣṭhannayati dharmajña dattapiṇḍāśanantataḥ /
tanyaktvā pretadehantu prāpyānyaṃ pretalokataḥ(1) //
368.d:
तिष्ठन्नयति धर्मज्ञ दत्तपिण्डाशनन्ततः /
तन्यक्त्वा प्रेतदेहन्तु प्राप्यान्यं प्रेतलोकतः(1) //
368.m: he passes the time, O knower of righteousness, feeding on the funeral cakes offered [to him]. / Casting off that, and having obtained another ghost-body from the realm of the ghosts,

368.s:
vaset kṣudhā tṛṣā yukta āmaśrāddhānnabhuṅnaraḥ /
ātivāhikedehāttu pretapiṇḍair vinā naraḥ //
368.d:
वसेत् क्षुधा तृषा युक्त आमश्राद्धान्नभुङ्नरः /
आतिवाहिकेदेहात्तु प्रेतपिण्डैर् विना नरः //
368.m: the person dwells afflicted with hunger and thirst, eating the food of raw ancestral offerings; / but without the funeral cakes for the deceased, a person from the vehicular body

368.s:
na hi mokṣamavāpnoti piṇḍāṃstatraiva so 'śrute /
kṛte sapiṇḍīkaraṇe naraḥ saṃvatsarātparaṃ //
:n
1 pretalaukike iti kha..
:p 302
368.d:
न हि मोक्षमवाप्नोति पिण्डांस्तत्रैव सो ऽश्रुते /
कृते सपिण्डीकरणे नरः संवत्सरात्परं //
:न्
1 प्रेतलौकिके इति ख..
:प् 302
368.m:
does not obtain release; he consumes the funeral cakes right there. / When the sapīṇḍīkaraṇa rite has been performed after a year, the man,
[Note]
1. Variant: 'pretalaukike' according to manuscript kha. / [Page 302]

368.s:
pretadehaṃ samutamṛjya bhogadehaṃ prapadyate /
bhogadehāvubhau proktāvaśubhaśubhasaṃjñitau //
368.d:
प्रेतदेहं समुतमृज्य भोगदेहं प्रपद्यते /
भोगदेहावुभौ प्रोक्तावशुभशुभसंज्ञितौ //
368.m: abandoning the ghost-body, attains the body of enjoyment. / The bodies of enjoyment are declared to be twofold, called inauspicious and auspicious.

368.s:
bhuktvā tu bhogadehena karmabandhānnipātyate /
taṃ dehaṃ paratastasmādbhakṣayanti niśācarāḥ //
368.d:
भुक्त्वा तु भोगदेहेन कर्मबन्धान्निपात्यते /
तं देहं परतस्तस्माद्भक्षयन्ति निशाचराः //
368.m: Having experienced [fruits] through the body of enjoyment, he is cast down by the bondage of action. / Afterwards, night-stalking demons devour that body.

368.s:
pāpe tiṣṭhati cet svargaṃ tena bhuktaṃ tadā dvija /
tadā dvitīyaṃ gṛhṇāti bhogadehantu pāpināṃ //
368.d:
पापे तिष्ठति चेत् स्वर्गं तेन भुक्तं तदा द्विज /
तदा द्वितीयं गृह्णाति भोगदेहन्तु पापिनां //
368.m: If sin remains while heaven has been enjoyed by him, O twice-born, / then he assumes a second body of enjoyment, meant for sinners.

368.s:
bhuktvā pāpantu vai paścādyena bhuktaṃ tripiṣṭapaṃ /
śucīnāṃ śrīmatāṃ gehe svargabhraṣṭo 'bhijāyate //
368.d:
भुक्त्वा पापन्तु वै पश्चाद्येन भुक्तं त्रिपिष्टपं /
शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे स्वर्गभ्रष्टो ऽभिजायते //
368.m: When a person by whom heaven was enjoyed subsequently experiences his sin, / he who has fallen from heaven is born in the house of the pure and prosperous.

368.s:
puṇye tiṣṭhati cetpāpantena bhuktaṃ tadā bhavet /
tasmin sambhakṣite dehe śubhaṃ gṛhṇāti vigraham //
368.d:
पुण्ये तिष्ठति चेत्पापन्तेन भुक्तं तदा भवेत् /
तस्मिन् सम्भक्षिते देहे शुभं गृह्णाति विग्रहम् //
368.m: If merit remains when sin has been experienced by him, / then, when that body has been devoured, he assumes an auspicious form.

368.s:
karmaṇyalpāvaśeṣe tu narakādapi mucyate /
muktastu narakādyāti tiryagyoniṃ na saṃśayaḥ //
368.d:
कर्मण्यल्पावशेषे तु नरकादपि मुच्यते /
मुक्तस्तु नरकाद्याति तिर्यग्योनिं न संशयः //
368.m: When only a small remainder of action is left, he is released even from hell; / and having been released from hell, he goes to an animal womb, without a doubt.

368.s:
jīvaḥ praviṣṭo garbhantu kalale 'pyatra tiṣṭhati(2) /
ghanībhūtaṃ dvitīye tu tṛtīye 'vayavāstataḥ //
368.d:
जीवः प्रविष्टो गर्भन्तु कलले ऽप्यत्र तिष्ठति(2) /
घनीभूतं द्वितीये तु तृतीये ऽवयवास्ततः //
368.m: The soul, having entered the womb, remains here in the embryonic mass; / in the second [month] it becomes solidified; in the third, limbs appear;

368.s:
caturthe 'sthīni tvaṅmāṃsampañcame romasambhavaḥ /
ṣaṣṭhe ceto 'tha jīvasya duḥkhaṃ vindati saptame //
368.d:
चतुर्थे ऽस्थीनि त्वङ्मांसम्पञ्चमे रोमसम्भवः /
षष्ठे चेतो ऽथ जीवस्य दुःखं विन्दति सप्तमे //
368.m: in the fourth [develop] bones, skin, and flesh; in the fifth, the growth of body hair; / in the sixth, the consciousness of the soul [arises]; and in the seventh, it experiences pain.

368.s:
jarāyuveṣṭite dehe mūrdhni baddhāñjalis tathā /
madhye klīvastu vāme strī dakṣiṇe puruṣasthitiḥ //
368.d:
जरायुवेष्टिते देहे मूर्ध्नि बद्धाञ्जलिस् तथा /
मध्ये क्लीवस्तु वामे स्त्री दक्षिणे पुरुषस्थितिः //
368.m: Enveloped in the placenta, the body has its hands folded at the head; / a eunuch stays in the middle, a female on the left, and a male on the right.

368.s:
tiṣṭhatyudarabhāge tu pṛṣṭhasyābhimukhas tathā /
yasyāṃ tiṣṭhatyasau yonau tāṃ sa vetti na saṃśayaḥ //
368.d:
तिष्ठत्युदरभागे तु पृष्ठस्याभिमुखस् तथा /
यस्यां तिष्ठत्यसौ योनौ तां स वेत्ति न संशयः //
368.m: He remains in the abdominal region, facing the back; / he undoubtedly knows the womb in which he stays,

368.s:
sarvañca vetti vṛttāntamārabhya narajammanaḥ /
:n
1 gacchatīti ka..
:p 303
andhakārañca mahatīṃ pīḍāṃ vindati mānavaḥ //
368.d:
सर्वञ्च वेत्ति वृत्तान्तमारभ्य नरजम्मनः /
:न्
1 गच्छतीति क..
:प् 303
अन्धकारञ्च महतीं पीडां विन्दति मानवः //
368.m:
and he knows the whole story [of his past lives] from the very beginning of human birth.
[Note]
1. Variant: 'gacchati' according to manuscript ka. / [Page 303]
A human being experiences darkness and great torment.

368.s:
māturāhārapītantu saptame māsyupāśnute /
aṣṭame navame māsi bhṛśamudvijata tathā //
368.d:
मातुराहारपीतन्तु सप्तमे मास्युपाश्नुते /
अष्टमे नवमे मासि भृशमुद्विजत तथा //
368.m: In the seventh month, he partakes of what his mother eats and drinks; / in the eighth and ninth months, he becomes intensely agitated.

368.s:
vyavāye pīḍāmāpnoti māturvyāyāmake tathā /
vyādhiś ca vyādhitāyāṃ syānmuhūrtaṃ śatavarṣavat //
368.d:
व्यवाये पीडामाप्नोति मातुर्व्यायामके तथा /
व्याधिश् च व्याधितायां स्यान्मुहूर्तं शतवर्षवत् //
368.m: He suffers pain during sexual intercourse [by the parents] and during the mother's exertion; / when she falls sick, there is disease [for him], and a single moment feels like a hundred years.

368.s:
santapyate karmabhistu kurute 'tha manorathān /
garbhādvinirgato brahman mokṣajñānaṃ kariṣyati //
368.d:
सन्तप्यते कर्मभिस्तु कुरुते ऽथ मनोरथान् /
गर्भाद्विनिर्गतो ब्रह्मन् मोक्षज्ञानं करिष्यति //
368.m: Tormented by his past actions, he then forms desires: / “Once emerged from the womb, O brāhmaṇa, I will pursue the knowledge that brings liberation!”

368.s:
sūtivātair adhībhūto niḥsaredyoniyantrataḥ /
pīḍyamāno māsamātraṃ karasparśena duḥkhitaḥ //
368.d:
सूतिवातैर् अधीभूतो निःसरेद्योनियन्त्रतः /
पीड्यमानो मासमात्रं करस्पर्शेन दुःखितः //
368.m: Overpowered by the winds of childbirth, he is expelled through the passage of the womb; / tormented for about a month, he suffers at the touch of hands.

368.s:
khaśabdāt kṣudraśrotāṃsi dehe śrotraṃ viviktatā /
śvāsocchāsau gatirvāyorvakrasaṃsparśanaṃ tathā(1) //
368.d:
खशब्दात् क्षुद्रश्रोतांसि देहे श्रोत्रं विविक्तता /
श्वासोच्छासौ गतिर्वायोर्वक्रसंस्पर्शनं तथा(1) //
368.m: From the sound of space [arise] the subtle channels in the body, the ear, and spatial openness; / inhalation, exhalation, movement, and the tactile sense of the mouth are from wind;

368.s:
agnerūpaṃ darśanaṃ syādūṣmā paṅktiś ca pittakaṃ /
medhā varṇaṃ balaṃ chāyā tejaḥ śauryaṃ śarīrake //
368.d:
अग्नेरूपं दर्शनं स्यादूष्मा पङ्क्तिश् च पित्तकं /
मेधा वर्णं बलं छाया तेजः शौर्यं शरीरके //
368.m: from fire come form, vision, bodily heat, digestion, bile, / intellect, complexion, strength, radiance, lustre, and valour in the body;

368.s:
jalātsvedaś ca rasanandehe vai saṃprajāyate /
kledo vasā rasā takraṃ śukramūtrakaphādikaṃ //
368.d:
जलात्स्वेदश् च रसनन्देहे वै संप्रजायते /
क्लेदो वसा रसा तक्रं शुक्रमूत्रकफादिकं //
368.m: from water, sweat and the sense of taste are produced in the body, / moisture, fat, chyme, buttermilk, semen, urine, phlegm, and the like;

368.s:
bhūmerdhrāṇaṃ keśanakhaṃ gauravaṃ sthirato 'sthitaḥ /
mātṛjāni mṛdūnyatra tvaṅmāṃsahṛdayāni ca //
368.d:
भूमेर्ध्राणं केशनखं गौरवं स्थिरतो ऽस्थितः /
मातृजानि मृदून्यत्र त्वङ्मांसहृदयानि च //
368.m: from earth come the sense of smell, hair, nails, heaviness, firmness, and bones. / The soft parts here originate from the mother: skin, flesh, and heart,

368.s:
nābhirmajjā(2) śakṛnmedaḥ kledānyāmāśayāni ca /
pitṛjāni śirāsnāyuśukrañcaivātmajāni tu //
368.d:
नाभिर्मज्जा(2) शकृन्मेदः क्लेदान्यामाशयानि च /
पितृजानि शिरास्नायुशुक्रञ्चैवात्मजानि तु //
368.m: navel, marrow, faeces, fat, fluid, and the stomach; / those originating from the father are veins, ligaments, and semen. And those arising from the self are:

368.s:
kāmakrodhau bhayaṃ harṣo dharmādharmātmatā tathā /
ākṛtiḥ svaravarṇau tu mehanādyaṃ tathā ca yat //
:n
1 śvāsocchāsau sanirvāpau vāhyasaṃsparśanamiti ña..
2 nābhirmeḍamiti kha.. , ña.. ca
:p 304
368.d:
कामक्रोधौ भयं हर्षो धर्माधर्मात्मता तथा /
आकृतिः स्वरवर्णौ तु मेहनाद्यं तथा च यत् //
:न्
1 श्वासोच्छासौ सनिर्वापौ वाह्यसंस्पर्शनमिति ञ..
2 नाभिर्मेडमिति ख.. , ञ.. च
:प् 304
368.m:
desire, anger, fear, joy, and the disposition towards righteousness and unrighteousness; / shape, voice, complexion, genitals, and so forth,
[Note]
1. Variant: 'śvāsocchāsau sanirvāpau vāhyasaṃsparśanam' according to manuscript ña.
2. Variant: 'nābhirmeḍam' according to manuscripts kha and ña. / [Page 304]

368.s:
tāmasāni tathājñānaṃ pramādālasyatṛṭkṣudhāḥ /
mohamātsaryavaiguṇyaśokāyāsabhayāni ca //
368.d:
तामसानि तथाज्ञानं प्रमादालस्यतृट्क्षुधाः /
मोहमात्सर्यवैगुण्यशोकायासभयानि च //
368.m: Ignorance, negligence, indolence, thirst, hunger, / delusion, envy, deficiency, grief, exhaustion, and fear are of the quality of darkness.

368.s:
kāmakrodhau tathā śauryaṃ yajñepsā bahubhāṣitā /
ahaṅkāraḥ parāvajñā rājasāni mahāmune //
368.d:
कामक्रोधौ तथा शौर्यं यज्ञेप्सा बहुभाषिता /
अहङ्कारः परावज्ञा राजसानि महामुने //
368.m: Desire, anger, valour, eagerness to sacrifice, garrulousness, / egoism, and contempt for others are of the quality of passion, O great sage.

368.s:
dharmepsā mokṣakāmitvaṃ parā bhaktiś ca keśave /
dākṣiṇyaṃ vyavasāyitvaṃ sātvikāni vinirdiśet //
368.d:
धर्मेप्सा मोक्षकामित्वं परा भक्तिश् च केशवे /
दाक्षिण्यं व्यवसायित्वं सात्विकानि विनिर्दिशेत् //
368.m: Desire for righteousness, yearning for liberation, supreme devotion to Keśava, / courteousness, and resolute determination are to be pointed out as of the quality of purity.

368.s:
capalaḥ krodhano bhīrurbahubhāṣo kalipriyaḥ /
svapne gaganagaś caiva bahuvāto naro bhavet //
368.d:
चपलः क्रोधनो भीरुर्बहुभाषो कलिप्रियः /
स्वप्ने गगनगश् चैव बहुवातो नरो भवेत् //
368.m: A person who is fickle, wrathful, timid, talkative, fond of quarrel, / and who travels in the sky in dreams, has an excess of wind.

368.s:
akālapalitaḥ krordho mahāprājño raṇapriyaḥ /
svapne ca dīptimatprekṣī bahupitto naro bhavet //
368.d:
अकालपलितः क्रोर्धो महाप्राज्ञो रणप्रियः /
स्वप्ने च दीप्तिमत्प्रेक्षी बहुपित्तो नरो भवेत् //
368.m: A person with premature grey hair, furious, highly intelligent, fond of battle, / and seeing bright objects in dreams, has an excess of bile.

368.s:
sthiramitraḥ sthirotsāhaḥ sthirāṅgo draviṇānvitaḥ /
svapne jalasitālokī bahuśle ṣmā naro bhavet //
368.d:
स्थिरमित्रः स्थिरोत्साहः स्थिराङ्गो द्रविणान्वितः /
स्वप्ने जलसितालोकी बहुश्ले ष्मा नरो भवेत् //
368.m: A person with steadfast friends, steady enthusiasm, firm limbs, endowed with wealth, / and seeing water and white objects in dreams, has an excess of phlegm.

368.s:
rasastu prāṇināṃ dehe jīvanaṃ rudhiraṃ tathā /
lepanañca tathā māṃsamedhasnehakarantu tat //
368.d:
रसस्तु प्राणिनां देहे जीवनं रुधिरं तथा /
लेपनञ्च तथा मांसमेधस्नेहकरन्तु तत् //
368.m: The chyle indeed [provides] nourishment in the body of living beings, and blood [provides] life; / and flesh provides plastering, while fat creates unctuousness.

368.s:
dhāraṇantv asthi majjā syātpūraṇaṃ vīryavardhanaṃ /
śukravīryakaraṃ hy ojaḥ prāṇakṛjjīvasaṃsthitiḥ //
368.d:
धारणन्त्व् अस्थि मज्जा स्यात्पूरणं वीर्यवर्धनं /
शुक्रवीर्यकरं ह्य् ओजः प्राणकृज्जीवसंस्थितिः //
368.m: Bone provides support, and marrow should be the filler, increasing virility. / Semen produces vigor, and *ojas* indeed creates vitality, being the abode of the individual soul.

368.s:
ojaḥ śukrāt sārataramāpītaṃ hṛdayopagaṃ /
ṣaḍaṅgaśakthinī bāhurmūrdhā jaṭharamīritaṃ //
368.d:
ओजः शुक्रात् सारतरमापीतं हृदयोपगं /
षडङ्गशक्थिनी बाहुर्मूर्धा जठरमीरितं //
368.m: *Ojas* is the most essential essence, superior to semen; yellowish, it enters the heart. / The six limbs are declared to be the two legs, the two arms, the head, and the trunk.

368.s:
ṣaṭtvacā vāhyato yadvadanyā rudhiradhārikā /
vilāsadhāriṇī cānyā caturthī kuṇḍadhāriṇī //
368.d:
षट्त्वचा वाह्यतो यद्वदन्या रुधिरधारिका /
विलासधारिणी चान्या चतुर्थी कुण्डधारिणी //
368.m: Just as the six layers of skin are outermost, another is the supporter of blood; / and another is the supporter of radiance, while the fourth is the supporter of the cavity;

368.s:
pañcamī vidradhisthānaṃ ṣaṣṭhī prāṇadharā matā /
kalāsaptamau māṃsadharā dvitīyā raktadhāriṇī //
368.d:
पञ्चमी विद्रधिस्थानं षष्ठी प्राणधरा मता /
कलासप्तमौ मांसधरा द्वितीया रक्तधारिणी //
368.m: the fifth is the location of abscesses, and the sixth is held to be the supporter of the vital breaths. / Of the seven layers (*kalā*), the first is the supporter of flesh, the second is the supporter of blood,

368.s:
yakṛtplīhāśrayā cānyā medodharāsthidhāriṇī /
:p 305
majjāśleṣmapurīṣāṇāṃ dharā pakvāśayasthitā /
ṣaṣṭhī pittadharā śukradharā śukrāśayāparā //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe ātyantikalayagarbhotpattinirūpaṇaṃ
nāmāṣṭaṣṭyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś athonasaptatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
śarīrāvayavāḥ
368.d:
यकृत्प्लीहाश्रया चान्या मेदोधरास्थिधारिणी /
:प् 305
मज्जाश्लेष्मपुरीषाणां धरा पक्वाशयस्थिता /
षष्ठी पित्तधरा शुक्रधरा शुक्राशयापरा //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे आत्यन्तिकलयगर्भोत्पत्तिनिरूपणं
नामाष्टष्ट्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथोनसप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
शरीरावयवाः
368.m:
and another rests upon the liver and spleen; there is the supporter of fat, the supporter of bone,
[Page 305]
the supporter of marrow, phlegm, and feces, located in the large intestine;
the sixth is the supporter of bile, and another is the supporter of semen, located in the receptacle of semen.
Thus ends the three hundred and sixty-eighth chapter in the Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni, entitled 'The Determination of Absolute Dissolution and the Origin of the Embryo.'
Now the three hundred and sixty-ninth chapter:
The Limbs of the Body

369.s:
agnir uvāca
śrotraṃ tvak cakṣuṣī jihvā ghrāṇaṃ dhīḥ khuñca bhūtagaṃ /
śabdasparśarūparamagandhāḥ khādiṣu tadguṇāḥ //
369.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
श्रोत्रं त्वक् चक्षुषी जिह्वा घ्राणं धीः खुञ्च भूतगं /
शब्दस्पर्शरूपरमगन्धाः खादिषु तद्गुणाः //
369.m: Agni said: / Ear, skin, two eyes, tongue, nose, intellect, and space belong to the elements. / Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are the qualities in space and the other [elements].

369.s:
pāyūpasthau karau pādau vāgbhavet karmakhuntathā /
utsargānandakādānagativāgādi karma tat //
369.d:
पायूपस्थौ करौ पादौ वाग्भवेत् कर्मखुन्तथा /
उत्सर्गानन्दकादानगतिवागादि कर्म तत् //
369.m: The anus, the genitals, the two hands, the two feet, and speech are the organs of action in space. / Excretion, sexual pleasure, taking, locomotion, and speech are their actions.

369.s:
pañcakarmendriyānyatra pañcabuddhīndriyāṇi ca /
indriyārthāś ca pañcaiva mahābhūtā mano 'dhipāḥ //
369.d:
पञ्चकर्मेन्द्रियान्यत्र पञ्चबुद्धीन्द्रियाणि च /
इन्द्रियार्थाश् च पञ्चैव महाभूता मनो ऽधिपाः //
369.m: Here are the five organs of action and the five organs of knowledge, / and the five objects of the senses, the gross elements, and the mind as ruler.

369.s:
ātmāvyaktaś caturviṃśatattvāni puruṣaḥ paraḥ /
saṃyuktaś ca viyuktaś ca yathā matsyodake ubhe //
369.d:
आत्माव्यक्तश् चतुर्विंशतत्त्वानि पुरुषः परः /
संयुक्तश् च वियुक्तश् च यथा मत्स्योदके उभे //
369.m: The soul is the unmanifest; these are the twenty-four principles, and the *puruṣa* is supreme. / Both are joined and disjoined, like fish and water.

369.s:
avyaktamāsritānīha rajaḥsattvatamāṃsi ca /
āntaraḥ puruṣo jīvaḥ sa paraṃ brahma kāraṇaṃ //
369.d:
अव्यक्तमास्रितानीह रजःसत्त्वतमांसि च /
आन्तरः पुरुषो जीवः स परं ब्रह्म कारणं //
369.m: Passion, goodness, and darkness reside here in the unmanifest. / The inner *puruṣa* is the individual soul; it is the supreme Brahman, the cause.

369.s:
sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yo vetti puruṣaṃ paraṃ /
saptāśayāḥ smṛtā dehe rudhirasyaika āśayaḥ //
369.d:
स याति परमं स्थानं यो वेत्ति पुरुषं परं /
सप्ताशयाः स्मृता देहे रुधिरस्यैक आशयः //
369.m: He who knows the supreme *puruṣa* goes to the highest abode. / Seven receptacles are taught in the body: one receptacle is of blood,

369.s:
śleṣmaṇaścāmapittābhyāṃ pakvāśayastu pañcamaḥ /
:p 306
vāyumūtrāśayaḥ saptaḥ strīṇāṃ garbhāśayo 'ṣṭamaḥ //
369.d:
श्लेष्मणश्चामपित्ताभ्यां पक्वाशयस्तु पञ्चमः /
:प् 306
वायुमूत्राशयः सप्तः स्त्रीणां गर्भाशयो ऽष्टमः //
369.m:
of phlegm, of undigested food and bile; the large intestine is the fifth,
[Page 306]
the receptacle of wind and urine is the seventh; in women, the uterus is the eighth.

369.s:
pittātpakvāśayo 'gneḥ syādyonirvikaśitā dyutau /
padmavadgarbhāśayaḥ syāttatra ghatte saraktakaṃ //
369.d:
पित्तात्पक्वाशयो ऽग्नेः स्याद्योनिर्विकशिता द्युतौ /
पद्मवद्गर्भाशयः स्यात्तत्र घत्ते सरक्तकं //
369.m: From bile, the large intestine comes into being from fire; the vagina opens in its luster. / The uterus is like a lotus; there it receives [the semen] mixed with blood.

369.s:
śukraṃ svaśukrataścāṅgaṃ kuntalānyatra kālataḥ /
nyastaṃ śukramato yonau neti garbhāśayaṃ mune //
369.d:
शुक्रं स्वशुक्रतश्चाङ्गं कुन्तलान्यत्र कालतः /
न्यस्तं शुक्रमतो योनौ नेति गर्भाशयं मुने //
369.m: From semen, and from one's own semen, limb and hair arise there in time. / Semen placed in the vagina goes from there to the uterus, O sage.

369.s:
ṛtāvapi ca yoniścedvātapittakaphāvṛtā /
bhavettadā vikāśitvaṃ naiva tasyāṃ prajāyate //
369.d:
ऋतावपि च योनिश्चेद्वातपित्तकफावृता /
भवेत्तदा विकाशित्वं नैव तस्यां प्रजायते //
369.m: Even during the fertile period, if the vagina is covered by wind, bile, and phlegm, / then dilation does not occur in it at all.

369.s:
bukkātpukkasakaplīhakṛtakoṣṭhāṅgahṛdvraṇāḥ /
taṇḍakaś ca mahābhāga nibaddhānyāśaye mataḥ //
369.d:
बुक्कात्पुक्कसकप्लीहकृतकोष्ठाङ्गहृद्व्रणाः /
तण्डकश् च महाभाग निबद्धान्याशये मतः //
369.m: The kidneys, the lungs, the spleen, the viscera of the trunk, the heart-sores, / and the *taṇḍaka*, O fortunate one, are considered attached to their receptacle.

369.s:
rasasya pacyamānasya sārādbhavati dehināṃ /
plīhā yakṛcca dharmajña raktapheṇācca pukkasaḥ //
369.d:
रसस्य पच्यमानस्य साराद्भवति देहिनां /
प्लीहा यकृच्च धर्मज्ञ रक्तफेणाच्च पुक्कसः //
369.m: From the essence of the cooking chyle arises in living beings / the spleen and liver, O knower of dharma, and the lungs from the foam of blood.

369.s:
raktaṃ pittañca bhavati tathā taṇḍakasaṃjñakaḥ /
medoraktaprasārācca vukkāyāḥ sambhavaḥ smṛtaḥ //
369.d:
रक्तं पित्तञ्च भवति तथा तण्डकसंज्ञकः /
मेदोरक्तप्रसाराच्च वुक्कायाः सम्भवः स्मृतः //
369.m: Blood and bile arise, and so does that called the *taṇḍaka*. / From the effusion of fat and blood, the origin of the kidney is remembered.

369.s:
raktamāṃsaprasārācca bhavantyantrāṇi dehināṃ /
sārdhatrivyāmasaṃkhyāni tāni nṝṇāṃ vinirdiśet //
369.d:
रक्तमांसप्रसाराच्च भवन्त्यन्त्राणि देहिनां /
सार्धत्रिव्यामसंख्यानि तानि नॄणां विनिर्दिशेत् //
369.m: From the effusion of blood and flesh the intestines of living beings come into being; / one should specify them as measuring three and a half *vyāma*s in men;

369.s:
trivyāmāni tathā strīṇāṃ prāhurvedavido janaḥ /
raktavāyusamāyogāt kāmeyasyodbhavaḥ smṛtaḥ //
369.d:
त्रिव्यामानि तथा स्त्रीणां प्राहुर्वेदविदो जनः /
रक्तवायुसमायोगात् कामेयस्योद्भवः स्मृतः //
369.m: people who know the Veda say they measure three *vyāma*s in women. / From the conjunction of blood and wind, the origin of the *kāmeya* is recorded.

369.s:
kaphaprasārādbhavati hṛdayaṃ padmasannibhaṃ /
adhomukhaṃ tacchūṣiraṃ yatra jīvo vyavasthitaḥ //
369.d:
कफप्रसाराद्भवति हृदयं पद्मसन्निभं /
अधोमुखं तच्छूषिरं यत्र जीवो व्यवस्थितः //
369.m: From the effusion of phlegm arises the heart, resembling a lotus / pointing downward, hollow, in which the individual soul is situated.

369.s:
caitanyānugatā bhāvaḥsarve tatra vyavasthitāḥ /
tasya vāme tathā plīhā dakṣiṇe ca tathā yakṛt //
369.d:
चैतन्यानुगता भावःसर्वे तत्र व्यवस्थिताः /
तस्य वामे तथा प्लीहा दक्षिणे च तथा यकृत् //
369.m: All states of being accompanying consciousness are located there. / To its left is the spleen, and to its right is the liver,

369.s:
dakṣiṇe ca tathā kloma padmasyaivaṃ prakīrtitaṃ /
śrotāṃsi yāni dehe 'smin kapharaktavahāni ca //
:p 307
369.d:
दक्षिणे च तथा क्लोम पद्मस्यैवं प्रकीर्तितं /
श्रोतांसि यानि देहे ऽस्मिन् कफरक्तवहानि च //
:प् 307
369.m:
and to its right is the *kloman*; thus is proclaimed [the anatomy] of the lotus. / The channels that are in this body carrying phlegm and blood—
[Page 307]

369.s:
teṣāṃ bhūtānumānācca bhavatīndriyasambhavaḥ /
netrayormaṇḍalaṃ śuklaṃ kaphādbhavati paitṛkaṃ //
369.d:
तेषां भूतानुमानाच्च भवतीन्द्रियसम्भवः /
नेत्रयोर्मण्डलं शुक्लं कफाद्भवति पैतृकं //
369.m: from the inference of the elements in them, the origin of the senses takes place. / The white circle of the two eyes comes from phlegm and is paternal;

369.s:
kṛṣṇañca maṇḍalaṃ vātāttathā mavati mātṛkaṃ /
pittāttvaṅmaṇḍalaṃ jñeyaṃ mātāpitṛsamudbhavaṃ //
369.d:
कृष्णञ्च मण्डलं वातात्तथा मवति मातृकं /
पित्तात्त्वङ्मण्डलं ज्ञेयं मातापितृसमुद्भवं //
369.m: the black circle comes from wind and is maternal. / The circle of the skin should be known as coming from bile, born of mother and father.

369.s:
māṃsāsṛkkaphajā jihvā medo 'sṛkkaphamāṃsajau /
vṛṣāṇau daśa prāṇasya jñeyānyāyatanāni tu //
369.d:
मांसासृक्कफजा जिह्वा मेदो ऽसृक्कफमांसजौ /
वृषाणौ दश प्राणस्य ज्ञेयान्यायतनानि तु //
369.m: The tongue is born of flesh, blood, and phlegm; the two testicles are born of fat, blood, phlegm, and flesh. / Ten seats of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) are to be known:

369.s:
mūrdhā hṛnnābhikaṇṭhāś ca jihvā śukrañca śoṇitaṃ /
gudaṃ vastiś ca gulphañca kaṇḍurāḥ śoḍaśeritāḥ //
369.d:
मूर्धा हृन्नाभिकण्ठाश् च जिह्वा शुक्रञ्च शोणितं /
गुदं वस्तिश् च गुल्फञ्च कण्डुराः शोडशेरिताः //
369.m: the head, heart, navel, throat, tongue, semen, blood, / rectum, bladder, and ankle. Sixteen large tendons are mentioned:

369.s:
dve kare dve ca caraṇe catasraḥ pṛṣṭhato gale /
dehe pādādiśīrṣānte jālāni caiva ṣoḍaśa //
369.d:
द्वे करे द्वे च चरणे चतस्रः पृष्ठतो गले /
देहे पादादिशीर्षान्ते जालानि चैव षोडश //
369.m: two in the hand, two in the foot, four behind in the neck. / In the body, from the feet to the head, there are also sixteen networks:

369.s:
māṃsasnāyuśirāsthinyaḥ catvāraś ca pṛthak pṛthak /
maṇibandhanagulpheṣu nibaddhāni parasparaṃ //
369.d:
मांसस्नायुशिरास्थिन्यः चत्वारश् च पृथक् पृथक् /
मणिबन्धनगुल्फेषु निबद्धानि परस्परं //
369.m: four of flesh, four of sinews, four of veins, and four of bones, separately, / bound to each other in the wrists and ankles.

369.s:
ṣaṭkūrcāni smṛtānīha hastayoḥ pādayoḥ pṛthak /
grīvāyāñca tathā meḍhre kathitāni manīṣibhiḥ //
369.d:
षट्कूर्चानि स्मृतानीह हस्तयोः पादयोः पृथक् /
ग्रीवायाञ्च तथा मेढ्रे कथितानि मनीषिभिः //
369.m: Six clusters (*kūrca*) are recorded here, in the two hands and two feet separately, / and in the neck and the penis, as declared by the wise.

369.s:
pṛṣṭhavaṃśasyopagatāś catasro māṃsarajjavaḥ /
navatyaś ca tathā peśyastāsāṃ bandhanakārikāḥ //
369.d:
पृष्ठवंशस्योपगताश् चतस्रो मांसरज्जवः /
नवत्यश् च तथा पेश्यस्तासां बन्धनकारिकाः //
369.m: Connected to the spinal column are four cords of flesh, / and ninety muscles that bind them.

369.s:
sīraṇyaś ca tathā sapta pañca mūrdhānamāśritāḥ /
ekaikā meḍhrajihvāstā asthi ṣaṣṭiśatatrayaṃ //
369.d:
सीरण्यश् च तथा सप्त पञ्च मूर्धानमाश्रिताः /
एकैका मेढ्रजिह्वास्ता अस्थि षष्टिशतत्रयं //
369.m: And seven sutures: five situated in the head, / and one each in the penis and tongue. The bones are three hundred and sixty.

369.s:
sūkṣmaiḥ saha catuḥṣaṣṭhirdaśanā viṃśatirnakhāḥ /
pāṇipādaśalākāś ca tāsāṃ sthānacatuṣṭayaṃ //
369.d:
सूक्ष्मैः सह चतुःषष्ठिर्दशना विंशतिर्नखाः /
पाणिपादशलाकाश् च तासां स्थानचतुष्टयं //
369.m: Together with the minute ones, there are sixty-four teeth and twenty nails. / There are the long bones (*śalākā*) of the hands and feet, and their four locations.

369.s:
ṣaṣṭyaṅgulīnāṃ dve pārṣṇyorgulpheṣu ca catuṣṭayaṃ /
catvāryaratnyorasthīni jaṅghayostadvadeva tu //
369.d:
षष्ट्यङ्गुलीनां द्वे पार्ष्ण्योर्गुल्फेषु च चतुष्टयं /
चत्वार्यरत्न्योरस्थीनि जङ्घयोस्तद्वदेव तु //
369.m: Sixty [bones] of the digits, two in the heels, and four in the ankles; / four bones in the two forearms, and likewise in the two shanks.

369.s:
dve dve jānukapoloruphalakāṃśasamudbhavaṃ /
:p 308
akṣasthānāṃśakaśroṇiphalake caivamādiśet //
369.d:
द्वे द्वे जानुकपोलोरुफलकांशसमुद्भवं /
:प् 308
अक्षस्थानांशकश्रोणिफलके चैवमादिशेत् //

369.s:
bhagāstokaṃ tathā pṛṣṭhe catvāriṃśacca pañca ca /
grīvāyāñca tathāsthīni jatrukañca tathā hamuḥ //
369.d:
भगास्तोकं तथा पृष्ठे चत्वारिंशच्च पञ्च च /
ग्रीवायाञ्च तथास्थीनि जत्रुकञ्च तथा हमुः //
369.m: a little in the vulva, and forty-five in the back; / and bones in the neck, the collar-bone, and the jaw;

369.s:
tanmūlaṃ dvelalāṭākṣigaṇḍanāsāṅghyravasthitāḥ /
parśukāstālukaiḥ sārdhamarvudaiś ca dvisaptatiḥ //
369.d:
तन्मूलं द्वेललाटाक्षिगण्डनासाङ्घ्य्रवस्थिताः /
पर्शुकास्तालुकैः सार्धमर्वुदैश् च द्विसप्ततिः //
369.m: its base, two situated in the forehead, eyes, cheeks, nose, and feet; / the ribs, together with the palatal parts and tubercles, are seventy-two;

369.s:
dveśaṅkhake kapālāni catvāryeva śiras tathā /
uraḥ saptadaśāsthīni sandhīnāṃ dve śate daśa //
369.d:
द्वेशङ्खके कपालानि चत्वार्येव शिरस् तथा /
उरः सप्तदशास्थीनि सन्धीनां द्वे शते दश //
369.m: two in the temples, four cranial bones in the head, / seventeen bones in the chest, and two hundred and ten joints:

369.s:
aṣṭaṣaṣṭistu śākhāsu ṣaṣṭiś caikavivarjitā /
antarā vai tryaśītiś ca snāyor navaśatāni ca //
369.d:
अष्टषष्टिस्तु शाखासु षष्टिश् चैकविवर्जिता /
अन्तरा वै त्र्यशीतिश् च स्नायोर् नवशतानि च //
369.m: sixty-eight in the limbs, fifty-nine / in the trunk, and eighty-three [in the head and neck]; and nine hundred sinews:

369.s:
triṃśādhike dve śate tu antarādhau tu saptatiḥ /
ūrdhvagāḥ ṣaṭśatānyeva śākhāstu kathitāni tu //
369.d:
त्रिंशाधिके द्वे शते तु अन्तराधौ तु सप्ततिः /
ऊर्ध्वगाः षट्शतान्येव शाखास्तु कथितानि तु //
369.m: two hundred and thirty [in the limbs], seventy in the trunk and lower body, / while six hundred are declared to go upward into the limbs.

369.s:
pañcapeśīśatānyeva(1) catvāriṃśattathordhvagāḥ /
catuḥśatantu śākhāsu antarādhau ca ṣaṣṭikā //
369.d:
पञ्चपेशीशतान्येव(1) चत्वारिंशत्तथोर्ध्वगाः /
चतुःशतन्तु शाखासु अन्तराधौ च षष्टिका //
369.m: There are five hundred muscles, forty going upward, / four hundred in the limbs, and sixty in the trunk and lower part.

369.s:
strīṇām caikādhikā vai syādviṃśatiś caturuttarā /
stanayordaśa yonau ca trayodaśa tathāśaye //
369.d:
स्त्रीणाम् चैकाधिका वै स्याद्विंशतिश् चतुरुत्तरा /
स्तनयोर्दश योनौ च त्रयोदश तथाशये //
369.m: In women there are twenty-four more: / ten in the two breasts, and thirteen in the vagina and receptacle [of semen],

369.s:
garbhasya ca catasraḥ syuḥ śirāṇāñca śarīriṇāṃ /
triṃśacchatasahasrāṇi tathānyāni navaiva tu //
369.d:
गर्भस्य च चतस्रः स्युः शिराणाञ्च शरीरिणां /
त्रिंशच्छतसहस्राणि तथान्यानि नवैव तु //
369.m: and four of the embryo. Of the veins of embodied beings / there are three million and nine [thousand] more;

369.s:
ṣaṭpañcāśatsahasrāṇi rasandehe vahanti tāḥ /
kedāra iva kulyāś ca kledalepādikañca yat //
369.d:
षट्पञ्चाशत्सहस्राणि रसन्देहे वहन्ति ताः /
केदार इव कुल्याश् च क्लेदलेपादिकञ्च यत् //
369.m: fifty-six thousand of them carry chyle in the body / like canals in a meadow, and what is moisture, plastering, and so forth.

369.s:
dvāsaptatis tathā koṭyo vyomnāmiha mahāmune /
majjāyā medasaś caiva vasāyāś ca tathā dvija //
369.d:
द्वासप्ततिस् तथा कोट्यो व्योम्नामिह महामुने /
मज्जाया मेदसश् चैव वसायाश् च तथा द्विज //
369.m: Likewise, O great sage, there are seventy-two crores of spaces here [in the body]. / Of bone marrow, fat, and lipid also, O twice-born,

369.s:
mūtrasya caiva pittasya śleṣmaṇaḥ śakṛtas tathā /
:n
1 pañcapeśīśatānyatreti kha.. , ña.. ca
:p 309
raktasya sarasasyātra kramaśo 'ñjalayo matāḥ //
369.d:
मूत्रस्य चैव पित्तस्य श्लेष्मणः शकृतस् तथा /
:न्
1 पञ्चपेशीशतान्यत्रेति ख.. , ञ.. च
:प् 309
रक्तस्य सरसस्यात्र क्रमशो ऽञ्जलयो मताः //
369.m:
and of urine, bile, phlegm, and feces,
[Footnote]
1. Manuscripts kha and ña read *pañcapeśīśatānyatra*.
[Page 309]
and here of blood together with fluid, the measures in handfuls (añjalis) are considered in order:

369.s:
ardhārdhābhyadhikāḥ sarvāḥ pūrvapūrvāñjalermatāḥ /
ardhāñjaliś ca śukrasya tadardhañca tataujasaḥ //
369.d:
अर्धार्धाभ्यधिकाः सर्वाः पूर्वपूर्वाञ्जलेर्मताः /
अर्धाञ्जलिश् च शुक्रस्य तदर्धञ्च ततौजसः //
369.m: Each succeeding one is considered to be half a handful greater than the preceding one; / and semen is half a handful, and vitality (ojas) is half of that.

369.s:
rajasastu tathā strīṇāñcatasraḥ kathitā budhaiḥ /
śarīraṃ maladoṣādi piṇḍaṃ jñātvātmani tyajet(1) //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe śarīrāvayavā nāmo na
saptatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś athasapratyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
narakanirūpaṇam
369.d:
रजसस्तु तथा स्त्रीणाञ्चतस्रः कथिता बुधैः /
शरीरं मलदोषादि पिण्डं ज्ञात्वात्मनि त्यजेत्(1) //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे शरीरावयवा नामो न
सप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथसप्रत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
नरकनिरूपणम्
369.m:
Four [handfuls] of menstrual fluid of women are taught by the wise. / Knowing the body to be a mass of impurities, afflictions, and the like, one should abandon attachment to it.
Thus ends the three hundred and sixty-ninth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled “The Bodily Parts”.
